problem.passage:
The manuscripts preserving Hildegard von Bingen's chants, compiled at her Rupertsberg convent in the twelfth century, ______ melodic lines that leap far beyond the narrow ranges typical of other plainchant of her era, a feature some scholars interpret as a sonic image of the soul's ascent toward the divine.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: The manuscripts preserving Hildegard von Bingen's chants, compiled at her Rupertsberg convent in the twelfth century, ______ melodic lines that leap far beyond the narrow ranges typical of other plainchant of her era, a feature some scholars interpret as a sonic image of the soul's ascent toward the divine.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: contain
contains
containing
has contained
problem.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 복수 명사 'manuscripts'이며, 'preserving ... chants'와 'compiled ... century'는 주어를 꾸미는 수식어구일 뿐이다. 따라서 빈칸에는 복수 주어와 일치하는 정동사가 필요하므로 A가 정답이다. B는 정동사이지만 단수형이어서 가까운 단수 명사 'convent'나 'century'에 맞춘 오류이다. C는 분사이므로 문장에 본동사가 없게 된다. D는 정동사이긴 하지만 단수형이고, 지금도 사실인 내용을 나타내는 현재 시제 문맥에도 맞지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The subject of this sentence is the plural noun "manuscripts." The phrases "preserving ... chants" and "compiled ... century" only modify that subject. So the blank needs a finite verb that agrees with a plural subject, which makes A correct. B is a finite verb, but it's singular, as if it agreed with the nearby singular nouns "convent" or "century." C is a participle, so the sentence would have no main verb. D is finite, but it's singular, and its tense doesn't fit a context that describes something that is still true now.

quality.seed: arts and humanities nonfiction — Hildegard von Bingen's use of neumes in musical notation encoding mystical theological concepts

hardJudge.note: 주어 'manuscripts'(복수)와 빈칸 사이에 'preserving ... chants', 'compiled at her Rupertsberg convent in the twelfth century'라는 긴 수식어구가 끼어 있고, 그 안의 단수 명사(convent, century)가 근접 일치 오류를 유도한다. A 'contain'만이 복수 주어와 일치하는 정동사이므로 정답 적절. B(단수 정동사), D(단수 완료형)는 정동사라는 점에서 부분적 타당성이 있어 비교가 필요하고, C는 본동사 부재로 배제된다. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 동일 결론과 글자 참조를 가지며 모순 없음. D에 대한 시제 언급은 부차적이지만 틀리지 않음. 힐데가르트 성가 사본이 12세기 루페르츠베르크에서 편찬되었고 당대 플레인챈트보다 넓은 음역을 지닌다는 내용도 사실에 부합. 중간 난이도 기준(주어 식별 + 수 일치 두 단계 판단, 오답 중 2개 이상 부분 타당) 충족.

advisory.note: 주어와 동사 사이에 긴 분사구 두 개가 끼어 있고 가까운 단수 명사(convent, century)가 함정 역할을 함. 중간 난이도에 적합.

options: reflecting

having reflected
problem.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 'This approach'이고, 'which ... recession'과 'in fact' 뒤에 본동사가 와야 한다. 단수 주어에 맞는 정동사인 B 'reflects'가 정답이다. C 'reflect'는 정동사이긴 하지만 바로 앞의 복수명사 'art historians'에 끌려 복수형을 고른 것으로, 단수 주어 'approach'와 맞지 않는다. A 'reflecting'과 D 'having reflected'는 분사라서 문장에 본동사가 없게 된다.

Choice B, "reflects," is a finite verb that agrees with the singular subject, so it is correct. Choice C is a finite verb too, but it is plural, so it agrees with the nearby noun "art historians" instead of the real subject, "approach." Choices A and D are participles, so with either one the sentence would have no main verb.

So the blank needs a finite verb that agrees with a singular subject, which makes C correct. hardJudge.note: 주어 'This interval'(단수)와 정동사 일치 문제. 관계절·동격·전치사구가 길게 끼어 있어 근접 복수 명사 'lines and steps'에 끌려 A를 고르기 쉬움(두 단계 판단: 정동사 필요 + 수 일치). options: has prompted
have prompted
prompting
to prompt
problem.explanation: 두 번째 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 "acquisition"이고, "of these paintings by ... houses, which ... fine art"는 주어와 동사 사이에 끼어든 긴 수식어구이다. 따라서 이 문장에는 단수 주어와 수가 일치하는 정동사가 필요하며, A의 "has prompted"가 이 조건을 충족한다. problem.explanationEn: The subject of the second sentence is the singular noun "acquisition." Everything from "of these paintings" through "fine art" is a long modifier that comes between the subject and its verb. That means the sentence needs a finite verb that agrees with a singular subject, and A, "has prompted," is the only choice that does this. B is a finite verb, but it matches the nearby plural "museums and auction houses" instead of the actual subject, so the subject and verb don't agree. C is a participle and D is an infinitive, so either one leaves "acquisition" without a main verb and makes the sentence incomplete.

hardJudge.note: 주어 "The rapid acquisition"(단수)과 동사 사이에 "of these paintings by major Western museums and auction houses, which ... fine art"라는 긴 수식어가 끼어 있어 (1) 정동사 필요 판단 + (2) 수 일치 확인의 두 단계가 요구됨. A "has prompted"가 유일하게 적합. B는 인접 복수 명사에 끌린 오답으로 강한 매력도, C는 분사로 문장 흐름상 그럴듯해 보이며, D도 문법적 형태로 말이 됨. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 동일 결론·글자 참조, 모순 없음, 영어 해설에 한글 없음. Papunya 1970년대 초·Clifford Possum Tjapaltjarri 사실관계 정확. 표준 SAT medium 수준에 부합.

advisory.note: 주어 acquisition과 동사 사이에 복수 명사(paintings, museums and auction houses)를 포함한 긴 수식어가 끼어 있어 B가 매력적인 오답이다. 수 일치와 정동사 필요성을 두 단계로 판단해야 하므로 medium에 맞다. Papunya 1970년대와 Clifford Possum에 관한 사실 진술은 대체로 정확하다.

A comma opens it, so a comma has to close it too. That puts the subject back together with its verb, "provoked," which is why D is correct. In A, the semicolon cuts the subject off from its verb, so neither side can stand as an independent clause. In B, a dash can close an interruption, but an interruption that opens with a comma can't close with a dash, because the marks don't match. In C, leaving out punctuation never closes the appositive, so "townspeople" reads as if it were the subject of "provoked."

hardJudge.note: 주어 'A Burial at Ornans' 뒤에 쉼표로 열린 비필수 동격구를 쉼표로 닫아 동사 provoked와 연결하는 D가 옳다. 세미콜론(A)은 독립절이 아닌 양쪽을 분리하고, 대시(B)는 여는 부호와 짝이 맞지 않으며, 무부호(C)는 동격구가 닫히지 않는다. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 동일 결론과 글자 참조를 갖고 정확하다. 사실관계(1849–50, 약 7m 폭, 아카데미 역사화 위계 논란)도 맞다. 긴 동격구와 내부 나열 쉼표 때문에 여는 부호를 추적해야 하는 두 단계 판단이 요구되며 B·C가 그럴듯한 오답으로 기능하므로 medium에 적합하다.

advisory.note: 긴 동격어구라서 쉼표 짝을 맞추려면 앞에서 연 쉼표를 다시 찾아봐야 하고, 이 단계가 중간 난이도에 맞다. 대시와 부호 없음 오답은 그럴듯하다. 사실관계(1849–50년, 약 6.6m)에도 문제가 없다.

Lenox Avenue") and you'll find that the text before the blank is a complete independent clause (subject "poem," verb "borrows"). The text after the blank, "the result is verse...," is also an independent clause. A semicolon can join two independent clauses, so B is correct. A uses only a comma, which creates a comma splice. C uses "and" with no comma before it, so the two independent clauses aren't joined correctly. D makes "which the result is verse..." a relative clause that doesn't work grammatically.

hardJudge.note: 빈칸 앞은 긴 비필수 관계절(which follows... Lenox Avenue)을 포함한 독립절(poem borrows...), 뒤는 독립절(the result is verse...)이므로 세미콜론(B)이 유일하게 적합. A는 콤마 스플라이스, C는 등위접속사 앞 쉼표 누락(또한 앞의 'blues and the loose cadence'와 병렬 혼동 유발), D는 'which the result is'가 비문. 사실 정보(1926년 출간, 렌녹스 애비뉴, 12마디 블루스의 반복 행)도 정확. 긴 삽입절을 지나 절 구조를 파악해야 하고 C가 부분적 매력 오답으로 기능하므로 medium에 부합.

advisory.note: 두 독립절을 세미콜론으로 연결하는 것이 맞다. 긴 비필수 관계절 때문에 주절을 찾는 단계가 하나 더 필요해 medium 수준에 맞다. 오답 C(쉼표 없는 and)와 D(which)도 그럴듯하게 만들어졌다. 사실 관계(1926년, 레녹스 애비뉴의 피아니스트, 블루스 형식)도 정확하다.

problem.stimulus: In 726, according to later chroniclers, Byzantine emperor Leo III ordered the removal of a prominent image of Christ from the Chalke Gate, the ceremonial entrance to the imperial palace in Constantinople______ the act, whether it reflected genuine theological conviction or political calculation, set off more than a century of bitter debate over whether sacred images could legitimately represent the divine.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: and
, being
problem.explanation: 빈칸 앞은 Leo III를 주어로 하는 독립절이고, 동격구 'the ceremonial entrance... Constantinople'로 끝난다. 빈칸 뒤는 삽입절을 사이에 두고 주어 'the act'와 동사 'set off'를 갖춘 또 하나의 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 이을 수 있으므로 정답은 C이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 오류(comma splice)가 되고, 쉼표가 동격구를 이어 가는 것처럼 보여 그럴듯할 뿐이다. B는 접속사 앞에 쉼표가 없어 두 긴 독립절이 제대로 구분되지 않고, D의 'being'은 뒤의 절을 수식어로 만들려 하지만 'the act... set off'와 문법적으로 맞지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The text before the blank is an independent clause with Leo III as its subject, and it ends with the long appositive "the ceremonial entrance... Constantinople." After the blank comes a second independent clause: its subject is "the act" and its verb is "set off," with a "whether" clause interrupting between them. A semicolon correctly joins two independent clauses, so C is correct. A joins the two clauses with only a comma, which makes a comma splice; it seems plausible only because a comma could look like it's continuing the appositive. B uses "and" with no comma before it, so these two long independent clauses aren't properly separated. D's "being" tries to turn what follows into a modifier, but that doesn't work grammatically with "the act... set off."

hardJudge.note: C(세미콜론)는 두 독립절을 올바르게 연결하며 유일한 정답으로 성립한다. A는 comma splice, D의 'being'은 뒤의 완전한 절과 결합 불가. 다만 B(쉼표 없는 'and')는 일부 문법 기준에서 허용 가능성이 논의되는 형태라 실제 SAT에서는 이런 오답을 피하는 경향이 있으나, 긴 두 독립절을 쉼표 없이 잇는 것은 표준 SAT 규칙상 오류로 처리되고 C가 명백히 더 우수하므로 정답 판정에는 영향이 없음. 역사적 사실(726년, Leo III, Chalke Gate 성화 철거)은 'according to later chroniclers'로 적절히 한정되어 있음. 난이도는 긴 동격구와 삽입절 사이에서 절 경계를 파악해야 하는 2단계 판단으로 medium에 적합.

advisory.note: 긴 동격구와 'whether' 삽입절 때문에 두 번째 독립절의 주어와 동사를 찾아야 함. 쉼표 접속 오류(A)와 쉼표 없는 'and'(B)가 그럴듯한 오답이라 medium 난이도에 맞음. 레오 3세의 칼케 문 성화 철거 이야기는 후대 연대기 기록으로 제시되어 있어 사실 관계에도 문제 없음.

problem.stimulus: Pérotin, a composer associated with Notre-Dame Cathedral in Paris around 1200, expanded the two-voice organum preserved in the Magnus liber organi into works for three and even four ______ in pieces such as Viderunt omnes, the added upper voices move in rapid, interlocking rhythmic patterns above a single chant note stretched out for many measures.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: voices;
voices,
voices
voices, which
problem.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "Pérotin ... expanded ... four voices"는 독립절이고, 뒤의 "in pieces such as Viderunt omnes, the added upper voices move ..."도 주어(the added upper voices)와 동사(move)를 갖춘 독립절이다. 접속사 없이 두 독립절을 잇는 데는 세미콜론이 맞으므로 정답은 A이다. B는 쉼표만으로 두 절을 이어 쉼표 오용(comma splice)이 된다. 빈칸 뒤 전치사구 다음에 쉼표가 있어 삽입 성분처럼 보이지만, 실제로는 새 절이 시작되는 자리다. C는 문장부호가 아예 없어 무종지문(run-on)이 되고, D는 관계대명사 which 뒤에 이미 주어를 갖춘 완전한 절이 와서 비문이 된다.
problem.explanationEn: The part before the blank ("Pérotin ... expanded ... four voices") is an independent clause. The part after it ("in pieces such as Viderunt omnes, the added upper voices move ...") is also an independent clause, since it has its own subject (the added upper voices) and verb (move). With no conjunction between them, a semicolon is the right way to join them, so A is correct. B joins the two clauses with only a comma, which is a comma splice. The comma after the introductory phrase can make the second part look like a modifier, but a new clause actually starts there. C uses no punctuation at all and creates a run-on, and D puts the relative pronoun "which" in front of a clause that already has a subject, so the sentence becomes ungrammatical.

quality.seed: arts and humanities nonfiction — Polyphonic music development in Notre-Dame de Chartres school and organum composition technique

hardJudge.note: 빈칸 앞은 독립절(Pérotin ... expanded ... voices), 뒤는 도입 전치사구 + 독립절(the added upper voices move ...)이므로 세미콜론(A)이 정답임을 직접 확인. B는 comma splice, C는 run-on, D는 which 뒤에 주어가 있는 완전절이 와 비문. 도입구 "in pieces such as Viderunt omnes," 뒤의 쉼표가 B를 그럴듯하게 만들어 두 절 경계를 정독해야 하므로 medium에 적합. 사실관계(Pérotin, Notre-Dame c.1200, Magnus liber organi, Viderunt omnes 4성 organum, 길게 늘인 성가 테너음) 모두 정확. 한/영 해설 결론·글자 참조 일치, 영어 해설에 한글 없음. 원문 창작 텍스트로 저작권 문제 없음.

advisory.note: 두 독립절 사이 세미콜론이 정답이다. 두 번째 절이 도입 전치사구(in pieces such as Viderunt omnes,)로 시작해 주절이 늦게 드러나므로, 훑어 읽으면 B를 고르기 쉽다. medium 난이도에 맞는다. 사실 관계(Pérotin, Magnus liber organi, 4성부 Viderunt omnes)도 정확하다.

problem.explanationEn: The words before the blank ("the poster ... reduced ... to pure geometry") and after it ("the image required no literacy ...") are both independent clauses, so a semicolon is the right way to join them. That makes C correct. A joins the two clauses with only a comma, which creates a comma splice. B uses the conjunction "and," but the comma comes after "and" when it should come before it, so the punctuation is wrong. hardJudge.note: 검산: 빈칸 앞 "El Lissitzky's 1919 poster ... reduced ... to pure geometry"와 뒤 "the image required no literacy ..."는 모두 독립절 → 세미콜론(C)만 적법. problem.passage:
Film historians often credit Akira Kurosawa's samurai films with shaping Western cinema, and the most commonly cited evidence is plot borrowing: Yojimbo (1961) was remade almost scene for scene as Sergio Leone's A Fistful of Dollars, and Seven Samurai (1954) became The Magnificent Seven. Yet scholar Stephen Prince argues that this focus on remakes understates Kurosawa's influence. Prince notes that directors who never adapted a Kurosawa story, such as Sam Peckinpah and George Lucas, adopted his techniques instead: multiple cameras filming a single action from different angles, telephoto lenses that compress crowds of fighters into dense layers, and wipe transitions that sweep one scene off the screen. For Prince, these visual methods spread far more widely than any borrowed plot and changed how Western filmmakers built action sequences.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
problem.stimulus: Film historians often credit Akira Kurosawa's samurai films with shaping Western cinema, and the most commonly cited evidence is plot borrowing: Yojimbo (1961) was remade almost scene for scene as Sergio Leone's A Fistful of Dollars, and Seven Samurai (1954) became The Magnificent Seven. Yet scholar Stephen Prince argues that this focus on remakes understates Kurosawa's influence. Prince notes that directors who never adapted a Kurosawa story, such as Sam Peckinpah and George Lucas, adopted his techniques instead: multiple cameras filming a single action from different angles, telephoto lenses that compress crowds of fighters into dense layers, and wipe transitions that sweep one scene off the screen. For Prince, these visual methods spread far more widely than any borrowed plot and changed how Western filmmakers built action sequences.
problem.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Prince contends that Western remakes of Kurosawa's samurai films were more visually inventive than the Japanese originals they adapted.
Prince contends that Kurosawa affected Western film more through methods of shooting and editing than through the stories that were remade.
Prince contends that Peckinpah and Lucas were the first Western directors to recognize the value of Kurosawa's samurai plots.
Prince contends that historians have exaggerated Kurosawa's role by treating remakes such as A Fistful of Dollars as proof of influence.
problem.explanation: 지문은 리메이크(줄거리 차용)에만 주목하면 구로사와의 영향력이 과소평가된다는 Prince의 주장을 소개하고, 다중 카메라·망원 렌즈·와이프 전환 같은 시각적 기법이 줄거리보다 더 널리 퍼졌다고 결론짓는다. 따라서 B가 중심 내용이다. A는 리메이크와 원작의 시각적 우열을 비교한 적이 없으므로 틀리다. C는 Peckinpah와 Lucas가 줄거리가 아니라 기법을 받아들였다는 지문 내용과 반대된다. D는 영향력이 '과장'되었다고 하지만, Prince는 오히려 영향력이 '과소평가'되었다고 주장하므로 틀리다.
problem.explanationEn: The text presents Prince's claim that looking only at remakes (borrowed plots) understates Kurosawa's influence, and it ends by saying his visual techniques, like multiple cameras, telephoto lenses, and wipes, spread more widely than any plot. So B states the main idea. A is wrong because the text never says whether the remakes or the originals were more visually inventive. problem.passage:
In late medieval English towns such as York and Chester, mystery plays were staged not by clergy but by craft guilds, each of which took responsibility for a single biblical episode. Performed on movable wagons that rolled from station to station through the streets, the cycles moved from the Creation to the Last Judgment over a single long day. Because most spectators could not read Latin scripture, these performances gave them a vivid, sequential account of sacred history in their own language. Scholars have often treated the plays mainly as teaching tools imposed from above, but recent research complicates that view. Guild records show that members spent their own money on costumes and stage effects, argued over which episodes they would be assigned, and sometimes chose episodes linked to their trade—the shipwrights, for instance, staged the building of Noah's ark. Such evidence suggests that the plays were not simply lessons handed to a passive public; they were also a way for townspeople to claim a place for themselves within the religious story they were helping to tell.

problem.passage:
In the 1930s, the French dramatist Antonin Artaud argued that European theater had become a polite parlor game. Audiences, he complained, sat safely in the dark while actors on a distant stage untangled the motives of believable characters, and spectators left feeling they had understood something rather than having been changed by it. Artaud's proposed "Theatre of Cruelty" did not mean staging violence for its own sake. Instead, he wanted performances that would bypass the intellect, using piercing sounds, sudden light, ritual gesture, and spectators seated in the middle of the action, so that the audience could no longer observe from a comfortable distance. Although Artaud staged few productions himself, and the ones he did stage mostly failed, directors such as Peter Brook and Jerzy Grotowski later took up his ideas while reshaping how performers and audiences share space.

problem.passage:
Listeners new to Indian classical music often assume that a raga performance is either strictly composed or entirely spontaneous. In fact, it is neither. A raga specifies a set of pitches, characteristic ascending and descending patterns, and certain phrases that must recur, and many of its intervals derive from simple whole-number frequency ratios, such as the 3:2 relationship that defines the perfect fifth. These constraints are fixed long before any musician sits down to play.

Yet within those limits, performers are expected to invent. In the slow opening section known as the alap, a sitarist may spend half an hour exploring a single raga, deciding moment by moment which pitch to linger on, how to bend toward the next, and when to introduce a signature phrase. Musicologist Martin Clayton has argued that this freedom is meaningful precisely because the boundaries are so precise: listeners recognize a performer's originality by hearing how inventively the musician moves while never stepping outside the raga's rules.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

problem.passage:
Because Banksy has never publicly confirmed his identity, the works attributed to him pose an unusual problem for galleries and auction houses. In most of the art market, a work's value rests heavily on provenance: a documented chain linking the object to the artist's hand. Banksy, however, created his best-known pieces illegally on public walls, often at night, leaving no witnesses willing to testify and no receipts. To fill this gap, his studio established Pest Control, an organization that issues certificates for authentic works but refuses to authenticate any piece removed from the street without the artist's consent. As a result, some murals cut from buildings and offered for sale have struggled to find buyers despite being widely accepted as genuine, while smaller prints certified by Pest Control routinely sell for high prices. Banksy's anonymity, in other words, has not removed authority over authenticity from the artist but has concentrated it in a single gatekeeper he controls.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

problem.passage:
For decades, scholars dated the Dead Sea Scrolls chiefly through paleography, comparing the shapes of letters in each manuscript with a sequence of scripts thought to have evolved gradually over time. A scroll whose scribe wrote a particular form of the letter aleph, for example, would be placed earlier or later in that sequence. Researcher Mladen Popović and colleagues have argued that this method, though valuable, rests on an assumption that every scribe of a given period wrote in roughly the same way. Using radiocarbon results from several scrolls together with computer analysis of ink traces, the team found that some manuscripts once assigned to the first century BCE were in fact copied decades earlier, and that two hands judged identical by eye differed in subtle stroke patterns. Popović's team does not propose abandoning letter-shape comparison; rather, they suggest that the traditional script sequence be recalibrated against physical evidence so that individual scribal habits are not mistaken for signs of a different era.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
problem.stimulus: For decades, scholars dated the Dead Sea Scrolls chiefly through paleography, comparing the shapes of letters in each manuscript with a sequence of scripts thought to have evolved gradually over time. A scroll whose scribe wrote a particular form of the letter aleph, for example, would be placed earlier or later in that sequence. Researcher Mladen Popović and colleagues have argued that this method, though valuable, rests on an assumption that every scribe of a given period wrote in roughly the same way. Using radiocarbon results from several scrolls together with computer analysis of ink traces, the team found that some manuscripts once assigned to the first century BCE were in fact copied decades earlier, and that two hands judged identical by eye differed in subtle stroke patterns. Popović's team does not propose abandoning letter-shape comparison; rather, they suggest that the traditional script sequence be recalibrated against physical evidence so that individual scribal habits are not mistaken for signs of a different era.
problem.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Radiocarbon testing and computer analysis have shown that paleography cannot reliably date the Dead Sea Scrolls and should be replaced by physical methods.
Computer analysis of ink traces has revealed that many Dead Sea Scrolls were copied by more scribes than scholars had previously recognized.
New physical and computational evidence suggests that the traditional letter-based dating of the Dead Sea Scrolls is useful but needs adjustment to account for differences among individual scribes.
Changes in the shape of letters such as aleph allow scholars to place Dead Sea Scroll manuscripts in a precise chronological order.
problem.explanation: 지문은 문자 형태 비교에 의한 연대 측정이 가치 있지만, 모든 서기가 같은 방식으로 썼다는 가정에 기대고 있으므로 물리적 증거로 재보정해야 한다고 말한다. C가 이 '유용하지만 조정 필요'라는 핵심을 정확히 담는다. A는 증거 내용은 맞지만 지문이 명시적으로 부정한 '폐기·대체'를 주장한다. B는 필체 차이라는 세부를 다루지만 서기 수가 늘었다는 결론은 지문에 없고 중심 내용도 아니다. D는 전통적 방법의 설명만 반복하며 지문이 그 정밀성을 의문시한다는 점을 놓친다.
problem.explanationEn: The text says letter-shape dating is valuable but relies on the assumption that all scribes of a period wrote alike, so it should be recalibrated against physical evidence. Choice C captures this "useful but needs adjustment" point. Choice A gets the evidence right but claims paleography should be replaced, which the text explicitly rejects. Choice B builds on the detail about differing hands, but the text never concludes that more scribes were involved, and that detail isn't the main point anyway. Choice D only restates the traditional method and misses that the text questions how precise it is.

A is a strong distractor using correct evidence with the wrong conclusion, directly refuted by "does not propose abandoning." B extrapolates from the "two hands differed" detail to an unsupported claim about more scribes. D restates the traditional method the text qualifies. problem.passage:
Critics have often described Clarice Lispector's novel The Passion According to G.H. (1964) as fragmented, since its narrator's account breaks off, circles back, and restates earlier sentences rather than moving from event to event. Some scholars have treated this as a sign that Lispector was indifferent to how her books were put together. However, manuscript research complicates that view: Lispector's drafts show that she repeatedly moved passages around and deliberately made each chapter begin by repeating the final sentence of the one before it. Because a writer careless about structure would be unlikely to spend that much effort controlling how sections connect, the manuscripts suggest that ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
problem.stimulus: Critics have often described Clarice Lispector's novel The Passion According to G.H. (1964) as fragmented, since its narrator's account breaks off, circles back, and restates earlier sentences rather than moving from event to event. Some scholars have treated this as a sign that Lispector was indifferent to how her books were put together. However, manuscript research complicates that view: Lispector's drafts show that she repeatedly moved passages around and deliberately made each chapter begin by repeating the final sentence of the one before it. Because a writer careless about structure would be unlikely to spend that much effort controlling how sections connect, the manuscripts suggest that ______
problem.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: Lispector's readers in the 1960s found the novel's repeated sentences confusing until critics explained their purpose.
Lispector's revisions made the novel more linear than her early drafts had been, removing most of its fragmentation.
Lispector's drafts are a more reliable guide to her intentions than the published novel is.
the novel's broken, looping form reflects a carefully planned design rather than a lack of interest in structure.
problem.explanation: 지문은 단편적 형식이 구조에 무관심한 결과라는 견해를 소개한 뒤, 원고에서 단락을 재배치하고 장 연결을 의도적으로 설계한 증거를 제시하므로, 단편성이 계획된 설계라는 D가 결론으로 적절하다. A는 1960년대 독자 반응을 다루는데 지문에 근거가 없다. B는 수정이 있었다는 사실은 맞지만, 수정 후에도 반복·순환 구조가 남아 있으므로 선형화되었다는 주장은 지문과 모순된다. C는 원고를 근거로 삼는다는 점은 맞지만, 원고가 출판본보다 더 신뢰할 만하다는 비교는 지문의 논증을 넘어선다.
problem.explanationEn: The passage presents the view that the novel's fragmentation shows Lispector didn't care about structure, then gives manuscript evidence that she rearranged passages and deliberately linked her chapters, so D is the logical conclusion: the form was planned. A talks about how readers reacted in the 1960s, and the passage never mentions this. B is right that she revised, but the looping, repeated structure is still in the finished novel, so the claim that she made it linear contradicts the passage. C uses the drafts as evidence too, but the passage never says the drafts are more reliable than the published book, so C goes beyond the argument.

quality.seed: arts and humanities nonfiction — Clarice Lispector's narrative fragmentation in Brazilian modernist literature challenging linear storytelling

hardJudge.note: 지문 논증(단편성→무관심 해석 / 원고 증거: 의도적 재배치·장 연결 / 구조에 무심한 작가는 그런 노력을 하지 않음)을 따라가면 D가 유일하게 도출되는 결론. advisory.note: 각 장이 앞 장의 마지막 문장으로 시작한다는 서술은 실제 작품과 맞다. 원고 연구 부분은 SAT식으로 꾸민 설정이지만 문제 될 정도는 아니다. B와 C는 부분적인 근거가 있다. A는 근거가 약해 쉽게 배제되고, D가 지문을 거의 그대로 바꿔 말한 것이라 medium 중에서도 쉬운 편이다.

problem.passage:
In the early 1920s, Arnold Schoenberg devised a method for organizing atonal music: a composer arranges all twelve pitches of the chromatic scale into a fixed order, called a row, and no pitch may recur until the other eleven have sounded. Because every pitch appears equally often, no single note can emerge as a "home" tone the way the tonic does in a major or minor key. Some critics have argued that Schoenberg's real goal was to make his music sound as random as possible. Yet Schoenberg insisted that every melody and chord in a piece be derived from its row, so that even passages that seem unrelated share the same underlying intervals. Taken together, these features suggest that ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
problem.stimulus: In the early 1920s, Arnold Schoenberg devised a method for organizing atonal music: a composer arranges all twelve pitches of the chromatic scale into a fixed order, called a row, and no pitch may recur until the other eleven have sounded. Because every pitch appears equally often, no single note can emerge as a "home" tone the way the tonic does in a major or minor key. Some critics have argued that Schoenberg's real goal was to make his music sound as random as possible. Yet Schoenberg insisted that every melody and chord in a piece be derived from its row, so that even passages that seem unrelated share the same underlying intervals. Taken together, these features suggest that ______
problem.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: the method was meant to replace the unity once supplied by a home key with a different source of coherence, not to abandon coherence altogether.
the method was meant to give one carefully chosen pitch the central role that the tonic had played, so that listeners could still sense a home tone.
the method was meant to free composers from any fixed ordering of pitches, so that each passage could be written independently of the others.
the method was meant to make pieces sound random to listeners, since equal use of all twelve pitches prevents any note from standing out.
problem.explanation: 지문은 음렬 기법이 '중심음'을 없앤다는 점과, 모든 선율·화음이 음렬에서 파생되어 공통 음정을 공유한다는 점을 제시하므로, 조성을 대신하는 새로운 통일성의 원천을 만든 것이라는 A가 결론으로 가장 적절하다. D는 첫 번째 정보와 비평가의 주장에는 맞지만, 'Yet'으로 시작하는 문장이 바로 그 무작위성 해석을 반박하므로 틀리다. B는 조성의 역할을 언급하지만, 모든 음이 똑같이 자주 나와 중심음이 생길 수 없다는 지문 내용과 모순된다. C는 고정된 음 순서와 모든 악절이 음렬에서 파생된다는 점 모두와 정면으로 충돌한다.
problem.explanationEn: The passage gives two facts: the row keeps any pitch from acting as a home tone, and every melody and chord comes from the row, so they all share the same intervals. Put together, these support A: the row takes over the unifying job the home key used to do. D matches the first fact and the critics' view, but the sentence beginning with "Yet" pushes back against that randomness reading, so D is wrong. B mentions the tonic's role, but it contradicts the passage, which says every pitch appears equally often, so no home tone can emerge. C conflicts with both the fixed order of the row and the rule that every passage comes from it.

quality.seed: arts and humanities nonfiction — Arnold Schoenberg's twelve-tone composition technique developing atonality and serialist musical structure

hardJudge.note: 정답 A 검산: 지문은 (1) 음렬이 중심음을 제거함, (2) 모든 선율·화음이 음렬에서 파생되어 공통 음정을 공유함을 제시하고, 'Yet' 문장이 비평가의 '무작위성' 해석을 반박한다. 두 정보를 종합하면 '조성의 통일성을 대체하는 새로운 응집성의 원천'이라는 A가 유일하게 타당하다. B는 "no single note can emerge as a home tone"과 직접 모순, C는 고정 순서(fixed order)와 모순, D는 'Yet' 문장이 반박하는 비평가 견해를 그대로 채택한 매력적 오답. 해설(한·영) 모두 정답·글자 참조 일치, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 쇤베르크 12음 기법 1920년대 초 고안은 사실과 부합. 난이도: 두 정보 결합 + 'Yet' 전환 인식이 필요하고 D·B가 부분적 근거를 가지므로 medium 적합.

advisory.note: 두 정보(중심음 제거 + 음렬 파생으로 인한 통일성)를 연결해야 하는 구조. D는 비평가 주장과 첫 정보에 부합해 매력적 오답이며 Yet을 읽어야 배제됨. B, C는 비교적 쉽게 배제되지만 말은 됨. 사실관계(1920년대 초 12음 기법)도 정확.

problem.passage:
In the 1920s, German artist Käthe Kollwitz increasingly abandoned etching, a technique that allows fine tonal gradations, in favor of woodcuts and lithographs, which produce bold, simplified forms. Some critics have read this shift as a purely aesthetic turn toward Expressionist style. Yet Kollwitz's own letters show that she wanted her images of hunger, grief, and unemployment in Weimar Germany to circulate as posters and inexpensive prints among working-class viewers, many of whom encountered art only on street walls or in union halls. Moreover, woodcuts and lithographs could be printed in far larger editions and at lower cost than etchings, whose copper plates wear down after relatively few impressions. Taken together, these points suggest that Kollwitz's change in technique ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
problem.stimulus: In the 1920s, German artist Käthe Kollwitz increasingly abandoned etching, a technique that allows fine tonal gradations, in favor of woodcuts and lithographs, which produce bold, simplified forms. Some critics have read this shift as a purely aesthetic turn toward Expressionist style. Yet Kollwitz's own letters show that she wanted her images of hunger, grief, and unemployment in Weimar Germany to circulate as posters and inexpensive prints among working-class viewers, many of whom encountered art only on street walls or in union halls. Moreover, woodcuts and lithographs could be printed in far larger editions and at lower cost than etchings, whose copper plates wear down after relatively few impressions. Taken together, these points suggest that Kollwitz's change in technique ______
problem.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: reflected mainly her growing admiration for the bold forms favored by other Expressionist artists of the period.
was motivated at least partly by a practical goal of reaching a broad audience, not by stylistic preference alone.
was intended to make her images of suffering more technically refined than her earlier etchings had been.
allowed her to sell her prints to wealthy collectors at higher prices than her etchings had commanded.
problem.explanation: 지문은 콜비츠가 노동계급 관객에게 작품을 널리 퍼뜨리고 싶어 했다는 점과, 목판화·석판화가 더 많은 부수를 더 싸게 찍을 수 있다는 점을 연결하므로, 기법 전환에 실용적 목적이 있었다는 B가 정답이다. A는 비평가들의 순수 미학적 해석을 되풀이할 뿐이며, 지문은 'Yet'으로 이 해석에 반박한다. C는 목판화가 미세한 계조가 아니라 단순한 형태를 만든다는 지문 내용과 반대된다. D는 부유한 수집가가 아니라 저렴한 판화와 노동계급 관객을 강조하는 지문과 맞지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The passage links two facts: Kollwitz wanted her work to circulate widely among working-class viewers, and woodcuts and lithographs could be printed in larger, cheaper editions. Put together, these point to B, a practical aim of reaching a broad audience. A just repeats the critics' purely aesthetic reading, which the passage pushes back on with "Yet." C gets it backwards, because the passage says woodcuts produce simplified forms, while etching is the technique with fine gradations. D clashes with the passage's focus on cheap prints and working-class audiences, not wealthy collectors.

quality.seed: arts and humanities nonfiction — Käthe Kollwitz's expressionist printmaking documenting working-class suffering in Weimar Germany politics

hardJudge.note: 정답 B 검산: 지문은 '노동계급 관객에게 널리 유통시키려는 의도'(편지)와 '목판화·석판화의 대량·저가 인쇄 가능성'이라는 두 정보를 'Taken together'로 결합하므로, 실용적 동기가 '적어도 부분적으로' 작용했다는 B가 유일하게 뒷받침된다. A는 'Yet'으로 반박되는 비평가 해석의 반복, C는 에칭이 미세 계조 기법이라는 지문과 반대, D는 저렴한 판화·노동계급 강조와 충돌. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 결론과 선택지 참조가 일치하고 모순 없음. 사실관계(1920년대 목판화·석판화 전환, 포스터·저가 판화 지향, 동판 마모)도 문제 없음. 난이도: A가 지문 속 'Expressionist' 언급으로 부분적 근거를 지니고, C도 기법 용어를 차용해 비교가 필요하나 D는 비교적 쉽게 배제됨. 'not by stylistic preference alone'의 완화 표현이 정답을 다소 드러내 medium 하한에 가깝지만, 두 정보 연결이 요구되므로 medium 적합으로 판정.

advisory.note: 두 근거(편지 속 의도 + 제작 비용·부수)를 연결해야 하는 medium 수준 문항. A는 비평가의 해석을 미끼로 쓰고, C·D는 지문과 반대되는 내용이라 비교적 쉽게 배제된다. 다만 사실 관계는 정확하다(콜비츠는 1920년대에 목판화·석판화로 전환했다).

options: built his motets on a tenor line chosen before he composed any of the other voices.
focused on keeping each added voice consonant with the tenor while paying little attention to how the added voices sounded together.
wrote his tenor lines after the other voices, so that the tenor was fitted to them.
planned how all the voices would sound together instead of setting each voice against the tenor alone.
problem.explanation: 지문은 이전 방식(각 성부를 테너에만 맞춤)에서는 추가 성부끼리 충돌할 수 있었으나, 조스캥의 모테트에서는 테너와 겹치지 않는 성부끼리도 불협화를 피하고 카덴스 화성이 모든 성부의 결합에 의존한다고 말한다. 따라서 모든 성부를 동시에 고려해 작곡했다는 D가 결론이다. A는 테너 우선이라는 옛 방식을 묘사하며 증거와 맞지 않는다. B는 바로 그 옛 방식으로, 성부 간 조화라는 관찰과 모순된다. C는 순서를 뒤집었을 뿐 여전히 한 번에 한 성부씩 짓는 방식이라 '모든 성부의 결합'을 설명하지 못한다.
problem.explanationEn: The passage says the older method checked each added voice only against the tenor, so added voices could clash with each other. In Josquin's motets, though, even voices that never meet the tenor avoid clashing with one another, and cadences depend on all the voices at once. That points to D: he thought about all the voices together. A describes the older tenor-first method, which the evidence argues against. B is that same older approach, and it contradicts the observed harmony between the added voices. C just flips the order but still has him writing one voice at a time, so it can't explain harmony that depends on every voice together.

quality.seed: arts and humanities nonfiction — The development of counterpoint in Renaissance Franco-Flemish composition and structural harmonic innovation

hardJudge.note: 정답 D 검산 완료: 테너와 겹치지 않는 성부끼리의 협화 + 카덴스가 전 성부에 의존 → 동시적(전 성부 고려) 작곡이라는 추론이 유일하게 증거를 설명함. A·B는 지문이 명시적으로 대비한 옛 방식이라 비교적 쉽게 배제되고, C만 강한 오답(순서만 뒤집음)이라 난이도는 medium 하단 경계에 가깝지만, '순차 vs 동시'라는 두 단계 판단이 필요하므로 적합으로 판정. 가상의 학자 Verbeek 인용은 문제 없음(Aron의 '동시 작곡' 개념과 부합하는 표준적 음악사 내용). 해설 한·영 결론 및 선택지 참조 일치, 영어 해설에 한글 없음.

advisory.note: 정답 D는 이전 방식과의 대비와 두 관찰을 연결해야 도출되며, 이는 medium 수준의 두 단계 추론이다. B는 지문과 정면으로 어긋나 비교적 쉽게 배제된다. A와 C는 작곡 순서라는 그럴듯한 쟁점을 다루므로 비교가 필요하다. D의 표현이 지문과 매우 비슷해 쉬운 쪽에 가깝지만 허용 범위 안이다. 역사적 배경인 '동시 작곡'론은 실제 음악학 논의와 일치한다.

problem.passage:
Completed in the early 1300s under the patronage of the Ilkhanid rulers Ghazan and Öljeitü, Rashid al-Din's Jami' al-tawarikh ("Compendium of Chronicles") is often described as the first attempt at a world history. Some scholars have treated the work mainly as a vehicle for Persian literary tradition, with Mongol patrons simply paying for it. Historian Leyla Marandi argues instead that the Mongol court actively shaped how the history was put together. According to Marandi, the project's reliance on oral and written materials held by the Mongol elite, especially the restricted genealogical record known as the Altan Debter, shows that Rashid al-Din's method depended on access only the court could grant.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support Marandi's argument?
problem.stimulus: Completed in the early 1300s under the patronage of the Ilkhanid rulers Ghazan and Öljeitü, Rashid al-Din's Jami' al-tawarikh ("Compendium of Chronicles") is often described as the first attempt at a world history. Some scholars have treated the work mainly as a vehicle for Persian literary tradition, with Mongol patrons simply paying for it. Historian Leyla Marandi argues instead that the Mongol court actively shaped how the history was put together. According to Marandi, the project's reliance on oral and written materials held by the Mongol elite, especially the restricted genealogical record known as the Altan Debter, shows that Rashid al-Din's method depended on access only the court could grant.
problem.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Marandi's argument?
options: Passages in the Jami' al-tawarikh describing Mongol genealogy are written in an elevated Persian prose style closely modeled on earlier Persian court chronicles.
Copies of the Jami' al-tawarikh were produced in a workshop in Tabriz that Rashid al-Din funded from his own estates, and many were sent to cities across the Ilkhanate.
Sections of the Jami' al-tawarikh on Mongol lineages contain details found in no surviving source other than records that could be consulted only with the khan's permission.
Rashid al-Din's accounts of Chinese and Indian history draw heavily on informants who traveled to the Ilkhanid court as merchants and diplomats.
problem.explanation: 마란디의 주장은 이 저작의 방법이 궁정만이 허락할 수 있는 접근권, 즉 제한된 몽골 계보 기록에 의존했다는 것이다. C는 칸의 허가가 있어야만 볼 수 있는 기록에만 나오는 세부 내용이 이 저작에 들어 있다고 하므로, 궁정이 허락한 접근권과 저술 방법을 직접 연결한다. A는 페르시아 문학 전통의 영향을 보여 주므로 오히려 마란디가 반박하는 견해에 가깝다. B는 필사본 제작과 배포에 관한 내용이며, 자금도 궁정이 아니라 라시드 앗딘 개인에게서 나왔다. D는 궁정을 찾은 정보 제공자를 언급하지만 몽골 엘리트의 제한된 자료와는 관련이 없고, 궁정의 허가가 필요했다는 점도 보여 주지 못한다.
problem.explanationEn: Marandi argues that the work's method depended on access that only the court could grant, namely access to restricted Mongol genealogical records. Choice C says the work contains details found only in records that could be consulted with the khan's permission, which directly ties the method to access granted by the court. Choice A points to the influence of Persian literary tradition, so it actually fits the view Marandi rejects. Choice B is about how copies were produced and distributed, and the money came from Rashid al-Din himself, not the court. Choice D mentions informants who visited the court, but they have nothing to do with the Mongol elite's restricted materials, and nothing shows that court permission was required.

quality.seed: arts and humanities nonfiction — Rashid al-Din's Jami' al-tawarikh and Persian historiography integration of Mongol court patronage

hardJudge.note: 정답 C 검산: 마란디 주장의 핵심은 '궁정만이 허락할 수 있는 접근권(제한된 몽골 계보 기록)에 의존한 방법'이며, C는 칸의 허가가 필요한 기록에만 있는 세부 내용이 몽골 계보 부분에 포함되어 있다는 발견으로 이를 직접 뒷받침한다. A는 페르시아 문학 전통 중심 견해(반박 대상)를 지지, B는 필사·배포 및 라시드 앗딘 개인 자금(궁정 무관), D는 궁정을 방문한 정보원이지만 몽골 엘리트의 제한 자료·허가와 무관하여 배제된다. 역사적 배경(가잔·울제이투 후원, 1300년대 초 완성, 알탄 뎁테르의 제한적 성격, 타브리즈 공방)은 사실과 부합하며 마란디는 가공 인물로 문제 없음. 한국어·영어 해설 결론 및 글자 참조 일치, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 난이도: 주장의 핵심(궁정 허가 접근) 파악 + 선택지의 '허가 필요' 요소 대조라는 두 단계 판단이 필요하고 D·B가 부분적 매력도를 가져 medium에 적합.

advisory.note: Leyla Marandi는 가상의 학자로 보이며, 이는 SAT 지문에서 허용되는 방식이다. 오답 D가 궁정과의 연관성으로 그럴듯하게 유인하고, A는 계보 부분을 언급해 부분적으로 맞아 보인다. 중간 난이도로 적절하다.

problem.passage:
Between 1906 and 1918, Béla Bartók traveled through rural Hungary and neighboring regions with a phonograph, recording thousands of peasant songs. Many listeners assume that Bartók simply quoted these tunes in his concert works. Musicologist Lena Farkas argues for a different view: by the 1920s, Bartók had absorbed the structural features of the peasant songs—such as their pentatonic scales and irregular, speech-based rhythms—so thoroughly that he could write wholly original melodies that followed the same rules, rather than borrowing existing tunes.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support Farkas's argument?
problem.stimulus: Between 1906 and 1918, Béla Bartók traveled through rural Hungary and neighboring regions with a phonograph, recording thousands of peasant songs. Many listeners assume that Bartók simply quoted these tunes in his concert works. Musicologist Lena Farkas argues for a different view: by the 1920s, Bartók had absorbed the structural features of the peasant songs—such as their pentatonic scales and irregular, speech-based rhythms—so thoroughly that he could write wholly original melodies that followed the same rules, rather than borrowing existing tunes.
problem.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Farkas's argument?
options: Many of Bartók's compositions from the 1920s contain melodies that match, note for note, songs preserved on his phonograph cylinders from rural Hungarian villages.
Bartók's private letters from the 1920s express his belief that peasant music was more authentic than the urban Hungarian music popular in Budapest's cafés.
Pentatonic scales and irregular rhythms appear frequently in Bartók's 1920s compositions, as they also do in works by several of his Hungarian contemporaries who never did fieldwork.
Many melodies in Bartók's 1920s works match none of the songs in his recordings, yet they share the scales and rhythmic patterns typical of the peasant songs he collected.
problem.explanation: Farkas의 주장은 두 요소로 이루어진다. 바르토크의 1920년대 선율이 녹음된 어떤 곡과도 일치하지 않는 독창적 선율이라는 점과, 그럼에도 민요의 구조적 규칙을 따른다는 점이다. D는 이 두 조건을 모두 충족하므로 정답이다. A는 선율이 그대로 인용되었음을 보여 주므로 오히려 '단순 인용'이라는 통념을 뒷받침한다. B는 민요에 대한 바르토크의 태도만 보여 줄 뿐 작곡 방식은 다루지 않고, C는 해당 특징이 현지 조사를 하지 않은 작곡가들에게도 나타난다는 내용이어서 그 특징이 민요를 흡수한 결과라는 연결을 약화한다.
problem.explanationEn: Farkas's claim has two parts: Bartók's 1920s melodies were original rather than borrowed, and they still followed the structural rules of peasant song. D satisfies both, since the melodies match none of the recorded songs yet share the songs' scales and rhythms, so D is correct. A shows note-for-note borrowing, which supports the popular quotation view instead of Farkas's. B describes only Bartók's attitude toward peasant music, not how he composed. C weakens the link to his fieldwork, because composers who never collected songs used the same features.

quality.seed: arts and humanities nonfiction — Béla Bartók's ethnomusicological collection of Hungarian folk music and modern compositional integration

hardJudge.note: Farkas's argument has two components (original melodies + peasant-song structural rules); D is the only option satisfying both. A supports the rival "quotation" view, B addresses attitude not method, C includes the structural features but severs the fieldwork link. Bartók's fieldwork dates (1906–1918) are historically accurate; Farkas is a plausible fictional scholar. Korean and English explanations agree in conclusion and letter references, English is natural with no Hangul. Two-step reasoning required; A and C are partially grounded distractors, B is plausible—medium fits.

advisory.note: D는 주장의 두 요소(독창적 선율 + 민요 규칙 준수)를 그대로 반영하고 있어 정답이 분명하다. A는 '인용'이라는 통념을 지지하는 함정이고, C는 특징이 나타난다는 점만 부분적으로 맞아 비교해야 배제된다. B는 주제는 관련 있지만 작곡 방식은 다루지 않는다. 중간 난이도로 적절하다. Farkas는 가상 인물로 보이나 지문이 그를 사실처럼 단정하지 않으므로 문제없다.

problem.passage:
Only a small portion of the poetry of Sappho, who lived on the Greek island of Lesbos around 600 BCE, has survived, often as torn scraps of papyrus or short lines quoted by later writers. Even so, these remains are enough to show that she was a skilled inventor of rhythm. The four-line stanza now named after her, the "Sapphic stanza," was so ______ that poets writing centuries later, including the Roman poet Catullus, copied its pattern in their own work.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.stimulus: Only a small portion of the poetry of Sappho, who lived on the Greek island of Lesbos around 600 BCE, has survived, often as torn scraps of papyrus or short lines quoted by later writers. Even so, these remains are enough to show that she was a skilled inventor of rhythm. The four-line stanza now named after her, the "Sapphic stanza," was so ______ that poets writing centuries later, including the Roman poet Catullus, copied its pattern in their own work.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: fragile
influential
obscure
brief
problem.explanation: 빈칸 뒤 'so ~ that' 구문은 수백 년 뒤 카툴루스 같은 시인들이 그 형식을 따라 썼다는 결과를 제시하므로, 빈칸에는 다른 이들에게 영향을 미쳤다는 뜻의 B가 들어가야 한다. A(깨지기 쉬운)는 파피루스 조각이 훼손되었다는 앞 내용과 연결되어 그럴듯해 보이지만, 연 형식이 약하다는 것으로는 후대 시인들이 모방한 이유가 되지 않는다. C(잘 알려지지 않은)는 후대 시인들이 널리 모방했다는 사실과 정반대이다. D(짧은)는 '네 줄 연'이라는 표현과 관련 있어 보이지만, 짧다는 것만으로는 후대 시인들이 따라 쓴 결과를 설명하지 못한다.
problem.explanationEn: The "so ___ that" structure tells you the blank must explain why poets centuries later, like Catullus, copied the stanza's pattern, so the stanza must have had a strong effect on others. That makes B the best answer. A is tempting because the papyrus scraps were torn, but a stanza being fragile wouldn't make later poets imitate it. C means little known, which is the opposite of a pattern that later poets widely copied. D may seem right because the stanza has only four lines, but being short doesn't explain why later poets copied it.

quality.seed: arts and humanities nonfiction — Sappho's lyric poetry fragments and metrical innovation in ancient Greek choral verse tradition

hardJudge.note: 'so ~ that' 결과절(후대 시인 카툴루스가 형식을 모방)이 빈칸을 직접 결정하므로 B(influential)가 유일하게 논리적임. 사실관계(사포 ~600 BCE 레스보스, 카툴루스의 사포 연 사용, 단편 전승) 정확. 오답 A·C·D는 각각 '찢어진 파피루스', '소량만 전승', '네 줄 연'이라는 지문 표면 단서에 끌리는 전형적 오개념으로 설계되어 있고 규칙을 알면 즉시 배제됨. 한·영 해설 모두 결론·글자 참조 일치, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 단일 문맥 단서·한 단계 추론으로 easy에 적합.

advisory.note: so~that 인과 단서가 직접 드러나 한 단계 추론으로 풀린다. 오답 fragile/brief/obscure는 지문 표현(torn scraps, four-line, small portion)과 연결된 그럴듯한 함정이다. 카툴루스가 사포 연을 사용했다는 사실(시 51, 11)은 정확하다.

problem.passage:
In the early fourteenth century, serious literature in Italy was expected to be written in Latin, the language of the Church, the universities, and classical authors such as Virgil. Dante Alighieri nonetheless composed the Divine Comedy in the Florentine vernacular. Some scholars have read this choice as a simple bid for a wider audience, since far more people could follow Tuscan speech than Latin. __Yet Dante had already argued, in his unfinished treatise De vulgari eloquentia, that the vernacular was nobler than Latin because it was learned naturally rather than through rules imposed by schooling.__ Seen in light of that earlier claim, the poem's language looks less like a concession to ordinary readers than a deliberate assertion that a living tongue could carry the weight of theology and philosophy once reserved for Latin.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
problem.stimulus: In the early fourteenth century, serious literature in Italy was expected to be written in Latin, the language of the Church, the universities, and classical authors such as Virgil. Dante Alighieri nonetheless composed the Divine Comedy in the Florentine vernacular. Some scholars have read this choice as a simple bid for a wider audience, since far more people could follow Tuscan speech than Latin. __Yet Dante had already argued, in his unfinished treatise De vulgari eloquentia, that the vernacular was nobler than Latin because it was learned naturally rather than through rules imposed by schooling.__ Seen in light of that earlier claim, the poem's language looks less like a concession to ordinary readers than a deliberate assertion that a living tongue could carry the weight of theology and philosophy once reserved for Latin.
problem.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It presents evidence that Dante's vernacular poem in fact reached a larger audience than Latin works of the period did.
It states the text's main conclusion that Dante's language choice was a challenge to Latin's literary authority.
It describes the cultural expectation that the Divine Comedy departed from, showing how unusual Dante's decision was.
It introduces a view Dante held earlier, which the text uses to complicate one interpretation and support a different one.
problem.explanation:
정답 D: 밑줄 문장은 'Yet'으로 앞의 '독자층 확대' 해석에 제동을 걸고, 『속어론』에서 Dante가 이전에 밝힌 견해를 제시한다. 마지막 문장은 이 견해를 근거로 삼아 다른 해석(라틴어 권위에 대한 의도적 도전)을 내놓는다. 즉 앞 해석을 흔드는 것과 결론을 뒷받침하는 것, 두 단계를 잇는 역할이다.
A(한 단계만 본 역할/오독): 이 문장은 실제 독자 수에 대한 증거가 아니다. 오히려 '더 많은 독자'라는 해석과 거리를 두려고 쓰였다.
B(전체 목적과 문장 기능을 뒤바꿈): 라틴어 권위에 도전했다는 결론은 마지막 문장에서 나온다. 밑줄 문장은 그 결론의 근거일 뿐이다.
C(인접 문장과 혼동): 라틴어가 당연시되던 관습을 설명하는 것은 첫 문장의 역할이다.
problem.explanationEn:
Correct answer, D: The underlined sentence starts with "Yet," which pushes back on the reading that Dante just wanted a wider audience. It then brings in a view Dante had stated earlier, in De vulgari eloquentia. The last sentence uses that earlier view as grounds for a different reading: Dante was deliberately challenging Latin's authority. So the sentence does two linked jobs. It weakens one interpretation and supports another.
A is wrong because the sentence gives no evidence about how many people actually read the poem. In fact, it moves the argument away from the audience explanation.
B is wrong because it mixes up the text's overall conclusion with this sentence's job. The conclusion comes in the final sentence. The underlined sentence only provides the basis for it.
C is wrong because explaining the expectation that serious literature be written in Latin is what the first sentence does, not the underlined one.

hardJudge.note: 지문은 관습(1문장)→Dante의 선택(2)→'독자 확대' 해석(3)→밑줄: 'Yet'으로 그 해석에 제동을 걸며 De vulgari eloquentia의 선행 견해 제시(4)→그 견해를 근거로 '의도적 도전' 결론(5)의 다단계 구조. 밑줄 문장은 앞 해석을 복잡하게 만들고 뒤 결론을 뒷받침하는 연결 역할이므로 D가 정확. A는 '독자 수 증거'로 오독, B는 결론(마지막 문장) 역할을 밑줄에 전가, C는 첫 문장 역할과 혼동—각각 레시피가 요구하는 오답 설계에 부합. De vulgari eloquentia가 미완성이며 속어를 라틴어보다 nobilior로 본다는 서술은 사실과 일치. 해설도 정답을 정확히 뒷받침하며 모순 없음. 난이도는 길이가 아니라 해석 전환 단계 통합에서 나옴.

advisory.note: 지문은 관습 → 기존 해석 → 반대 근거(밑줄) → 대안 결론의 4단계 구조다. 정답 D가 성립하려면 밑줄 문장이 앞 해석을 반박하는 역할과 뒤 결론을 뒷받침하는 역할을 함께 파악해야 한다. B는 근거와 결론을 바꿔 놓은 오답이고, C는 첫 문장의 역할을, A는 둘째 문장의 해석을 가져온 오답이다. De vulgari eloquentia에서 속어가 라틴어보다 고귀하다고 한 내용은 사실에 맞는다.

problem.passage:
Historians of English have long described the Great Vowel Shift as a chain: when the long vowels of Middle English rose, each one supposedly pushed or pulled its neighbor upward so that the vowels kept their distinctness. Linguist Teresa Hale accepts much of this account but argues that the "chain" image overstates how orderly the change was. Records from fifteenth- and sixteenth-century spelling reformers, she notes, show that in some London speech the vowels of words like "meat" and "meet" fell together for a time, a merger the chain model says should not have happened. __Hale points out that later standard English nonetheless kept these pairs apart only because "meat" eventually shifted again, joining a vowel that speakers in other regions had never merged at all.__ For Hale, then, the distinct vowels of modern English reflect not a self-preserving system but the outcome of competition among regional varieties.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
problem.stimulus: Historians of English have long described the Great Vowel Shift as a chain: when the long vowels of Middle English rose, each one supposedly pushed or pulled its neighbor upward so that the vowels kept their distinctness. Linguist Teresa Hale accepts much of this account but argues that the "chain" image overstates how orderly the change was. Records from fifteenth- and sixteenth-century spelling reformers, she notes, show that in some London speech the vowels of words like "meat" and "meet" fell together for a time, a merger the chain model says should not have happened. __Hale points out that later standard English nonetheless kept these pairs apart only because "meat" eventually shifted again, joining a vowel that speakers in other regions had never merged at all.__ For Hale, then, the distinct vowels of modern English reflect not a self-preserving system but the outcome of competition among regional varieties.
problem.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It explains how modern English could end up with the distinct vowels that chain-model historians attribute to an orderly shift, even though the merger Hale cites seemed to rule out such order.
It concedes that the chain-model historians were correct that the vowels never merged, which leads Hale to withdraw her objection to their account.
It shows that spelling reformers in London recorded the merger, which is the main evidence Hale uses to establish her claim about the shift.
It suggests that Hale believes regional varieties of English should be studied separately from the Great Vowel Shift altogether.
problem.explanation: 정답 A: 체인 모델은 현대 영어 모음의 구분을 질서 있는 이동의 결과로 본다. Hale은 런던에서 병합이 있었다고 지적하므로, 현대 영어에 구분이 남아 있다는 사실은 그녀에게 반론처럼 보일 수 있다. 밑줄 문장은 그 구분이 나중에 일어난 재이동과 지역 변종의 영향에서 생겼다고 설명한다. 이로써 체인 모델의 근거를 Hale의 결론으로 다시 해석한다. B: 두 입장을 뒤바꿨다. 밑줄 문장은 병합이 실제로 있었다는 전제 위에 있고, Hale이 반론을 거두는 내용은 없다. C: 한쪽 근거만 사용했다. 철자 개혁가의 기록은 앞 문장의 내용이며, 밑줄 문장은 병합 이후 일어난 일을 다룬다. D: 지문에 없는 반응을 지어냈다. Hale은 지역 변종들의 경쟁을 바로 그 모음 변화를 설명하는 데 쓴다.
problem.explanationEn: A is correct. The chain model says modern English has distinct vowels because the shift was orderly. Hale points to a merger in London speech, so the fact that modern English still keeps these vowels apart could look like evidence against her. The underlined sentence explains that the distinction came back through a later shift and the influence of regional varieties. That reinterprets the chain model's evidence in a way that supports Hale's conclusion. B reverses the two positions. The sentence assumes the merger really happened, and Hale never drops her objection. C uses only one side's evidence. The reformers' records come in the previous sentence, while the underlined sentence describes what happened after the merger. D invents a reaction the text doesn't contain. Hale uses competition among regional varieties to explain the shift itself, not to separate the two topics.

hardJudge.note: 밑줄 문장은 '병합이 있었다면 왜 현대 영어에 구분이 남았는가'라는 암묵적 반론을 선제적으로 처리하며 체인 모델의 핵심 근거(구분 유지)를 Hale의 결론(지역 변종 경쟁)으로 재해석하는 기능을 한다. A가 이를 정확히 기술. B는 입장 역전(병합 부정·반론 철회), C는 앞 문장의 근거를 밑줄 문장에 귀속, D는 지문에 없는 주장. 체인 모델의 전제→병합 관찰→재이동 설명→결론으로 이어지는 다단계 논리를 종합해야 하므로 hard 적합. Teresa Hale은 가상 인물이며 meat/meet 병합·재분화 서술은 역사적 논의와 대체로 부합해 사실 오류로 보지 않음.

advisory.note: 밑줄 문장은 병합 증거(Hale)와 현대 영어의 모음 구분(체인 모델의 근거) 사이의 겉보기 긴장을 풀고, 이를 지역 변종 간 경쟁이라는 결론으로 잇는다. 그래서 A가 정답이다. 이 기능을 파악하려면 Hale의 증거와 결론 사이에서 체인 모델 측이 낼 수 있는 반론을 암묵적으로 추론해야 하므로 hard에 적합하다. 오답 유형도 각각 입장 뒤바뀜(B), 한쪽 근거만 사용(C), 지문에 없는 내용 지어냄(D)으로 잘 나뉜다.

problem.passage:
The Persian philosopher Ibn Sina (980–1037), known in Europe as Avicenna, wrote about many subjects, including the nature of beauty. He argued that a thing is beautiful when its parts fit together in the right proportions, so that nothing is too large, too small, or out of place. __For example, he explained that a building pleases the eye when its walls, arches, and domes are sized in balanced relation to one another.__ Later writers on architecture in the Islamic world drew on this idea, treating harmony among parts as a guide for designing mosques and palaces.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
problem.stimulus: The Persian philosopher Ibn Sina (980–1037), known in Europe as Avicenna, wrote about many subjects, including the nature of beauty. He argued that a thing is beautiful when its parts fit together in the right proportions, so that nothing is too large, too small, or out of place. __For example, he explained that a building pleases the eye when its walls, arches, and domes are sized in balanced relation to one another.__ Later writers on architecture in the Islamic world drew on this idea, treating harmony among parts as a guide for designing mosques and palaces.
problem.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It introduces a view of beauty that later architectural writers argued against.
It offers a specific case that illustrates the general view of beauty described in the previous sentence.
It describes a building that Ibn Sina personally designed using his theory of proportion.
It presents a criticism of the view that beauty depends on balanced parts.
problem.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 "For example"로 시작해, 앞 문장의 일반적 주장(부분들이 알맞은 비례로 맞아떨어질 때 아름답다)을 건물이라는 구체적 사례로 보여 주므로 B가 정답이다. A는 틀렸다. 후대 저자들은 이 생각을 반박한 것이 아니라 받아들여 활용했다. C는 틀렸다. 이븐 시나가 직접 건물을 설계했다는 내용은 지문에 없다. D는 틀렸다. 밑줄 문장은 그 견해를 비판하지 않고 뒷받침한다.
problem.explanationEn: The underlined sentence starts with "For example" and shows a building as a concrete case of the general claim in the previous sentence, that beauty comes from parts fitting together in the right proportions, so B is correct. A is wrong because the later writers built on this idea instead of arguing against it. C is wrong because the text never says Ibn Sina designed any building himself. D is wrong because the sentence supports the view rather than criticizing it.

hardJudge.note: 밑줄 문장이 "For example"로 시작하고 앞 문장의 일반 주장을 건물 사례로 구체화하므로 B가 정확하다. 마지막 문장은 후대 저자들이 이 생각을 '활용(drew on)'했다고 하므로 A는 배제되고, C는 지문에 없는 내용, D는 비판이 아닌 뒷받침이므로 배제된다. 한 가지 명시적 단서(예시 표지어)로 한 단계 추론으로 풀 수 있어 easy에 적합하며, 오답들은 전형적 오개념(반대/비판/과잉추론)으로 그럴듯하다. 이븐 시나 생몰년(980–1037), 아비센나 명칭 등 사실관계도 문제없음. 한·영 해설이 동일 결론·글자 참조를 가지며 영어 해설에 한글 없음.

advisory.note: "For example"라는 명시적 단서로 한 단계 만에 풀 수 있다. 오답은 전형적인 오개념이다. 다만 이븐 시나가 미에 관해 쓴 내용, 특히 건물 사례는 실제 출처로 확인하기 어려우므로 사실 검증이 권장된다(조건부).

problem.passage:
In the second half of the eighteenth century, composers such as Joseph Haydn and Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart wrote symphonies whose first movements often followed a pattern now called sonata form. In this pattern, the opening section presents a main theme in the home key and then moves to a second theme in a new key. A middle section follows, in which the composer breaks the themes into fragments and passes them through several unstable keys. __For example, in the first movement of his Symphony No. 40, Mozart takes a short sighing figure from the opening melody and carries it restlessly from key to key.__ Finally, the closing section brings back both themes, this time keeping them in the home key, which gives listeners a strong sense of arrival.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
problem.stimulus: In the second half of the eighteenth century, composers such as Joseph Haydn and Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart wrote symphonies whose first movements often followed a pattern now called sonata form. problem.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It introduces the main theme that the rest of the text goes on to analyze.
It challenges the claim that Haydn and Mozart used the same pattern in their symphonies.
It offers a specific case of the middle-section technique described in the previous sentence.
It explains why the closing section gives listeners a strong sense of arrival.
problem.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 "For example"로 시작하며, 바로 앞 문장에서 설명한 중간 부분의 기법(주제를 조각내 여러 불안정한 조성으로 옮기는 것)을 모차르트 교향곡 40번이라는 구체적 사례로 보여 준다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A는 이 문장이 글 전체의 중심 주제를 소개하지 않고 뒤에서 분석되지도 않으므로 틀렸다. B는 이 문장이 하이든과 모차르트의 공통점을 반박하지 않으므로 틀렸다. D는 귀결감에 대한 설명이 밑줄 문장이 아니라 마지막 문장에 나오므로 틀렸다.
problem.explanationEn: The underlined sentence starts with "For example," and it shows the middle-section technique from the sentence just before it, where themes are broken into fragments and moved through unstable keys. It uses a specific piece, Mozart's Symphony No. 40, so C is correct. A is wrong because the sentence doesn't introduce the text's main topic, and the rest of the text doesn't analyze it. B is wrong because nothing in the sentence argues against the idea that Haydn and Mozart shared this pattern. D is wrong because the sense of arrival is explained in the final sentence, not in the underlined one.

hardJudge.note: 밑줄 문장은 "For example"로 시작하여 직전 문장(중간 부분에서 주제를 조각내 불안정한 조성으로 옮김)의 구체적 사례를 제시하므로 C가 명확히 정답. 모차르트 교향곡 40번 1악장 전개부가 첫 주제의 한숨 음형을 조성을 옮겨 가며 전개한다는 서술도 사실과 부합. 오답 A(주제 소개), B(반박), D(종결부 귀결감 설명)는 글의 어휘를 빌려 그럴듯하지만 담화 표지와 위치를 보면 바로 배제됨. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 결론·글자 참조 일치, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 단일 담화 표지로 한 단계 추론으로 풀리므로 easy 적합.

advisory.note: "For example"라는 명시적 단서 하나로 풀 수 있다. 모차르트 교향곡 40번 1악장의 발전부(탄식 음형을 여러 조로 옮김)와 재현부(제2주제를 으뜸조로 되돌림)에 대한 서술은 사실과 맞는다. A는 'main theme'이라는 표현, D는 인접한 마지막 문장을 이용한 오답으로, 그럴듯한 오개념 역할을 한다.

problem.passage:
For centuries, engineers assumed that the longevity of Roman vaults such as the Pantheon's dome resulted mainly from the careful selection of volcanic ash, which reacts with lime to form a strong binding matrix. Recent analyses of opus caementicium samples, however, have drawn attention to small white lumps of lime scattered throughout the material, long dismissed as evidence of sloppy mixing. __Researchers led by Admir Masic found that these lumps form when quicklime is mixed in hot, and that when cracks later admit water, the lumps dissolve and recrystallize as calcium carbonate, sealing the fractures.__ This finding suggests that Roman builders may have relied not only on durable ingredients but also on a mixing method that allowed their concrete to repair itself over time.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
problem.stimulus: For centuries, engineers assumed that the longevity of Roman vaults such as the Pantheon's dome resulted mainly from the careful selection of volcanic ash, which reacts with lime to form a strong binding matrix. Recent analyses of opus caementicium samples, however, have drawn attention to small white lumps of lime scattered throughout the material, long dismissed as evidence of sloppy mixing. __Researchers led by Admir Masic found that these lumps form when quicklime is mixed in hot, and that when cracks later admit water, the lumps dissolve and recrystallize as calcium carbonate, sealing the fractures.__ This finding suggests that Roman builders may have relied not only on durable ingredients but also on a mixing method that allowed their concrete to repair itself over time.
problem.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It presents evidence that reinterprets a feature of the material previously regarded as a flaw.
It presents evidence that confirms the long-held view about why volcanic ash made Roman vaults strong.
It presents a criticism of Roman builders for mixing their concrete carelessly.
It presents an example of how modern engineers have copied Roman concrete in new buildings.
problem.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 앞 문장에서 '부주의한 혼합의 증거'로 여겨지던 석회 덩어리가 실제로는 균열을 메우는 자가 치유 기능을 한다는 연구 결과를 제시하므로 A가 정답이다. B는 화산재 설명을 언급하지만, 밑줄 문장은 기존 견해를 확인하는 것이 아니라 새로운 요인을 추가한다. C는 '부주의한 혼합'이라는 표현을 활용하지만, 그것은 밑줄 문장이 뒤집는 과거의 해석이다. D의 현대 건물 적용은 지문에 나오지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The underlined sentence reports findings showing that the lime lumps, once dismissed as signs of sloppy mixing, actually seal cracks, so it reinterprets a supposed flaw. That makes A correct. B mentions volcanic ash, but the sentence adds a new factor instead of confirming the old view. C picks up the "sloppy mixing" idea, but that is the old interpretation the sentence overturns. D is wrong because the text never talks about modern buildings copying Roman concrete.

hardJudge.note: 밑줄 문장은 앞 문장의 '부주의한 혼합의 증거'라는 기존 해석을 뒤집는 자가 치유 메커니즘을 제시하므로 A가 명확히 정답. B(화산재 견해 확인), C(부주의 비판)는 지문 어구를 차용한 부분적 오답이며 D는 지문 밖 내용. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 정답과 일치하고 선택지 글자 참조 정확. 과학 내용은 Masic 연구팀(2023)의 실제 발견과 부합. 문두 '장기간 간과된 특징의 재해석'을 두 문장 연결로 파악해야 하므로 medium 적합.

advisory.note: 내용 사실관계(Masic 연구팀 2023, hot mixing, 석회 덩어리의 자가 치유)는 정확하다. 정답 A도 옳다. 다만 A는 지문의 'long dismissed as evidence of sloppy mixing'을 거의 그대로 바꿔 말한 것이라 정답이 바로 보인다. C(로마 건축가 비판)는 지문의 논조와 정면으로 어긋나고, D(현대 건물 모방)는 지문에 근거가 전혀 없어 곧바로 배제된다. 부분적 근거를 갖춘 오답은 B 하나뿐이다. 따라서 '오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 비교해야 배제'라는 medium 기준을 충족하지 못한다.

problem.passage:

Immanuel Kant, writing three decades later, accepted that such scenes at first overwhelm our senses, but he drew a very different conclusion. Romantic poets such as Wordsworth took up this view and praised the mind's power that is revealed in the moment the senses fail.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

indication
problem.explanation:
정답 C(vindication, 정당성 입증·승리). 'not ... a defeat of the mind, but rather a ______'는 '패배'를 부정하고 그와 반대되는 개념을 요구한다. 뒤 문장에서 상상력은 실패하지만 이성이 자연보다 큰 무한의 이념을 자기 안에서 발견한다고 했고, 낭만주의 시인들이 '드러난 정신의 힘'을 찬양했다고 한다. 따라서 정신이 오히려 자신의 우월성을 입증받는다는 뜻의 vindication이 맞다.
A(subjugation, 굴복시킴)는 부정어 not을 무시하고 defeat와 같은 뜻의 단어를 고른 경우다. 이는 칸트가 아니라 버크의 견해에 해당한다.
B(capitulation, 항복)는 'not A but B'를 '패배에 그치지 않고 아예 항복까지'라는 강조 구문으로 잘못 읽어서, 대조로 뒤집혀야 할 의미를 다시 부정 쪽으로 되돌린 경우다.
D(indication, 징후)는 vindication과 철자·발음만 비슷할 뿐, 패배와 대조되는 의미가 없고 'an indication of the mind'도 문맥에 맞지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn:
The correct answer is C, "vindication." The sentence says the sublime is "not ultimately a defeat of the mind, but rather a ______ of it," so the blank needs a word that means the opposite of defeat. The next clause backs this up. Imagination fails, but reason finds in itself an idea of infinity "that no mountain can match." The Romantics then praise "the mind's power." So the mind isn't beaten. Instead, its superiority is proven, which is exactly what "vindication" means.
A, "subjugation," ignores the word "not." It means about the same thing as defeat, and it describes Burke's view, not Kant's.
B, "capitulation" (surrender), comes from misreading "not... but rather" as building up ("not just a defeat but even a surrender"). That flips the meaning back to the negative side when the sentence calls for a contrast.
D, "indication," only looks and sounds like "vindication." It isn't the opposite of defeat, and "an indication of the mind" doesn't make sense here.

hardJudge.note: 'not ultimately a defeat of the mind, but rather a ______ of it' 구조에서 부정+대조로 극성이 뒤집히며, 뒤의 콜론절(이성이 무한의 이념을 발견)과 마지막 문장(정신의 힘을 찬양)이 vindication을 뒷받침한다. A·B는 모두 defeat와 동극성(부정어 무시/이중반전 결과), D는 형태 유사 오답으로 기능 구분이 적절하다. 버크 1757, 칸트 1790(약 30년 후), 워즈워스 수용 등 사실관계 문제 없음. 버크→칸트 관계 역전 구조와 콜론 뒤 근거 통합을 요구해 medium 이상이나, A·B가 둘 다 '패배' 동의어라 소거가 비교적 쉬운 편임은 참고.

advisory.note: 버크→칸트로 관점이 역전되고 'not defeat but rather' 대조로 극성을 판단하는 구조라 정답 C가 유일하다. 그러나 오답 A·B가 둘 다 defeat의 유의어여서 극성을 이중으로 뒤집은 진짜 오답은 없다(항목 4 미충족). D는 철자만 비슷하게 만든 함정이다. hard로는 경계선 수준이다.

problem.passage:
Text 1
Scholars often describe Matsuo Bashō's haiku as poetry shaped by Zen Buddhism. In this view, the form's extreme brevity mirrors Zen meditation: by stripping a poem down to a single image, such as a frog leaping into an old pond, Bashō sought to record a moment of sudden insight, free of commentary. The poem's minimalism, these scholars argue, is itself a spiritual practice.

Text 2
Bashō did study Zen with the priest Butchō, and Zen ideas plainly color his travel journals. Yet the brevity of his verse was not his invention: the seventeen-syllable hokku had been a fixed opening stanza in linked-verse gatherings long before he began writing. What distinguishes Bashō is less the shortness of his poems than the way he filled that inherited frame with plain, everyday images, a choice that rival poets of his day also made for purely literary reasons.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the scholars' claim in Text 1 about the source of the haiku's brevity?
problem.stimulus:
Text 1
Scholars often describe Matsuo Bashō's haiku as poetry shaped by Zen Buddhism. In this view, the form's extreme brevity mirrors Zen meditation: by stripping a poem down to a single image, such as a frog leaping into an old pond, Bashō sought to record a moment of sudden insight, free of commentary. The poem's minimalism, these scholars argue, is itself a spiritual practice.

Text 2
Bashō did study Zen with the priest Butchō, and Zen ideas plainly color his travel journals. Yet the brevity of his verse was not his invention: the seventeen-syllable hokku had been a fixed opening stanza in linked-verse gatherings long before he began writing. What distinguishes Bashō is less the shortness of his poems than the way he filled that inherited frame with plain, everyday images, a choice that rival poets of his day also made for purely literary reasons.
problem.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the scholars' claim in Text 1 about the source of the haiku's brevity?
options: By agreeing that the brevity reflects Zen meditation, since Bashō studied Zen with the priest Butchō
By arguing that Zen influenced Bashō's poems far more deeply than it influenced his travel journals
By asserting that Bashō's poems actually contain extensive commentary rather than single images
By contending that the brevity came from an established poetic convention rather than from Bashō's Zen practice
problem.explanation: Text 1은 하이쿠의 짧음이 선 명상을 반영한다고 보지만, Text 2는 17음절 홋쿠가 바쇼 이전부터 연가 모임의 고정된 형식이었다고 지적하므로 D가 정답이다. A는 Text 2가 바쇼의 선 수행을 인정한다는 부분적 근거가 있지만, Text 2는 바로 그 형식의 짧음이 선에서 나온 것이 아니라고 반박한다. B는 Text 2가 선이 기행문에 드러난다고 말한 부분을 비틀었을 뿐, 시와 기행문을 비교하지 않는다. C는 Text 2가 바쇼의 일상적 이미지를 강조한 것과 반대이며 어디서도 뒷받침되지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: Text 1 says the haiku's brevity mirrors Zen meditation, but Text 2 points out that the seventeen-syllable hokku was already a fixed stanza in linked verse before Bashō, so D is correct. A has partial support because Text 2 admits Bashō studied Zen, but Text 2 then denies that the short form came from Zen. B twists Text 2's remark that Zen colors the travel journals; Text 2 never compares the journals with the poems. C has no support, and Text 2's focus on plain, everyday images actually goes against it.

quality.seed: arts and humanities nonfiction — Matsuo Bashō's haiku form and zen Buddhist philosophy integration in minimalist poetic composition

hardJudge.note: Text 1의 '짧음=선 명상' 주장에 대해 Text 2는 17음절 홋쿠가 바쇼 이전부터 연가의 고정 형식이었다고 반박하므로 D가 정답임을 직접 확인함. A는 Text 2가 바쇼의 선 수행(붓초 사사)을 인정하는 부분적 근거가 있어 비교가 필요하고, B는 기행문 언급을 비튼 오답, C는 본문과 반대되지만 말은 됨. 한·영 해설 모두 선택지 글자와 결론이 일치하고 영어 해설에 한글 없음. 바쇼가 붓초에게 선을 배운 사실, 홋쿠가 렌가/하이카이의 17음절 발구였다는 점 모두 사실과 부합. 두 텍스트의 주장을 연결해야 하는 medium 수준에 적합.

advisory.note: 정답 D는 Text 2의 '홋쿠는 이미 고정 형식' 진술로 명확히 뒷받침됨. A는 Butchō 언급으로 그럴듯한 유인이고, B는 기행문 언급을 비튼 선택지임. C는 약한 편이지만 medium 수준에 적합함. 사실관계(Butchō, 홋쿠/렌가)도 정확함.

problem.passage:
In a 1968 study, psychologists Robert Rosenthal and Lenore Jacobson told elementary school teachers that certain pupils, actually chosen at random, were about to show unusual intellectual growth. The claim that these students, whom the researchers labeled "bloomers," outperformed their classmates on IQ tests given months later ______ since been tempered by longitudinal classroom research, which suggests that teacher expectation effects are real but generally modest and fade over time.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: In a 1968 study, psychologists Robert Rosenthal and Lenore Jacobson told elementary school teachers that certain pupils, actually chosen at random, were about to show unusual intellectual growth. The claim that these students, whom the researchers labeled "bloomers," outperformed their classmates on IQ tests given months later ______ since been tempered by longitudinal classroom research, which suggests that teacher expectation effects are real but generally modest and fade over time.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: have
has
having
to have
problem.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 "The claim"이고, "that these students ... months later"는 claim의 내용을 설명하는 긴 동격절이다. 문장에는 주절의 정동사가 필요하므로 단수 주어와 일치하는 B "has"가 정답이다. A "have"는 정동사이긴 하지만 바로 앞의 복수 명사 "students"나 "classmates"에 일치시킨 것이어서 단수 주어 claim과 맞지 않는다. C "having"과 D "to have"는 각각 분사와 부정사여서 정동사 역할을 할 수 없고, 그러면 주절에 동사가 없는 불완전한 문장이 된다.
problem.explanationEn: The subject of this sentence is the singular noun "The claim." Everything from "that these students" to "months later" is a long clause that explains what the claim says. The sentence's main clause still needs a finite verb, and it has to be singular to match "claim," so B, "has," is correct. A, "have," is a finite verb, but it agrees with the nearby plural nouns "students" and "classmates" instead of the actual subject. C, "having," is a participle and D, "to have," is an infinitive, so neither one can serve as the main verb, and either choice would leave the sentence incomplete.

quality.seed: social science research — Pygmalion effect in teacher expectations and student academic performance gains longitudinal classroom studies

hardJudge.note: 주어 "The claim"(단수) + 긴 동격 that절 뒤에 정동사 "has since been tempered"가 와야 하므로 B가 정답임을 직접 확인. A는 인접 복수명사(students/classmates)에 끌린 근접 일치 오답으로 매력적이고, C·D는 비정형 동사라 주절 동사 부재. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 결론·글자 참조 일치, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음. Rosenthal & Jacobson 1968 Pygmalion 연구 사실 관계 정확. 다만 오답 중 '부분적으로 맞는 근거'를 가진 것은 A 하나뿐이고 C·D는 같은 유형(비정형)이라 변별 구조가 다소 단순하나, 긴 삽입절로 주어 식별을 요구하는 두 단계 판단이 있어 표준 SAT medium에 부합.

advisory.note: Pygmalion study (1968) facts accurate. Long appositive clause with plural nouns (students, classmates) plus embedded relative clause creates a proper agreement trap; two-step reasoning (finite verb needed + singular subject).

problem.stimulus: A widely cited comparison between speakers of Otjiherero, the language of Namibia's Himba people, and speakers of English, whose vocabularies divide the range of blues and greens at different points, ______ that the color categories a language names may subtly shape how quickly its speakers tell one shade from another.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: suggest
have suggested
suggests
suggesting
problem.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 "comparison"이고, "between ... different points"는 주어를 꾸미는 긴 수식어구이므로 동사는 단수형이어야 한다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A와 B는 바로 앞의 복수 명사 "speakers"나 "vocabularies"에 맞춘 복수 동사라 단수 주어와 수가 일치하지 않는다. D는 분사라서 정동사가 될 수 없고, 이를 넣으면 문장에 본동사가 없는 불완전한 문장이 된다.
problem.explanationEn: The subject of this sentence is the singular noun "comparison." Everything from "between" to "different points" is a long modifier describing it, so the verb has to be singular, and that makes C correct. A and B are plural verbs. They match nearby plural nouns like "speakers" or "vocabularies," but they don't agree with the actual subject. D is a participle, so it can't serve as the main verb, and using it would leave the sentence without a main verb.

hardJudge.note: 주어 "comparison"(단수)과 동사 수 일치 문제. 긴 수식어구(between ... points) 속 복수 명사 speakers/vocabularies가 A·B를 그럴듯한 오답으로 만들고, D는 정동사 부재로 배제됨. 정답 C 검산 완료, 한·영 해설 결론 및 글자 참조 일치, 사실 오류·저작권 문제 없음. 난이도 medium 적합.

advisory.note: 주어 comparison과 동사 사이에 복수 명사가 여럿 끼어 있는 주어-동사 수일치 문항이다. 수식어구 안에 복수 명사가 많아 함정 역할을 하고, 문항은 medium 난이도에 맞다. Himba 색채 연구에 대한 서술도 'may subtly shape'로 신중하게 표현되어 사실 오류가 없다.

The finding that tutored students, especially those paired with partners just one grade level ahead, outperformed their solo counterparts on later tests ______ that the size of the gap between learner and helper may matter as much as the help itself.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: suggesting
suggest
have suggested
suggests
problem.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 "The finding"이고, "that tutored students ... on later tests"는 이 주어를 설명하는 동격절이다. 따라서 빈칸에는 단수 주어와 일치하는 정동사가 필요하므로 D가 정답이다. A는 분사여서 문장에 본동사가 없게 된다. B와 C는 정동사이지만 복수형이라, 빈칸 바로 앞의 "counterparts"나 "tests"에 맞춘 것처럼 보이는 함정이며 단수 주어와 일치하지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The subject of this sentence is the singular noun "The finding." The clause "that tutored students ... on later tests" just describes it. So the blank needs a singular main verb, and that makes D correct. A is a participle, which would leave the sentence with no main verb. B and C are main verbs, but they're plural. They're tempting because they seem to agree with nearby plural nouns like "counterparts" or "tests," but they don't agree with the singular subject.

hardJudge.note: 주어 "The finding"(단수) + 긴 동격 that절 뒤에 정동사 필요. D "suggests"만 단수 정동사로 옳음. A는 분사(본동사 부재), B·C는 복수형으로 인접 명사(counterparts/tests)에 끌린 함정. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 정답과 일치하고 글자 참조 정확, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 주어 식별 + 수 일치 두 단계 판단이 필요하고 오답들이 각각 그럴듯하여 medium 적합. 사실 오류·저작권 문제 없음.

advisory.note: 주어 "The finding"과 동사 사이에 긴 동격절이 끼어 있어 수 일치를 판단해야 하는 표준 중간 난이도 문항이다. 복수 명사 함정과 분사형 오답이 모두 그럴듯하다.
