His distinction between "restricted" codes, which depend on meanings already shared within a close-knit group, and "elaborated" codes, which spell out meaning explicitly for listeners of any background, ______ researchers a way to explain why schools, which tend to reward explicit and context-free speech, might favor middle-class students over their working-class peers.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: offered
have offered
offering
were offering
problem.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 "distinction"이고, 그 뒤의 긴 전치사구와 관계절("between ... codes, which ... and ... codes, which ...")은 수식어일 뿐이므로 단수 주어에 맞는 정동사가 필요하다. A는 단수 주어와 함께 쓸 수 있는 과거형 정동사이므로 정답이다. B와 D는 정동사이긴 하지만 빈칸 바로 앞의 복수 명사 "codes"에 일치시킨 복수형이라 단수 주어 "distinction"과 맞지 않는다. C는 분사이므로 문장에 정동사가 없게 되어 완전한 문장이 되지 못한다.
problem.explanationEn: The subject of this sentence is the singular noun "distinction." Everything after it up to the blank ("between ... codes, which ... and ... codes, which ...") is a modifier, so the blank needs a finite verb that agrees with a singular subject. A is a past-tense finite verb that works with a singular subject, so it's correct. B and D are finite verbs, but they're plural forms that match the nearby noun "codes," not the singular subject "distinction." C is a participle, which leaves the sentence without a main verb, so it isn't a complete sentence.

hardJudge.note: 주어 "distinction"(단수) + 긴 수식어 삽입 후 정동사 일치 문제. A "offered"만 단수 주어와 호환되는 정동사. B·D는 정동사이지만 복수형(근접 명사 "codes"에 끌리는 오답), C는 비정형으로 주절 동사 부재. 긴 삽입 수식어로 주어 식별 단계가 필요해 medium에 적합. Bernstein의 restricted/elaborated code 사실관계도 정확. 지문은 원작으로 보이며 저작권 문제 없음.

advisory.note: 주어 "His distinction"(단수)와 동사 사이에 긴 수식어가 끼어 있는 주어-동사 일치 문항이다. A만 단수 주어와 맞는 정동사다. B와 D는 복수형 정동사로 근처의 복수 명사(codes, listeners)에 끌려 고르게 만드는 함정이고, C는 분사라 문장이 불완전해진다. 수식어를 걷어내고 주어를 찾은 뒤 수 일치를 확인하는 두 단계가 필요해 medium 난이도에 맞다.

D adds "and that," which sets up a parallel "that" clause even though no earlier "that" clause exists, so the sentence breaks down grammatically and loses the explanatory link.

Anthropologist Victor Turner argued that rituals often move participants through a "liminal" phase, a stage in which ordinary social ranks are temporarily suspended. During initiation ceremonies he observed among the Ndembu of Zambia, novices were stripped of names, clothing, and status markers, and they were treated as equals regardless of their family standing. Turner called the intense sense of shared humanity that emerged in such moments "communitas." Crucially, however, he did not view communitas as a rejection of social structure. Once the ritual ended, initiates returned to a hierarchy that assigned them new roles, and Turner maintained that the memory of having stood together as equals made those roles easier to accept. In his account, the brief experience of leveling ultimately helped the community's ordered arrangement of ranks endure.

According to the text, what did Turner believe about the relationship between ritual equality and everyday social order?

problem.explanationEn: D is correct. The text says Turner did not see communitas as rejecting social structure. In his view, the memory of having been equals made people's new roles easier to accept and helped the hierarchy endure. A is the intuitive guess that equality weakens hierarchy, but it directly contradicts the "did not view ... as a rejection" line. B uses a true detail (novices lose their status markers), but it wrongly treats that as the main purpose of ritual equality and says nothing about what happens to social order afterward. C relies on the Ndembu example, but the text never says other societies lack this kind of ritual equality.

problem.passage:
Sociologists have long argued that adolescence in post-industrial societies became a distinct life stage largely because factory and farm work disappeared as routine paths into adulthood, leaving teenagers with years spent mainly among peers in schools. Researcher Ilse Marquardt, studying former mining towns in Germany's Ruhr region, accepts that account but finds it incomplete. Her interviews with three generations of residents show that teenagers in the 1990s and 2000s did not simply fill the gap left by vanished industrial jobs with peer culture. Instead, many deliberately defined themselves against what their grandparents' generation had been, describing mining identity as something to be "outgrown" rather than inherited. Marquardt concludes that generational identity in these towns was shaped as much by active rejection of a remembered past as by the structural absence of work.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

Marquardt's research suggests that young people in former mining towns formed their sense of generation partly by consciously distancing themselves from an older way of life.

D wrongly makes the grandparents the ones pushing rejection, while the text says the teenagers themselves chose to "outgrow" mining identity.

However, the lengthening also appeared at similar rates when younger speakers addressed peers in the presence of an elder who was not part of the conversation. If vowel lengthening signaled only the status of the addressee, this second pattern would not be expected; therefore, Wulandari's findings suggest that ______

options: the feature responds to the social makeup of the whole setting, not just to the person being spoken to.
the feature is used mainly by younger speakers to signal respect toward their peers in everyday conversation.
the feature has gradually replaced krama vocabulary as the main way villagers show deference to elders.
the feature appears only when elders take part in a conversation and is absent among peers otherwise.

B는 동료 대상 사용을 언급해 부분적으로 맞아 보이지만, 사용 조건이 연장자의 존재였다는 점을 무시하고 동료에 대한 존경으로 잘못 해석한다. C는 krama 대체를 주장하지만 지문에 그런 역사적 변화 근거가 없다. D는 연장자가 대화에 참여하지 않을 때도 나타났다는 결과와 정면으로 모순된다.

B seems partly right because it mentions peers, but it misreads the trigger as respect for those peers, when the key factor was the elder's presence. C says lengthening has replaced krama vocabulary, and nothing in the passage supports any historical change like that. D directly contradicts the finding that lengthening appeared even when the elder wasn't part of the conversation.

options: users disclose more about themselves on Instagram than on Facebook because Instagram's design encourages them to post candidly.
users' willingness to share candidly depends less on which platform they use than on how narrow and familiar the audience they expect is.
users' willingness to share candidly depends less on how many followers they have than on how often they update their accounts.

A는 Instagram에서 더 솔직하다는 부분적 관찰에 근거하지만, 공개 Instagram 게시물도 솔직하지 않았으므로 플랫폼 설계를 원인으로 볼 수 없다. C는 B와 같은 틀이지만 게시 빈도는 솔직함의 원인으로 제시되지 않았다. problem.explanationEn: Goffman's theory says people change how they present themselves based on the audience they expect, and the candid posts showed up only on private accounts seen by close friends, which differed from public posts on both platforms. That means candor tracks the audience, not the platform, so B is correct. A builds on the partial observation that users were more candid on Instagram, but their public Instagram posts weren't candid either, so you can't credit Instagram's design. C uses the same structure as B, but the text never connects posting frequency to candor. D isn't supported, because the text says public posts on both platforms differed from the private ones, so it gives you no reason to think public Instagram posts are more accurate.

options: the adults have reasoned at a more advanced stage than the adolescents, since they are older and have had more opportunities for development.
the two groups have reasoned at the same stage, since they reached matching verdicts on the dilemma at matching rates.

A leans on a plausible assumption about age and development, but it decides the stages without any data on reasoning. B treats the same verdict as meaning the same stage, which directly contradicts the passage's main point. D judges the dilemma by whether it produced different verdict rates, but in Kohlberg's approach the dilemma is a tool for drawing out reasoning, so this result doesn't show the dilemma is unsuitable.

That means the difference can't come from how often good things happened. It has to come from how these people mentally engaged with those events, so D is correct. A contradicts the finding that both groups had similar numbers of events. B misses that the study tracked increases in satisfaction, not starting levels, and C brings in unpleasant events, which the passage never discusses.

problem.passage:
When a company automatically enrolls new employees in its retirement savings plan, participation typically rises sharply compared with plans that require employees to sign up on their own. Some economists attribute this jump mainly to inertia: enrolling takes effort, so people tend to stay with whatever arrangement they start in. Behavioral economist Lena Marsh offers a different explanation. She argues that many employees read the default as an implicit recommendation, assuming that the employer chose the default contribution rate because it is a sensible amount to save. If Marsh is right, the default should shape not just whether employees participate but also how much they choose to contribute, even among employees who actively make changes to their plans.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support Marsh's explanation?
problem.stimulus: When a company automatically enrolls new employees in its retirement savings plan, participation typically rises sharply compared with plans that require employees to sign up on their own. Some economists attribute this jump mainly to inertia: enrolling takes effort, so people tend to stay with whatever arrangement they start in. Behavioral economist Lena Marsh offers a different explanation. She argues that many employees read the default as an implicit recommendation, assuming that the employer chose the default contribution rate because it is a sensible amount to save. If Marsh is right, the default should shape not just whether employees participate but also how much they choose to contribute, even among employees who actively make changes to their plans.
problem.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Marsh's explanation?
options: At firms that switched from opt-in to automatic enrollment, participation among new hires rose from about 45 percent to about 85 percent within a year, and few of the automatically enrolled employees left the plan.

Among automatically enrolled employees who logged in to change their investment funds, those whose default contribution rate was 6 percent ended up saving at a much higher rate than those whose default rate was 3 percent.
Among automatically enrolled employees who never logged in to their accounts, nearly all were still contributing at the default rate several years after they were hired.
Among employees at opt-in firms, those who received a simplified one-page sign-up form enrolled at a much higher rate than those who received the standard multipage form.
problem.explanation: Marsh의 설명은 사람들이 기본값을 권장 사항으로 받아들인다는 것이고, 그렇다면 플랜을 적극적으로 바꾸는 직원들조차 기본 납입률의 영향을 받아야 한다. B에서는 계정에 접속해 설정을 바꾼, 즉 관성에 머물지 않은 직원들의 저축률이 기본 납입률에 따라 달라졌으므로 Marsh의 설명을 직접 뒷받침한다. A는 참여율 상승만 보여 주는데, 이는 관성 설명으로도 똑같이 설명된다. C는 접속조차 하지 않은 직원들이 기본값에 머문 경우라서 오히려 관성의 사례에 가깝다. D는 가입 노력을 줄였더니 참여가 늘었다는 내용으로, 노력과 관성을 강조하는 경쟁 설명을 지지한다.
problem.explanationEn: Marsh claims employees treat the default as a recommendation, so the default should affect how much they contribute even when they actively change their plans. B shows that employees who logged in and made changes (so they weren't just stuck through inertia) still saved more when their default rate was higher. That points directly to the default acting as advice. A only shows that participation went up, which the inertia explanation predicts just as well. C describes employees who never logged in and stayed at the default, which is exactly what inertia would predict. D shows that making sign-up easier raised enrollment, which supports the effort-based inertia view rather than Marsh's.

problem.passage:
Psychologists studying the misinformation effect have shown that eyewitnesses who encounter misleading details after an event often later report those details as part of what they saw. Researcher Dana Okafor argues that this distortion arises mainly at retrieval rather than at storage: according to her view, the original memory trace remains intact, but when witnesses are questioned, the more recently encountered misleading detail is simply easier to access and therefore wins out. If Okafor is right, conditions that make the original details easier to reach should reduce the effect.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support Okafor's hypothesis?
problem.stimulus: Psychologists studying the misinformation effect have shown that eyewitnesses who encounter misleading details after an event often later report those details as part of what they saw. Researcher Dana Okafor argues that this distortion arises mainly at retrieval rather than at storage: according to her view, the original memory trace remains intact, but when witnesses are questioned, the more recently encountered misleading detail is simply easier to access and therefore wins out. If Okafor is right, conditions that make the original details easier to reach should reduce the effect.
problem.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Okafor's hypothesis?
options: Witnesses who received misleading details reported them more often when they were questioned one week after the event than when they were questioned one hour after it.
Witnesses who received misleading details reported them less often when the misleading information came from a source they had been told was unreliable.
Witnesses who received misleading details reported them less often when they were questioned in the same room where they had first watched the event, a setting known to cue original memories.
Witnesses who received misleading details reported them just as often when they were given a recognition test as when they were asked to freely describe the event.
problem.explanation: Okafor의 가설은 원래 기억은 보존되며 회상 시점의 접근성 경쟁이 왜곡을 낳는다는 것이고, 따라서 원래 세부에 접근하기 쉬운 조건에서 효과가 줄어야 한다고 예측한다. C는 원래 기억을 떠올리게 하는 장소 단서가 회상 시 오정보 보고를 줄였음을 보여 주므로 이 예측과 직접 일치한다. A는 시간 경과에 따른 효과 증가로, 원래 기억의 소멸(저장 손상)로도 설명되어 회상 가설을 특정해 지지하지 않는다. B는 정보 출처의 신뢰도, 즉 오정보를 받아들이는 단계에 관한 것이어서 회상 시 접근성과 무관하다. D는 검사 형식과 무관하게 효과가 같다는 것으로, 오히려 원래 기억이 덮어써졌다는 저장 설명에 더 가깝다.
problem.explanationEn: Okafor claims the original memory survives and the distortion comes from competition for access at retrieval, so the effect should shrink when the original details are easier to reach. C shows exactly that: a retrieval cue tied to the original event (the same room) reduced reports of misleading details. A shows the effect growing over time, which could just as easily reflect the original memory fading, so it doesn't single out a retrieval explanation. B is about whether witnesses accept the misinformation in the first place, based on source credibility, not about how easy the original details are to access later. D shows no difference between test formats, which actually fits better with the idea that the original memory was overwritten.

advisory.note: 지문 마지막 문장이 예측을 명시해 C가 꽤 쉽게 도출되지만, A·D는 회상/저장 구분을 따져야 배제되므로 medium 범위 안에 있음.

problem.passage:
Many pet owners describe their dogs and cats as feeling guilt, jealousy, or embarrassment. Psychologist Lena Varga and colleagues propose that such anthropomorphic attributions are not simply a result of spending a lot of time with an animal. Instead, they argue, owners attribute complex humanlike mental states to a pet mainly because they are emotionally attached to it: the stronger the bond, the more an owner reads humanlike minds into the animal's behavior, even when the amount of daily contact is the same.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support Varga and colleagues' claim?
problem.stimulus: Many pet owners describe their dogs and cats as feeling guilt, jealousy, or embarrassment. Psychologist Lena Varga and colleagues propose that such anthropomorphic attributions are not simply a result of spending a lot of time with an animal. Instead, they argue, owners attribute complex humanlike mental states to a pet mainly because they are emotionally attached to it: the stronger the bond, the more an owner reads humanlike minds into the animal's behavior, even when the amount of daily contact is the same.
problem.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Varga and colleagues' claim?
options: Owners who spent more hours per day with their pets attributed more complex emotions such as guilt to those pets than did owners who spent fewer hours with their pets.
Owners who were strongly attached to their pets reported spending more hours per day with those pets than did owners who were weakly attached to their pets.
Owners who were strongly attached to their pets and owners who were weakly attached to their pets attributed simple emotions such as fear to those pets at similar rates.

Among owners who spent the same number of hours per day with their pets, those who were strongly attached attributed more complex emotions such as guilt to those pets than did those who were weakly attached.
problem.explanation: 연구진의 주장은 하루 접촉 시간이 같을 때에도 애착이 강할수록 반려동물에게 복잡한 인간적 정신 상태를 더 많이 부여한다는 것이다. D는 접촉 시간을 같게 맞춘 상태에서 애착이 강한 집단이 죄책감 같은 복잡한 감정을 더 많이 부여했다고 보여 주므로 주장을 직접 지지한다. A는 접촉 시간이 원인일 수 있음을 보여 줄 뿐이어서 연구진이 배제하려는 설명에 더 가깝다. B는 애착과 접촉 시간이 함께 움직인다는 것만 보여 주므로 두 요인을 구분하지 못하고, 감정 부여에 대해서도 아무것도 말하지 않는다. C는 공포 같은 단순한 감정에 관한 결과라서 복잡한 정신 상태에 관한 주장과 직접 연결되지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The researchers claim that stronger emotional attachment leads owners to attribute more complex humanlike mental states to their pets, even when daily contact time is the same. D directly supports this: it holds contact time constant and shows that strongly attached owners attributed more complex emotions, such as guilt. A points to time spent together as the cause, which is the explanation the researchers argue against. B shows only that attachment and contact time tend to go together, so it can't separate the two factors, and it says nothing about attributing emotions. C is about simple emotions such as fear, not the complex mental states the claim is about.

problem.passage:
Drawing on Lev Vygotsky's concept of the zone of proximal development—the gap between what a learner can do alone and what she can do with guidance—education researcher Mariela Ostrander studied kindergarten reading instruction. She argues that scaffolding, in which a teacher offers hints, prompts, and modeling while a child attempts a text slightly beyond her independent level, improves early literacy only when the support is gradually withdrawn. According to Ostrander, the benefit comes not from the assistance itself but from the transfer of responsibility: children who keep receiving the same level of help never learn to apply decoding strategies on their own.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support Ostrander's claim?
problem.stimulus: Drawing on Lev Vygotsky's concept of the zone of proximal development—the gap between what a learner can do alone and what she can do with guidance—education researcher Mariela Ostrander studied kindergarten reading instruction. She argues that scaffolding, in which a teacher offers hints, prompts, and modeling while a child attempts a text slightly beyond her independent level, improves early literacy only when the support is gradually withdrawn. According to Ostrander, the benefit comes not from the assistance itself but from the transfer of responsibility: children who keep receiving the same level of help never learn to apply decoding strategies on their own.
problem.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Ostrander's claim?
options: Children whose teachers reduced prompts over the semester decoded unfamiliar texts independently better at year's end than children whose teachers kept prompts at a constant level, even though both groups received the same total minutes of guided reading.

Children whose teachers gave frequent prompts throughout the semester read guided texts more accurately during lessons than children whose teachers gave few prompts, though the two groups were not tested on reading alone.

Children whose teachers selected texts slightly beyond their independent level made larger reading gains than children whose teachers selected texts at their independent level, with prompting held constant in both groups.
Children whose teachers withdrew all prompts at the start of the semester decoded unfamiliar texts independently about as well at year's end as children whose teachers never gave prompts at all.
problem.explanation: Ostrander의 핵심 주장은 도움 자체가 아니라 도움을 '점진적으로' 줄이는 것이 독립적 해독 능력을 높인다는 것이다. A는 총 지도 시간을 같게 통제한 채 도움을 줄인 집단이 일정하게 유지한 집단보다 독립 해독을 더 잘했다고 보여 주므로 주장을 직접 지지한다. B는 도움을 받는 상태에서의 정확도만 보여 주며 독립 읽기는 측정하지 않았다. C는 근접발달영역에 맞춘 텍스트 난이도의 효과일 뿐 도움을 줄이는 것과는 관계가 없다. D는 도움을 한꺼번에 없애는 것과 아예 주지 않는 것을 비교한 것이라 점진적 철회를 검증하지 못한다.
problem.explanationEn: Ostrander's main claim is that the gradual withdrawal of support, not the support itself, is what builds independent decoding. Choice A keeps total guided time the same and shows that children whose prompts were reduced did better on independent decoding than children whose prompts stayed constant, so it directly supports her claim. Choice B only measures accuracy while children were being helped, and it never tests reading alone. Choice C shows that text difficulty within the zone of proximal development matters, but it says nothing about withdrawing support. Choice D compares removing all help at once with never giving help, so it doesn't test gradual withdrawal.

options: Yoruba speakers in towns with active drumming traditions report enjoying drummed praise poetry more than speakers in towns where such traditions have disappeared do.
Yoruba speakers in towns with active drumming traditions distinguish words that differ only in tone more accurately than speakers in otherwise similar towns where such traditions have disappeared do.
Yoruba speakers in towns with active drumming traditions recognize more traditional drummed phrases than speakers in towns where such traditions have disappeared do.
Yoruba speakers in towns with active drumming traditions use more borrowed words from English than speakers in towns where such traditions have disappeared do.
problem.explanation: 가설의 핵심은 북 언어에 대한 노출이 '말하는 언어' 자체의 성조 구분을 보존한다는 것이다. B는 북 전통이 살아 있는 지역 화자가 성조만 다른 단어를 더 정확히 구분한다고 하므로, 노출과 구어의 성조 민감성을 직접 연결한다. A는 북 시에 대한 선호만 보여 줄 뿐 성조 인식과 무관하다. C는 북 문구 자체를 아는 정도일 뿐, 그 노출이 일상 구어의 성조 구분으로 이어지는지는 보여 주지 않는다. D는 차용어로 어휘 변화를 다룰 뿐 성조 보존과는 관련이 없다.
problem.explanationEn: The hypothesis says that exposure to drumming helps preserve tonal distinctions in the spoken language itself. Choice B links exposure to drumming with better recognition of words that differ only in tone, so it supports the claim directly. Choice A shows only that people enjoy the drumming more, which says nothing about tone perception. Choice C shows that people know more drummed phrases, but it doesn't show that this knowledge carries over to tone in everyday speech. Choice D is about borrowed vocabulary, not tone, so it doesn't address the hypothesis.

quality.seed: social science research — Talking drums in west african griots communication systems and linguistic tonal language preservation

hardJudge.note: 정답 B는 가설의 두 요소(북 전통 노출 → 구어 성조 구분 능력)를 직접 연결하며 'otherwise similar towns'로 교란 변수까지 통제해 가장 직접적 지지 근거가 맞다. C는 노출 자체를 보여 주지만 구어 성조로의 전이를 보여 주지 못해 비교가 필요한 양질의 오답이고, D는 '언어 변화'라는 표면적 연결로 그럴듯하다. A는 다소 약한 오답. 한국어·영어 해설 결론과 글자 참조가 일치하고 영어 해설에 한글 없음. dùndún의 작동 원리·요루바 3성조 기술은 사실과 부합. 난이도는 medium 하한에 가깝지만(A·D가 비교적 쉽게 배제됨) 표준 SAT medium 범위 내로 판단.

advisory.note: 정답 B는 옳다. 다만 오답 중 그럴듯한 것은 C(북 문구 인지 ≠ 구어 성조 구분) 하나뿐이다. A(선호)와 D(차용어)는 성조와 관련이 없어 바로 배제된다. 또 B에만 'otherwise similar'라는 통제 조건이 붙어 있어 정답 단서가 된다. 그래서 medium 기준인 '오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가질 것'을 충족하지 못한다. 참고로 'griot'는 원래 만데(Mande) 문화권의 용어라서 요루바 세습 고수(Àyàn 계보)에 'griot-like'라고 붙인 것은 다소 부정확할 수 있다. 실존 학자처럼 보이는 이름에 가설을 귀속한 점도 확인이 필요하다.

problem.passage:
In the late 1800s, reformers in cities such as New York studied crowded tenement buildings, where many families shared small rooms with few windows. The reformers found that tuberculosis spread far more often in these packed, poorly aired apartments than in less crowded homes. Their research led many cities to ______ new housing laws requiring every bedroom to have a window that opened to fresh air.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.stimulus: In the late 1800s, reformers in cities such as New York studied crowded tenement buildings, where many families shared small rooms with few windows. The reformers found that tuberculosis spread far more often in these packed, poorly aired apartments than in less crowded homes. Their research led many cities to ______ new housing laws requiring every bedroom to have a window that opened to fresh air.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: repeal
ignore
adopt
postpone
problem.explanation: 지문은 개혁가들의 연구가 결핵이 환기가 나쁜 과밀 주거에서 잘 퍼진다는 점을 보여 주었고, 그 연구가 도시들로 하여금 침실마다 창문을 요구하는 법을 만들게 '이끌었다(led)'고 말한다. 따라서 새 법을 '채택하다'라는 뜻의 C가 논리적이다. A는 '폐지하다'인데 아직 없는 '새' 법을 폐지할 수 없고 연구 결과와도 반대된다. B '무시하다'와 D '미루다'는 연구가 변화를 이끌었다는 흐름과 맞지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The text says the reformers' research showed that tuberculosis spread more in crowded, poorly aired apartments, and that this research "led" cities to act on new housing laws requiring windows. So the cities must have put those laws into effect, which makes C, meaning to take up or put into effect, the logical choice. A means to cancel a law, but you can't cancel a "new" law that doesn't exist yet, and canceling would go against the research. B and D mean to pay no attention to or to delay, and neither fits the idea that the research pushed cities toward change.

quality.seed: social science research — Tenement reform movement housing density and public health tuberculosis transmission in industrial cities

hardJudge.note: 'research led many cities to ___ new housing laws'에서 'led'와 'new'가 직접 단서가 되어 C(adopt)만 성립. A(repeal)는 아직 없는 새 법에 적용 불가, B·D는 연구가 변화를 이끌었다는 흐름과 모순. 오답 3개 모두 '법에 대해 취할 수 있는 행동'이라 표면적으로 그럴듯하며 단서를 알면 즉시 배제됨. 어휘·문장 평이, 한 단계 추론으로 easy에 적합. 해설 한·영 결론 및 글자 참조 일치, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 역사적 배경(뉴욕 공동주택 개혁, 창문 의무화)도 사실에 부합. 저작권 의심 없음.

advisory.note: 'led ... to'와 'new laws'라는 단서가 직접 드러나 있다. 오답들은 모두 법과 관련된 어휘라 그럴듯하지만, 흐름을 보면 하나의 판단으로 배제된다. 역사적 배경(1901년 뉴욕 공동주택법의 창문 요건)도 맞다.

problem.passage:
Cognitive linguists such as Charles Fillmore and George Lakoff argued that word meanings are not stored as isolated definitions. Instead, a word calls up a larger body of knowledge. For example, the preposition "over" in "the plane flew over the town" brings to mind a whole scene of movement above and across a place. Lakoff showed that this spatial scene is then extended to abstract ideas, as in "the meeting is over." In this view, understanding even a small word ______ a listener's broader knowledge of how the world is organized.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.stimulus: Cognitive linguists such as Charles Fillmore and George Lakoff argued that word meanings are not stored as isolated definitions. Instead, a word calls up a larger body of knowledge. For example, the preposition "over" in "the plane flew over the town" brings to mind a whole scene of movement above and across a place. Lakoff showed that this spatial scene is then extended to abstract ideas, as in "the meeting is over." In this view, understanding even a small word ______ a listener's broader knowledge of how the world is organized.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: ignores
replaces
conceals
draws on
problem.explanation: 지문은 단어가 고립된 정의가 아니라 '더 큰 지식 덩어리를 불러온다'고 말하므로, 작은 단어를 이해하려면 듣는 사람의 폭넓은 지식을 활용해야 한다. 따라서 '~에 의존하다, ~을 끌어 쓰다'라는 뜻의 D가 정답이다. A(무시하다)는 지식이 필요하다는 지문의 요지와 정반대이다. B(대체하다)는 단어 이해가 배경 지식을 없애고 그 자리를 차지한다는 뜻이 되어 논리에 맞지 않는다. C(숨기다)는 지식이 드러나 쓰인다는 지문 내용과 어긋난다.
problem.explanationEn: The passage says a word does not work as an isolated definition but instead "calls up a larger body of knowledge," so understanding a word requires using the listener's broader knowledge. That makes D, "draws on," the correct answer. A, "ignores," says the opposite of the passage's main point that this knowledge is needed. B, "replaces," would mean that understanding a word takes the place of background knowledge, which doesn't make sense. C, "conceals," doesn't fit either, because the passage describes that knowledge being brought forward and used, not hidden.

quality.seed: social science research — Frame semantics fillmore and conceptual metaphor lakoff cognitive linguistics spatial preposition interpretation

hardJudge.note: 정답 D 검증: 지문의 "calls up a larger body of knowledge"와 "brings to mind a whole scene"이 직접 단서로, "draws on"이 유일하게 논리적으로 맞음. A/B/C는 모두 지문 요지와 반대 또는 무관하여 규칙(문맥 단서 확인)을 알면 즉시 배제되지만 어휘 자체는 평이해 그럴듯함. Fillmore(프레임 의미론)와 Lakoff의 "over" 분석(Brugman/Lakoff 1987) 인용은 사실과 부합. 한·영 해설 결론 및 선택지 글자 참조 일치, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 단일 단계 추론, easy 적합.

advisory.note: "calls up a larger body of knowledge"라는 직접 단서가 있어 한 단계 추론으로 D를 고를 수 있음. 오답 A·C는 문맥과 정반대이고 B는 논리에 맞지 않아 easy 수준에 적절함. Fillmore와 Lakoff의 'over' 분석, 즉 프레임 의미론과 방사형 범주 설명은 사실에 부합함.

problem.passage:
Text 1
Education researchers comparing tailoring apprentices with vocational-school students have argued that classroom instruction is the more efficient route to skill. Their reasoning is that a classroom isolates each technique, presents it in a logical sequence, and tests it directly, so learners avoid the slow, unplanned exposure of a busy workshop. Once a principle is mastered in this clean form, they contend, it can be carried into any shop.

Text 2
Anthropologist Jean Lave, studying apprentice tailors in Liberia, found that novices began with peripheral tasks such as sewing buttons and pressing finished garments. These tasks were not filler: through them apprentices absorbed how the shop's work fit together and what counted as competent work among the masters. On Lave's account, knowing a craft cannot be separated from taking part in the community that practices it; skill is the gradually changing role a person comes to hold within that group.

Based on the texts, how would Lave (Text 2) most likely respond to the researchers' claim in Text 1 that a principle mastered in the classroom can be carried into any shop?
problem.stimulus:
Text 1
Education researchers comparing tailoring apprentices with vocational-school students have argued that classroom instruction is the more efficient route to skill. Their reasoning is that a classroom isolates each technique, presents it in a logical sequence, and tests it directly, so learners avoid the slow, unplanned exposure of a busy workshop. Once a principle is mastered in this clean form, they contend, it can be carried into any shop.

Text 2
Anthropologist Jean Lave, studying apprentice tailors in Liberia, found that novices began with peripheral tasks such as sewing buttons and pressing finished garments. These tasks were not filler: through them apprentices absorbed how the shop's work fit together and what counted as competent work among the masters. On Lave's account, knowing a craft cannot be separated from taking part in the community that practices it; skill is the gradually changing role a person comes to hold within that group.
problem.question: Based on the texts, how would Lave (Text 2) most likely respond to the researchers' claim in Text 1 that a principle mastered in the classroom can be carried into any shop?
options: She would object that the claim treats skill as something a learner holds apart from the setting, whereas she sees competence as made up of a person's growing participation in a particular working community.
She would agree that the claim is sound, since presenting techniques in a logical order and testing them directly lets learners avoid the inefficiency of an unplanned workshop.
She would contend that the claim overlooks how apprentices start with peripheral tasks, such as sewing buttons, before they move on to the more central work of the shop.
She would argue that the claim ignores how much cheaper apprenticeships are to run than vocational schools, because masters train novices while producing goods for sale.
problem.explanation:
정답 A: Text 2의 전제는 '지식은 그것을 실천하는 공동체에 참여하는 것과 분리할 수 없다'는 것이다. Text 1의 주장은 원리를 맥락과 떼어 내 어디로든 옮길 수 있다고 보므로, Lave는 바로 그 분리 가능성이라는 가정을 반박할 것이다. 이 반응은 Text 2 어디에도 직접 쓰여 있지 않고 전제에서 추론해야 나온다.
B: Text 1의 논리(순서대로 제시, 직접 평가, 효율성)를 되풀이할 뿐이며 Lave의 관점과 맞지 않는다.
C: Text 2에 나온 관찰(주변적 과제부터 시작)만 반복한다. 이 사실 자체로는 '전이가 가능하다'는 주장을 반박하지 못한다. 반박의 근거가 되는 것은 지식이 참여와 분리될 수 없다는 전제다.
D: 비용 문제는 Text 2가 전혀 다루지 않은 쟁점이다.
problem.explanationEn:
A is correct. Text 2 rests on the idea that knowing a craft can't be separated from taking part in the community that practices it. Text 1's claim assumes that a principle can be pulled out of any setting and carried anywhere. Lave would reject that assumption. Text 2 never states this reply outright, so you have to infer it from her premise.
B just repeats Text 1's reasoning about logical sequence, direct testing, and efficiency. It doesn't match Lave's view.
C only restates something Lave observed: apprentices start with peripheral tasks. That fact alone doesn't push back on the claim that skills transfer. What pushes back is her premise that knowledge can't be separated from participation.
D brings in cost, an issue Text 2 never discusses.

hardJudge.note: Text 2는 Text 1을 언급하지 않으며, 정답 A는 '지식은 공동체 참여와 분리될 수 없다'는 Lave의 전제를 Text 1의 '맥락 독립적 전이' 주장에 적용해 스스로 추론해야 도출된다. B는 Text 1 논리 반복, C는 Text 2의 관찰 사실만 반복(전이 가능성 반박 근거가 아님), D는 본문에 없는 비용 쟁점. Lave의 라이베리아 재단사 연구(단추 달기·다림질 등 주변적 과제로 시작) 묘사는 실제 연구와 부합하며 원문 복제 흔적 없음. 해설은 정답과 오답 사유를 정확히 뒷받침한다.

advisory.note: Text 2는 Text 1을 언급하지 않으며, 정답은 '지식과 공동체 참여는 분리 불가'라는 전제에서 추론된다. C는 Text 2의 사실만 되풀이하는 그럴듯한 함정이다. 다만 A의 'apart from the setting'이 Text 2 마지막 문장과 거의 같은 말이라 추론 부담은 중간 이상 정도다.

problem.passage:
Text 1
In a series of school studies, students who were praised for their effort ("You worked hard on that") persisted longer on difficult puzzles than students praised for their intelligence ("You're so smart"). Researchers argue that effort praise teaches students that ability can grow, and that this belief makes them treat setbacks as chances to learn. Because the belief comes first and the persistence follows, the researchers conclude that schools should train teachers to replace intelligence praise with effort praise.

Text 2
A follow-up team tracked students who got effort praise in the same way and measured both their beliefs about ability and their persistence. Persistence rose in many students whose beliefs about ability did not change at all. Interviews pointed to something else: students read effort praise as a sign that the adult was paying close attention and expected them to keep going, and they kept going to meet that expectation. The team agrees that effort praise tends to produce more persistence than intelligence praise does.

Based on the texts, which part of the reasoning in Text 1 would the author of Text 2 most likely dispute?
problem.stimulus:
Text 1
In a series of school studies, students who were praised for their effort ("You worked hard on that") persisted longer on difficult puzzles than students praised for their intelligence ("You're so smart"). Researchers argue that effort praise teaches students that ability can grow, and that this belief makes them treat setbacks as chances to learn. Because the belief comes first and the persistence follows, the researchers conclude that schools should train teachers to replace intelligence praise with effort praise.

Text 2
A follow-up team tracked students who got effort praise in the same way and measured both their beliefs about ability and their persistence. Persistence rose in many students whose beliefs about ability did not change at all. Interviews pointed to something else: students read effort praise as a sign that the adult was paying close attention and expected them to keep going, and they kept going to meet that expectation. The team agrees that effort praise tends to produce more persistence than intelligence praise does.
problem.question: Based on the texts, which part of the reasoning in Text 1 would the author of Text 2 most likely dispute?
options: The finding that students praised for effort kept working on hard puzzles longer than students praised for intelligence did
The claim that students persist longer because effort praise first changes what they believe about whether ability can grow
The recommendation that schools train teachers to use effort praise in place of intelligence praise
The choice to measure students' persistence with difficult puzzles rather than with regular classroom assignments
problem.explanation:
정답 B: Text 1은 노력 칭찬이 먼저 '능력은 자랄 수 있다'는 신념을 만들고 그 신념 때문에 끈기가 생긴다는 인과 경로를 가정한다. Text 2는 능력에 대한 신념이 전혀 바뀌지 않은 학생들에게서도 끈기가 늘었고, 실제 이유는 어른의 기대에 부응하려는 마음이었다고 보고한다. 따라서 Text 2가 직접 겨냥하는 것은 이 인과 가정이다.
A 오답: Text 2는 노력 칭찬이 더 큰 끈기를 낳는다는 점에 분명히 동의한다(마지막 문장).
C 오답: Text 1의 결론 자체다. Text 2의 설명대로라도 노력 칭찬은 여전히 효과가 있으므로, Text 2가 이 권고를 반박한다고 볼 근거는 없다. Text 2가 문제 삼는 것은 그 이유다.
D 오답: 측정 방법이라는 부수적 세부이고, Text 2는 이에 대해 아무 말도 하지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn:
Correct answer, B: Text 1 assumes a specific chain of cause and effect. First, effort praise changes students' belief that ability can grow, and then that belief makes them persist. Text 2 found that persistence rose in many students whose beliefs about ability never changed. Those students kept going to meet an adult's expectation. That observation attacks exactly this assumed mechanism.
A is wrong because Text 2 openly agrees that effort praise produces more persistence than intelligence praise does.
C is wrong because it is Text 1's conclusion, not the assumption behind it. Even if Text 2's explanation is right, effort praise still works, so Text 2 gives no reason to reject the recommendation. It only questions why the praise works.
D is wrong because the use of puzzles is a minor detail of method, and Text 2 never mentions it.

hardJudge.note: Text 1 구조: 관찰(노력 칭찬→더 긴 끈기) → 기제 가정(능력 성장 신념이 먼저 형성되어 끈기를 낳음) → 결론(교사 훈련 권고). Text 2는 신념이 변하지 않은 학생도 끈기가 증가했고 실제 기제는 어른의 기대 인식이라 보고하며, 노력 칭찬의 효과 자체(A)에는 명시적으로 동의한다. 따라서 Text 2가 반박하는 것은 기제 가정 B이며, 결론 C는 기제가 달라도 유지되므로 반박 대상이 아니다. D는 어느 텍스트도 문제 삼지 않는다. 체크리스트 4항목 모두 충족. 난이도 측면에서 Text 2 마지막 문장이 A를 명시적으로 배제해 주지만, 기제 반박이 결론 반박으로 이어지지 않음을 스스로 판단해 C를 걸러내야 하므로 medium 이상의 입장 추론을 요구한다. 해설은 정답과 오답 근거를 정확히 뒷받침하며 내부 모순 없음.

advisory.note: 정답 B는 Text 1이 가정한 인과 경로(신념→끈기)이고, Text 2는 바로 이 부분과만 충돌한다. A는 Text 2가 동의하는 부분이고, C는 결론이며, Text 2가 이를 반박한다는 근거는 없다. 결론과 가정을 구분해야 하는 문항이지만, 'Because the belief comes first'라는 표현이 정답을 꽤 직접적으로 드러내서 hard로서는 다소 약하다.

problem.passage:
Economists have long noticed that homeowners often refuse to sell their houses for less than they originally paid, even when market prices have clearly fallen. Researchers explain this pattern with the idea of loss aversion: people feel the pain of losing money more strongly than the pleasure of gaining the same amount. __In one study of condominium sales in Boston during the 1990s, owners facing a loss set asking prices well above those of similar units and waited much longer for buyers.__ This evidence suggests that the original purchase price acts as an anchor, shaping sellers' decisions long after it stops reflecting what a home is actually worth.

It describes a problem that the final sentence offers a way to solve.

It raises a question about loss aversion that the text leaves unanswered.

problem.explanationEn: The underlined sentence begins with "For example" and describes the graffiti study, a concrete case of people resisting a message that threatens their freedom, which is exactly the claim made in the sentence before it. problem.passage:
In Hawaiian kinship terminology, a single word, makua, refers to one's father, mother, and all of their siblings, while the term for brother or sister also covers every cousin of one's own generation. Early ethnographers often read this system as a sign of confusion about biological parentage. Anthropologist Elena Vaipulu argues instead that the terms map how responsibility was organized in extended landholding households, where any adult of the parental generation might feed, discipline, or adopt a child. __Supporting this view, Vaipulu notes that when households were broken apart by land privatization in the nineteenth century, speakers increasingly began separating the words for parents from those for aunts and uncles.__ If the vocabulary had simply reflected ignorance of biology, she reasons, a shift in property arrangements should not have changed it.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?

problem.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It presents a historical change that Vaipulu uses as evidence linking the terminology to household organization rather than to beliefs about biology.
It presents a historical change that early ethnographers used as evidence that Hawaiians were uncertain about biological parentage.

problem.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 가구 구조가 해체되자 용어가 분화했다는 역사적 변화를 들며, 이어지는 문장에서 이것이 '생물학적 무지' 해석이 아닌 Vaipulu의 사회 조직 해석을 뒷받침한다고 설명하므로 A가 정답이다. B는 이 사례를 쓴 주체를 초기 민족지학자로 바꾸고 그들의 결론에 연결해 틀렸다. C는 용어가 '분화'되기 시작했다는 내용을 어휘와 가구의 '완전한 포기'로 과장했다. D는 'Supporting this view'라는 표현과 반대로, 이 사례를 Vaipulu 주장의 약점으로 보았다.
problem.explanationEn: The underlined sentence describes how the kinship terms began to split apart once households were broken up. The next sentence explains that this change supports Vaipulu's social-organization account over the "ignorance of biology" reading, so A is correct. B is wrong because it says the early ethnographers used this example, and it ties the example to their conclusion instead of hers. C goes too far: speakers only "increasingly began separating" the terms, which is not the same as abandoning the households and the vocabulary entirely. D is wrong because the sentence begins with "Supporting this view," so it backs up Vaipulu's claim rather than complicating it.

problem.passage:
In Albert Bandura's 1961 Bobo doll study, preschool children watched an adult either attack an inflatable doll—striking it with a mallet and shouting phrases such as "Sock him in the nose"—or play quietly beside it. Later, left alone with the doll, children who had seen the aggressive adult were far more likely to hit it, often repeating the adult's exact words. Many commentators took this as evidence that children absorb violent behavior simply by seeing it. __Yet a 1965 follow-up complicates that reading: when children saw the adult punished for the attack, they imitated it far less, but once offered a reward for copying, they reproduced the aggression just as accurately as the other children did.__ Bandura concluded that watching gives children knowledge of a behavior, while expected consequences decide whether they actually perform it.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
problem.stimulus: In Albert Bandura's 1961 Bobo doll study, preschool children watched an adult either attack an inflatable doll—striking it with a mallet and shouting phrases such as "Sock him in the nose"—or play quietly beside it. Later, left alone with the doll, children who had seen the aggressive adult were far more likely to hit it, often repeating the adult's exact words. Many commentators took this as evidence that children absorb violent behavior simply by seeing it. __Yet a 1965 follow-up complicates that reading: when children saw the adult punished for the attack, they imitated it far less, but once offered a reward for copying, they reproduced the aggression just as accurately as the other children did.__ Bandura concluded that watching gives children knowledge of a behavior, while expected consequences decide whether they actually perform it.
problem.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It gives evidence that children who see an adult punished come to reject violent behavior altogether.
It reports findings indicating that children could learn a behavior they had seen without choosing to carry it out.
It reports findings indicating that rewards, rather than observation, are what teach children aggressive behavior.
It gives evidence that the original study's results came from flaws in how the children were observed.
problem.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 처벌을 본 아이들이 모방을 덜 했지만, 보상을 주자 똑같이 정확하게 공격 행동을 재현했다고 전한다. 즉 행동을 '배운 것'과 '실행하는 것'이 따로 있음을 보여 주며, 이는 마지막 문장의 결론으로 이어지므로 B가 정답이다. A는 처벌 뒤 모방이 줄었다는 부분만 맞을 뿐, 아이들이 나중에 그 행동을 재현했으므로 공격성을 완전히 거부했다는 말은 틀렸다. C는 보상의 역할을 거꾸로 말한다. 보상은 행동을 실행하게 했을 뿐이고, 학습은 관찰로 이미 이루어졌다. problem.explanationEn: The underlined sentence says that children who saw the adult punished imitated less, but when offered a reward, they reproduced the aggression just as accurately as the others. This shows they had learned the behavior without choosing to perform it, which sets up the final sentence's conclusion, so B is correct. A is only partly right: imitation did drop after punishment, but the children later reproduced the behavior, so they did not reject it altogether. C reverses the role of the reward. The reward only got the children to perform the behavior, while the learning had already happened through watching. D claims the original study was flawed, but the text only complicates how the original results were interpreted and never says the results themselves were wrong.

problem.passage:
In the 1950s, psychologist Albert Ellis developed rational emotive therapy, which holds that depression is sustained less by painful events themselves than by rigid beliefs about them, such as "I must succeed at everything or I am worthless." Early accounts of the approach described therapists cataloguing these beliefs as clients reported them, and many later reviewers treated this identification step as the core of the method. Ellis himself ______ that view: in his writings, merely naming an irrational belief accomplished little unless the therapist went on to dispute it actively, pressing the client to test whether the belief was logical, supported by evidence, or useful.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.stimulus: In the 1950s, psychologist Albert Ellis developed rational emotive therapy, which holds that depression is sustained less by painful events themselves than by rigid beliefs about them, such as "I must succeed at everything or I am worthless." Early accounts of the approach described therapists cataloguing these beliefs as clients reported them, and many later reviewers treated this identification step as the core of the method. Ellis himself ______ that view: in his writings, merely naming an irrational belief accomplished little unless the therapist went on to dispute it actively, pressing the client to test whether the belief was logical, supported by evidence, or useful.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: recorded
encountered
rejected
rejection of
problem.explanation:
지문의 앞부분은 초기 설명과 후대 평자들의 해석(신념 식별이 핵심)을 소개하고, 빈칸부터는 Ellis 자신의 반박이 시작된다. 콜론 뒤에서 '식별만으로는 별 효과가 없고 적극적 논박이 필요하다'고 하므로 그 견해를 '거부했다(rejected)'가 맞다. 정답은 C.
A 'recorded'(기록했다)는 치료자가 신념을 목록화하던 첫 단계의 서술에 어울리는 단어일 뿐, 콜론 뒤의 반박 내용과 이어지지 않는다.
B 'encountered'(접했다)는 중립적인 단어라서, Ellis가 그 견해에 반대했다는 점을 드러내지 못한다.
D 'rejection of'는 뜻은 맞지만 명사구여서, 주어 Ellis himself 뒤에 와야 할 동사 자리를 채울 수 없다.
problem.explanationEn:
The first part of the text describes early accounts and later reviewers, who saw identifying beliefs as the core of the method. The blank opens a second stage: Ellis's own response. After the colon, the text says that just naming a belief did little unless the therapist actively disputed it. That means Ellis "rejected" the reviewers' view, so the answer is C.
A, "recorded," fits the first stage, where therapists catalogued beliefs. It doesn't set up the disagreement that follows the colon.
B, "encountered," is neutral. It doesn't show that Ellis opposed the view.
D, "rejection of," has the right meaning, but it's a noun phrase. The sentence needs a verb after the subject "Ellis himself."

hardJudge.note: 지문은 (1) 초기 설명·후대 평자들의 '식별이 핵심' 해석 → (2) Ellis 자신의 반박으로 명확히 두 단계로 나뉘며, 빈칸은 'Ellis himself'로 시작하는 2단계 첫머리에 있다. 콜론 뒤 'merely naming... accomplished little unless... dispute it actively'가 평자들의 견해와 역전된 관계임을 보여 'rejected'가 유일하게 정밀하다. A 'recorded'는 1단계의 cataloguing에 끌리는 오답, D 'rejection of'는 의미는 맞지만 동사 자리에 명사구인 품사 오류 오답으로 체크리스트 4·5를 충족한다. B는 중립어로 반박 기능 결여. REBT(1950s, Ellis, 비합리적 신념 논박)에 관한 사실 서술도 정확하다. 정답자는 평자들의 통념과 Ellis 본인의 입장이 대립한다는 관계 역전을 파악하고 글의 단계 구조를 읽어야 하므로 전형적 medium(단일 문맥 단서 매칭)을 넘어선다. 해설은 정답 및 각 오답 배제 근거를 일관되게 뒷받침한다.

advisory.note: 정답은 옳고 해설과 형식에도 문제가 없다. 다만 'Ellis himself'와 콜론 뒤 'accomplished little unless'가 반박 방향을 직접 알려 주므로 사실상 단서 하나로 풀린다. D는 품사 오류라 바로 걸러지고 A·B는 극성이 중립이라 쉽게 제외된다. 역전 구조가 표면에 그대로 드러나 있어 전형적인 medium 수준이다.

problem.passage:
Historians of Victorian public health long assumed that the health visitors sent into working-class homes in 1890s Manchester did little to improve infant survival, since the women offered advice rather than medicine or money. However, when historian Alys Brennan compared parish burial registers from districts with and without regular visits, she found that infant deaths from diarrheal illness fell markedly only where visitors had taught mothers to boil milk and keep feeding bottles clean. Brennan concludes that the visitors' influence on infant health was far from negligible; it was, in fact, ______.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.stimulus: Historians of Victorian public health long assumed that the health visitors sent into working-class homes in 1890s Manchester did little to improve infant survival, since the women offered advice rather than medicine or money. However, when historian Alys Brennan compared parish burial registers from districts with and without regular visits, she found that infant deaths from diarrheal illness fell markedly only where visitors had taught mothers to boil milk and keep feeding bottles clean. Brennan concludes that the visitors' influence on infant health was far from negligible; it was, in fact, ______.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: inconsequential
modest
controversial
substantial
problem.explanation: 정답 D(substantial). 통념은 방문원이 영아 생존에 거의 기여하지 못했다는 것이었으나, 'However' 뒤의 증거(방문 지역에서만 설사성 질환 사망이 크게 감소)와 'far from negligible; in fact'가 통념과 정반대인 '상당한' 영향을 요구한다. A(inconsequential)는 통념을 그대로 반복한 단어로 'far from negligible'과 모순된다. B(modest)는 전환을 반만 반영한 약한 정도의 표현으로, '현저히(markedly)' 감소했다는 증거와 'far from'의 강한 부정을 담아내지 못한다. C(controversial)는 영향의 크기가 아니라 논란 여부라는 무관한 의미이며, 지문에 논쟁에 관한 근거가 없다.
problem.explanationEn: The correct answer is D (substantial). The old assumption was that health visitors did little for infant survival. After "However," the burial-register evidence shows infant deaths fell markedly only in visited districts, and the phrase "far from negligible; it was, in fact" calls for a word meaning the opposite of the old view: a large effect. A (inconsequential) just repeats the old view and contradicts "far from negligible." B (modest) only half follows the reversal. A "markedly" large drop and the strong wording "far from" point to a big effect, not a small one. C (controversial) is about whether people dispute the effect, not how big it is, and nothing in the text mentions a dispute.

hardJudge.note: 통념(거의 기여 없음)→However→증거(방문 지역에서만 markedly 감소)→'far from negligible; in fact' 구조가 명확하고 D(substantial)가 유일 정답. A는 통념 방향, B는 같은 방향 약한 강도, C는 무관 의미로 오답 설계가 레시피에 부합. 다만 'far from negligible; in fact'가 정답 방향을 매우 직접적으로 지시해 부정어 처리의 난도는 높지 않은 편이며, hard 중에서는 비교적 쉬운 쪽(강도 교정으로 B를 배제하는 부분이 주요 변별점). 가상의 역사가 인물 사용으로 사실 오류·저작권 문제 없음.

advisory.note: 통념(did little)→However→증거(markedly fell)→far from negligible; in fact 구조. A는 통념 방향, B는 같은 방향의 약한 강도로 체크리스트를 충족함. 'far from negligible'은 이중부정을 다시 풀어야 하는 표현이라 medium보다 한 단계 더 생각해야 함. 다만 'in fact'와 'markedly'가 강한 단서여서 hard로서는 다소 쉬운 편임.

problem.passage:
Text 1
Many sustainability campaigns try to change everyday habits, such as how often people do laundry, by giving individuals information about energy use. The assumption is that once people know the facts, they will choose to act differently. According to this view, a person's attitudes and decisions are the main drivers of routine behavior.

Text 2
Sociologist Theodore Schatzki and other practice theorists argue that routines are not mainly the product of individual choices. Instead, practices like laundry are shaped by shared rhythms: work schedules, school timetables, and expectations about clean clothes. Because these timings are woven into daily life, information alone rarely shifts habits; the surrounding schedules and social norms must change too.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the assumption described in Text 1?

B is wrong because Text 2 never talks about how much energy laundry uses. C is wrong because Text 2 says nothing about whether people want to learn about energy. D is wrong because it says informed people drop their habits quickly, which is the opposite of what Text 2 claims.

problem.passage:
Text 1
In the 1950s, psychologist Solomon Asch asked participants to match the length of a line to one of three comparison lines. When a group of actors gave an obviously wrong answer, many participants went along with them. Some researchers concluded that the group's pressure had actually changed what participants saw, making the wrong line look correct to them.

Text 2
Interviews conducted after Asch's sessions suggest a different picture. Most participants who agreed with the group reported that they knew the group's answer was wrong. They said they went along anyway because they did not want to look foolish or stand out. When participants were allowed to write their answers privately, agreement with the incorrect group answer dropped sharply.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the conclusion reached by some researchers in Text 1?

C는 과제가 어려웠다는 내용인데, Text 1은 오답이 '명백히' 틀렸다고 하며 Text 2도 과제 난이도를 언급하지 않는다. D는 참가자들이 오히려 집단의 답이 틀렸다는 것을 알았다고 보고한 Text 2와 정반대이다.
problem.explanationEn: In Text 1, some researchers conclude that group pressure changed what participants actually saw. A misreads the private-answer finding: that finding shows people knew the right answer, which works against the idea that their perception changed. C claims the task was too difficult, but Text 1 describes the wrong answers as obviously wrong, and Text 2 never says the task was hard. D contradicts Text 2, where participants said they knew the group's answer was wrong.

problem.passage:
The Peace of Westphalia, signed in 1648, is often credited with inventing the modern system of sovereign states, in which each government holds supreme authority within its own borders. Historian Andreas Osiander and others have questioned this view. They note that the treaties said little about sovereignty as an abstract principle; instead, they settled specific disputes over territory, religion, and the constitution of the Holy Roman Empire, and they even gave foreign powers such as Sweden and France the right to help guarantee the empire's internal arrangements. Such provisions hardly fit a model of fully independent states. Still, these scholars concede that the settlement mattered: by confirming that rulers could determine the official religion of their lands, it removed one of the main justifications for outside intervention and helped end a century of religious warfare. On this reading, Westphalia advanced the idea of sovereignty without establishing it, and the clear principle later attributed to it was largely built up by nineteenth- and twentieth-century writers looking back.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

options: Because the Peace of Westphalia allowed foreign powers to guarantee arrangements within the Holy Roman Empire, it actually weakened the authority of rulers and prolonged religious conflict.
The Peace of Westphalia created the modern system of sovereign states by declaring that each government holds supreme authority within its own borders.
Historians now agree that the Peace of Westphalia had little lasting importance, since its provisions dealt mainly with narrow territorial and constitutional disputes.
Although the Peace of Westphalia helped end religious wars and moved Europe toward sovereignty, its reputation as the clear origin of the sovereign state system was mostly shaped by later writers.
problem.explanation: 지문은 베스트팔렌 조약이 주권 국가 체제를 '발명'했다는 통념을 반박하면서도, 이 조약이 종교 전쟁을 끝내고 주권 개념을 진전시켰음은 인정한다. 그리고 명확한 원칙이라는 평판은 후대 저술가들이 만들어 낸 것이라고 결론짓는다. 이 두 내용을 모두 담은 D가 정답이다. A는 외국 보증권이라는 세부 내용을 활용하지만, 지문은 조약이 종교 전쟁을 끝내는 데 기여했다고 말하므로 '분쟁을 연장했다'는 서술은 지문과 반대된다. B는 지문이 반박하는 통념을 그대로 되풀이한다. C는 구체적 분쟁이라는 근거를 쓰지만, 학자들이 조약의 중요성을 인정한다는 점(the settlement mattered)과 맞지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The text pushes back on the common claim that Westphalia invented the sovereign state system. At the same time, it grants that the treaty helped end religious warfare and moved Europe toward sovereignty, and it concludes that the treaty's image as a clear origin point was mostly created by later writers. D is correct because it includes both of these points. A uses a real detail, the foreign guarantee rights, but the text says the treaty helped end religious wars, so it did not prolong them. B simply restates the traditional view that the text disputes. C picks up the point about specific disputes, but it ignores the scholars' admission that the settlement mattered.

problem.passage:
When Louis XIV revoked the Edict of Nantes in 1685, he expected the decision to strengthen France by uniting its subjects under a single faith. Roughly 200,000 Huguenots, as French Protestants were called, instead fled the country despite laws forbidding their departure. Many settled in Protestant states such as the Dutch Republic, England, and Brandenburg-Prussia, where rulers welcomed them with tax exemptions and offers of citizenship.

Historians note that the refugees were not a random sample of the French population. Many were skilled silk weavers, watchmakers, printers, and merchants, and they brought trade techniques and commercial networks with them. In Berlin, Huguenot newcomers at one point made up about a fifth of the city's residents and helped establish industries that had barely existed there before. In this way, a policy meant to make France stronger ended up transferring valuable expertise to its rivals.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

problem.explanation: 지문은 칙령 폐지로 숙련된 위그노들이 망명했고, 그들의 기술이 프랑스의 경쟁국들에 이익이 되어 정책 의도와 반대 결과가 났다는 것이 핵심이므로 A가 정답이다. B는 많은 위그노가 떠났다는 사실은 맞지만, 지문은 정책이 의도대로 성공했다고 보지 않고 역효과를 강조한다. C의 세금 면제는 지문에 나오지만, 칙령이 철회되었다는 내용은 없다. D는 베를린 사례를 다루지만 그것은 근거로 든 한 예시일 뿐이고, 작은 마을이 대도시로 성장했다는 주장도 지문에 없다.
problem.explanationEn: The text explains that revoking the edict drove skilled Huguenots abroad, and that their expertise ended up strengthening France's rivals, the opposite of what Louis XIV intended. That makes A the answer. B gets right that many Huguenots left, but the text treats the policy as backfiring, not succeeding. C mentions the tax exemptions from the text, but nothing says the decision was reversed. D focuses on Berlin, which is only one supporting example, and the text never says Berlin grew from a small town into a major capital.

hardJudge.note: 정답 A 검산: 지문 두 문단의 결론 문장("a policy meant to make France stronger ended up transferring valuable expertise to its rivals")을 정확히 요약. B는 '단일 신앙 통합' 목적 문장을 훑어 읽으면 고를 수 있는 부분 정답형 오답, C는 세금 면제 세부를 활용하되 철회는 지문에 없음, D는 베를린 예시를 주제로 과장하고 '소도시→대도시' 미언급 내용 포함 — 오답 구성이 medium 기준에 부합. 사실관계(1685 낭트 칙령 폐지, 약 20만 명 망명, 출국 금지법, 네덜란드·잉글랜드·브란덴부르크-프로이센 수용, 베를린 인구 약 1/5)는 통상 역사 서술과 일치. 한·영 해설 결론 및 선택지 참조 일치, 영어 해설 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 원문 창작으로 저작권 의심 없음.

advisory.note: 정답 A가 지문 마지막 문장의 결론과 일치함. B·C·D는 각각 지문 속 세부(이주, 세금 면제, 베를린)를 일부 활용하므로 비교해야 배제되는 구조로 medium 수준에 적합함. 역사적 사실(약 20만 명, 베를린 인구의 약 1/5)도 통설과 맞음.

problem.passage:
For much of the early eighteenth century, the Navigation Acts, which required that many colonial goods be shipped only to England and carried on English or colonial vessels, existed largely on paper in British North America. Customs officers were few, often underpaid, and frequently willing to accept bribes, so colonial merchants routinely traded with French and Dutch Caribbean ports without consequence. Historians sometimes call this period one of "salutary neglect." After 1763, however, Parliament, burdened by debt from the Seven Years' War, began enforcing the laws in earnest: it expanded the customs service, authorized general search warrants known as writs of assistance, and moved smuggling cases to vice-admiralty courts that operated without juries. Many colonists who had long accepted the Acts in principle now viewed them as intrusive, and their complaints about searches and jury-less trials became early arguments in the broader case against British authority.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
problem.stimulus: For much of the early eighteenth century, the Navigation Acts, which required that many colonial goods be shipped only to England and carried on English or colonial vessels, existed largely on paper in British North America. Customs officers were few, often underpaid, and frequently willing to accept bribes, so colonial merchants routinely traded with French and Dutch Caribbean ports without consequence. Historians sometimes call this period one of "salutary neglect." After 1763, however, Parliament, burdened by debt from the Seven Years' War, began enforcing the laws in earnest: it expanded the customs service, authorized general search warrants known as writs of assistance, and moved smuggling cases to vice-admiralty courts that operated without juries. Many colonists who had long accepted the Acts in principle now viewed them as intrusive, and their complaints about searches and jury-less trials became early arguments in the broader case against British authority.
problem.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Colonial merchants turned to French and Dutch Caribbean ports mainly because the Navigation Acts made trade with England unprofitable.
Parliament passed the Navigation Acts after 1763 as a way to pay off debts left over from the Seven Years' War.
Colonial opposition grew less from the Navigation Acts themselves than from Britain's shift toward strictly enforcing laws it had long overlooked.
Colonists objected to the Navigation Acts chiefly because vice-admiralty courts punished smugglers more harshly than juries had.
problem.explanation: 지문은 항해법이 오랫동안 사실상 집행되지 않다가 1763년 이후 엄격히 집행되면서, 원칙적으로는 이를 받아들이던 식민지인들이 침해적이라고 느끼게 되었다고 설명하므로 C가 정답이다. A는 카리브해 무역이 처벌받지 않았다는 점만 언급될 뿐, 영국과의 무역이 수익성이 없었다는 내용은 없다. B는 전쟁 부채라는 세부를 쓰지만, 이 법은 1763년 이전부터 존재했고 1763년 이후 바뀐 것은 집행이었다. D는 배심원 없는 재판이라는 세부를 쓰지만, 처벌의 엄격함을 비교하지 않으며 글 전체의 요지도 아니다.
problem.explanationEn: C is correct. The text explains that the Navigation Acts went mostly unenforced for decades, and then after 1763 Britain began enforcing them strictly, so colonists who had accepted the laws in principle started seeing them as intrusive. A is wrong because the text only says trade with Caribbean ports went unpunished; it never says trade with England was unprofitable. B uses the war-debt detail, but the Acts already existed before 1763, and what changed afterward was enforcement, not the laws themselves. D picks up the detail about jury-less trials, but the text never compares how harsh the punishments were, and that point isn't the passage's main idea anyway.

hardJudge.note: 정답 C 검산: 지문은 (1) 1763년 이전 항해법의 사실상 미집행, (2) 1763년 이후 엄격한 집행, (3) 원칙적으로 법을 받아들이던 식민지인들이 집행 방식(수색·배심원 없는 재판)을 침해적이라 여기게 됨을 서술하므로 "법 자체보다 집행으로의 전환이 반발을 낳았다"는 C가 요지와 일치. A는 영국 무역의 수익성 언급 없음, B는 법이 1763년 이전부터 존재했다는 지문 내용과 모순, D는 처벌 강도 비교가 지문에 없음. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 동일 결론·글자 참조이며 영어 해설에 한글 없음. 역사적 사실(salutary neglect, writs of assistance, vice-admiralty courts, 7년전쟁 부채)은 정확. 난이도: 시기 구분(법의 존재 vs 집행)과 식민지인의 태도 변화를 연결해야 하며, B·D가 지문 세부를 활용한 부분적 근거를 가져 비교가 필요하므로 medium 적합.

advisory.note: 오답 B·D는 지문 세부(전쟁 부채, 배심원 없는 재판)를 왜곡해 부분 근거를 갖추고 있음. A는 다소 약하지만 그럴듯함. 역사적 사실(항해법, salutary neglect, writs of assistance, vice-admiralty courts)도 정확함.

problem.passage:
Before 1832, many English parliamentary seats belonged to "rotten boroughs," tiny constituencies such as Old Sarum that had almost no residents yet still returned two members to the House of Commons. Meanwhile, fast-growing manufacturing towns like Manchester and Birmingham had no representatives of their own. The Great Reform Act of 1832 took seats away from many rotten boroughs and gave them to these industrial towns, and it also extended the vote to men who occupied property worth at least £10 a year. Some historians have nonetheless argued that the Act left the political influence of the landed aristocracy largely intact. They note that most of the redistributed seats still went to county and small-town constituencies where landlords dominated, and that the £10 property requirement excluded most factory workers in the new urban seats. If these historians are correct, then the Act's main effect was probably that ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
problem.stimulus: Before 1832, many English parliamentary seats belonged to "rotten boroughs," tiny constituencies such as Old Sarum that had almost no residents yet still returned two members to the House of Commons. Meanwhile, fast-growing manufacturing towns like Manchester and Birmingham had no representatives of their own. The Great Reform Act of 1832 took seats away from many rotten boroughs and gave them to these industrial towns, and it also extended the vote to men who occupied property worth at least £10 a year. Some historians have nonetheless argued that the Act left the political influence of the landed aristocracy largely intact. They note that most of the redistributed seats still went to county and small-town constituencies where landlords dominated, and that the £10 property requirement excluded most factory workers in the new urban seats. If these historians are correct, then the Act's main effect was probably that ______
problem.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: industrial workers in Manchester and Birmingham became the largest group of voters in the House of Commons elections that followed.
landowners lost most of their control over county constituencies, even though they kept their hold on small towns.
middle-class urban property holders gained a voice in Parliament while power stayed mostly with the existing landed elite.
rotten boroughs were preserved mostly unchanged, since the redistributed seats were taken from county constituencies instead.
problem.explanation: 이 역사가들은 개정 이후에도 지주 귀족의 영향력이 대체로 유지되었고, 10파운드 재산 요건 때문에 공장 노동자 대부분이 배제되었다고 본다. 그렇다면 투표권을 새로 얻은 사람은 일정 재산을 가진 도시 중산층이었고 권력은 여전히 지주층에 있었다는 결론이 나오므로 C가 정답이다. A는 노동자가 배제되었다는 지문 내용과 반대된다. B는 카운티에서 지주가 우세했다는 진술과 모순된다. D는 이 법이 부패 선거구의 의석을 빼앗았다는 지문 내용과 어긋난다.
problem.explanationEn: These historians argue that the landed aristocracy kept most of its influence and that the £10 property requirement kept most factory workers from voting. That means the new voters were urban middle-class property holders, while power stayed mostly with landowners, so C is correct. A goes against the point that workers were excluded. B contradicts the claim that landlords dominated the county seats. D goes against the passage, which says the Act took seats away from rotten boroughs.

quality.seed: history and civics — The Great Reform Act of 1832 and British electoral franchise expansion rural to urban

hardJudge.note: 지문의 두 근거(지주 우세 선거구로의 의석 재분배 + £10 요건에 따른 노동자 배제)를 결합해야 C에 도달하는 구조로, 정답은 명확하나 두 단계 추론이 필요하다. A(산업도시가 의석을 얻음), B(지주가 영향력 유지), D(의석 재분배)는 각각 지문의 일부 사실을 끌어와 그럴듯하지만 정독 시 지문 진술과 직접 충돌해 배제된다. Old Sarum, 맨체스터·버밍엄의 무대표 상태, £10 가구주 선거권 등 역사적 사실도 정확하다. 한·영 해설 모두 같은 결론과 글자 참조를 가지며 영어는 자연스럽고 한글 혼입이 없다.

advisory.note: C는 £10 재산 요건으로 투표권이 확대된 점과 지주 영향력이 유지되었다는 역사가들의 주장을 합쳐야 도출되므로, 두 단계 추론이 필요하다. B와 D에는 부분적으로 맞는 근거가 들어 있고 A도 말은 된다. 다만 오답 세 개가 모두 지문과 직접 모순되어 난이도가 medium 중에서도 쉬운 편이다. 역사적 서술은 역사가들의 견해로 제시되어 있어 사실 오류로 보지 않는다.

problem.passage:
After the Compromise of 1867 divided the Habsburg realm into Austrian and Hungarian halves, the empire's many nationalities, including Czechs, Croats, Slovaks, Romanians, and others, pressed for greater recognition. Some historians argue that ethnic nationalism alone did not doom the Dual Monarchy. Historian Pieter Judson, for one, contends that before 1914 most nationalist movements sought expanded rights, such as language use in schools and courts, within the empire rather than independence from it, and that the empire's collapse resulted mainly from the strains of the First World War.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support Judson's claim?
problem.stimulus: After the Compromise of 1867 divided the Habsburg realm into Austrian and Hungarian halves, the empire's many nationalities, including Czechs, Croats, Slovaks, Romanians, and others, pressed for greater recognition. Some historians argue that ethnic nationalism alone did not doom the Dual Monarchy. Historian Pieter Judson, for one, contends that before 1914 most nationalist movements sought expanded rights, such as language use in schools and courts, within the empire rather than independence from it, and that the empire's collapse resulted mainly from the strains of the First World War.
problem.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Judson's claim?
options: Programs issued by major Czech and Croatian parties between 1890 and 1910 demanded official status for their languages in local administration while explicitly endorsing continued loyalty to the Habsburg crown.
Programs issued by major Czech and Croatian parties between 1890 and 1910 demanded official status for their languages, and some party leaders later headed independent states formed after 1918.
Programs issued by major Czech and Croatian parties between 1890 and 1910 grew increasingly popular, with membership in nationalist associations rising sharply across the empire.

Programs issued by major Czech and Croatian parties between 1890 and 1910 were frequently debated in parliament, where disputes over language laws repeatedly brought legislative business to a standstill.
problem.explanation: 저드슨의 주장은 1914년 이전 민족주의 운동이 독립이 아니라 제국 '안에서' 권리 확대를 추구했다는 것이다. A는 언어 권리를 요구하면서 합스부르크 왕실에 대한 충성을 명시해 두 요소를 모두 충족한다. B는 언어 요구는 맞지만, 지도자들이 1918년 이후 독립국가를 이끌었다는 내용은 전쟁 이전 목표가 무엇이었는지 보여주지 못하고 오히려 분리주의로 읽힐 수 있다. C는 민족주의가 성장했다는 점만 보여줄 뿐 그 목표가 자치였는지 독립이었는지 알려주지 않는다. D는 민족 갈등이 제국을 마비시켰다는 의미로 읽혀, 민족주의가 불안정을 낳았다는 반대 견해에 더 가깝다.
problem.explanationEn: Judson claims that before 1914, nationalist movements wanted more rights within the empire, not independence from it. Choice A shows parties asking for language rights while openly pledging loyalty to the Habsburg crown, so it matches both parts of the claim. Choice B includes the language demands, but the fact that leaders later headed independent states says nothing about what they wanted before the war, and it may even suggest separatism. Choice C only shows that nationalism grew, not whether its goal was autonomy or independence. Choice D suggests that ethnic conflict paralyzed the government, which fits the opposing view that nationalism destabilized the empire.

A directly supports both components (rights-within-empire + loyalty, not independence). B shares the language-demand stem but the post-1918 detail is irrelevant/undercutting; C shows growth without goals; D supports the opposing view. Requires linking two parts of the claim—medium-appropriate. Explanations in both languages consistent, accurate, no Korean in English version.

problem.passage:
After the Meiji Restoration of 1868, Japan's new government abolished the samurai class's hereditary privileges, and in 1876 it converted the samurai's annual rice stipends into one-time government bonds. Some historians have argued that this conversion did more than end an old social order: by giving former samurai a lump of capital and taking away their guaranteed income, it pushed many of them into new commercial ventures, so that the bonds themselves helped supply the founders of Japan's early modern enterprises.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support the historians' argument?
problem.stimulus: After the Meiji Restoration of 1868, Japan's new government abolished the samurai class's hereditary privileges, and in 1876 it converted the samurai's annual rice stipends into one-time government bonds. Some historians have argued that this conversion did more than end an old social order: by giving former samurai a lump of capital and taking away their guaranteed income, it pushed many of them into new commercial ventures, so that the bonds themselves helped supply the founders of Japan's early modern enterprises.
problem.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the historians' argument?
options: Many former samurai who received stipend bonds in 1876 had already left their domains to take posts in the new national bureaucracy before the conversion took place.
Many former samurai who founded banks and textile firms in the late 1870s paid for their start-up capital by pledging or selling the stipend bonds they had received in 1876.
Many former samurai who founded banks and textile firms in the late 1870s came from families that had run side businesses, such as moneylending, long before the Restoration.
Many former samurai who received stipend bonds in 1876 took part in armed revolts against the government, such as the Satsuma Rebellion of 1877.
problem.explanation: 이 주장의 핵심은 녹봉을 채권으로 바꾼 조치가 직접 원인이 되어 옛 사무라이들이 사업을 시작하게 되었다는 것이다. B는 사무라이 출신 창업자들이 바로 그 채권을 담보로 잡히거나 팔아서 창업 자본을 마련했다고 하므로, 채권과 창업을 직접 이어 준다. C도 사무라이 출신 창업자를 다루지만, 그들의 사업 경험이 왕정복고 이전부터 있었다고 하므로 채권이 아닌 다른 원인을 가리키고, 오히려 주장을 약화한다. A는 관료로 진출한 이야기이고 그마저 채권 전환 이전의 일이라서 상업 활동과 관련이 없다. D는 채권을 받은 뒤 반란에 가담했다는 내용으로, 사업 진출이 아니라 정치적 저항을 보여 준다.
problem.explanationEn: The historians argue that turning stipends into bonds actually caused former samurai to start businesses. B directly links the two by showing that samurai founders paid for their start-up capital with those very bonds. C is also about samurai founders, but it says their business experience came from before the Restoration, which points to a different cause and actually weakens the argument. A is about bureaucratic jobs that came before the conversion, so it says nothing about commerce. D shows samurai rebelling after getting the bonds, which is political resistance, not business activity.

hardJudge.note: 주장의 핵심(채권 → 창업 자본 → 창업)을 B가 직접 연결함을 검산으로 확인. C는 사무라이 창업자를 다루지만 왕정복고 이전 경험을 원인으로 제시해 대안 원인(약화), A·D는 채권 수령자를 다루지만 관료 진출(전환 이전)·무장 반란으로 상업 진출과 무관. 역사적 사실(1868 유신, 1876 질록처분·금록공채, 1877 세이난 전쟁) 정확. 한·영 해설 결론·선택지 글자 일치, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 인과 주장 파악 + 선택지의 시점·대상 대조라는 두 단계 판단이 필요해 medium 적합.

advisory.note: B만 채권과 창업 자본을 직접 잇는다. C는 같은 창업자 집단을 다루면서 다른 원인을 제시해 유력한 오답이다. A·D는 채권 수령자를 언급해 표면적 관련성은 있으나 비교적 쉽게 배제된다. 역사적 사실(1876 녹봉 처분, 1877 세이난 전쟁)은 정확하다.

problem.passage:
Historians have long described the Berlin Conference of 1884–85 as the moment when European powers "carved up" Africa, since no African rulers were invited to the negotiations. Historian Adaeze Okonkwo argues that this image overstates what happened in Berlin. In her view, the conference mainly set procedural rules, such as requiring that claims to coastal territory be announced to other signatories and backed by "effective occupation," and that most actual boundaries were drawn later, through bilateral treaties and agreements with local African authorities whose responses shaped where those lines fell.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support Okonkwo's argument?
problem.stimulus: Historians have long described the Berlin Conference of 1884–85 as the moment when European powers "carved up" Africa, since no African rulers were invited to the negotiations. Historian Adaeze Okonkwo argues that this image overstates what happened in Berlin. In her view, the conference mainly set procedural rules, such as requiring that claims to coastal territory be announced to other signatories and backed by "effective occupation," and that most actual boundaries were drawn later, through bilateral treaties and agreements with local African authorities whose responses shaped where those lines fell.
problem.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Okonkwo's argument?
options: Records show that delegates at the Berlin Conference spent much of their time debating free navigation on the Congo and Niger Rivers, a topic that affected trade routes across a large part of the continent.
Maps produced by European geographers in the decade before the conference already showed several colonial boundaries similar to those that appeared on maps of Africa after 1900.

Archival studies show that most colonial borders in West Africa were set after 1885 in Anglo-French and Franco-German agreements, and many were moved when local leaders refused or bargained over treaty terms.
Several African rulers, including leaders in the Kongo region, sent letters protesting their exclusion from the conference, but European delegates did not respond to those letters.
problem.explanation: 오콘쿼의 주장은 두 부분으로 되어 있다. 회의는 주로 절차 규칙만 정했고, 실제 국경은 회의 이후 양자 협정과 아프리카 현지 권력자의 대응을 통해 정해졌다는 것이다. C는 국경이 1885년 이후 양자 협정으로 정해졌고 현지 지도자의 거부나 협상 때문에 옮겨지기도 했다고 하므로 두 부분을 모두 뒷받침한다. A는 회의에서 다룬 의제가 영토 분할이 아니었음을 보여 줄 수는 있지만, 실제 국경이 언제 어떻게 그어졌는지는 말해 주지 않는다. B는 국경 구상이 회의 이전에 이미 있었다는 내용이라 이후 협정을 통해 국경이 정해졌다는 주장과 맞지 않고, 아프리카인의 역할도 다루지 않는다. D는 아프리카인이 배제되었다는 점만 확인할 뿐, 그들이 국경 형성에 영향을 주었다는 증거가 되지 못한다.
problem.explanationEn: Okonkwo's argument has two parts. She says the conference mostly set procedures, and that real borders were drawn afterward through bilateral treaties shaped by how African authorities responded. Choice C supports both parts: borders were set after 1885 in bilateral agreements, and local leaders' refusals or bargaining moved them. Choice A may suggest that the conference's agenda was not mainly about dividing territory, but it says nothing about when or how actual borders were drawn. Choice B points to boundary ideas that existed before the conference, which doesn't fit the claim that borders came out of later agreements, and it leaves out any African role. Choice D only confirms that Africans were excluded; it gives no evidence that they influenced where the borders fell.

quality.seed: history and civics — The Berlin Conference of 1884 and European partition of Africa without African representation
