In the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries, tapestry workshops in Flemish cities such as Brussels and Arras supplied wall hangings to royal courts across Europe. Because a single large tapestry could take a team of weavers years to finish, workshop owners had strong reasons to guard the dyeing recipes and weaving techniques that set their products apart. Local guilds helped them do so: apprentices were bound to a master for several years, and guild rules barred trained weavers from leaving town to work for foreign rivals. Historians have often concluded that these restrictions kept Flemish skills from spreading. Economic historian Lien Vermeulen argues that the evidence suggests otherwise. Her review of workshop contracts shows that when wars and religious persecution pushed many weavers to flee to England, France, and Italy, foreign rulers quickly set up workshops staffed by these migrants, and the new workshops soon produced tapestries rivaling those of Flanders. In Vermeulen's view, guild rules slowed the movement of expertise only in peaceful times; they could not hold back skills carried by workers who had already decided to leave.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

In Vermeulen's view, guild rules slowed the movement of expertise only in peaceful times; they could not hold back skills carried by workers who had already decided to leave.
problem.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Flemish guilds created apprenticeship rules mainly to keep foreign rulers from buying tapestries made outside Flanders.
Flemish tapestries were valued by European courts chiefly because each one took a team of weavers years to finish.
Flemish guild restrictions succeeded in keeping tapestry techniques within Flanders until foreign workshops developed their own methods.
Flemish guild restrictions did less to contain weaving expertise than historians have assumed, since migrating weavers spread it abroad.
problem.explanation: 지문은 길드 규제가 기술 확산을 막았다는 기존 견해를 소개한 뒤, Vermeulen이 전쟁과 박해로 떠난 직공들이 해외에 기술을 퍼뜨렸으므로 규제의 효과가 제한적이었다고 주장하는 구조이므로 D가 정답이다. A는 길드 규칙의 목적을 지문에 없는 내용(외국 군주의 구매 방지)으로 바꾸었다. B는 지문의 세부 사실(제작 기간)을 담고 있지만 그것은 비밀 보호의 동기를 설명하는 배경일 뿐 중심 생각이 아니다. C는 기존 역사가들의 견해에 가깝고, 해외 공방이 독자적으로 기법을 개발한 것이 아니라 이주 직공들이 기술을 옮겼다는 지문 내용과도 어긋난다.
problem.explanationEn: The text first presents the traditional view that guild rules kept Flemish skills from spreading, then gives Vermeulen's argument that weavers fleeing war and persecution carried those skills abroad anyway, so D is correct. A gives the guild rules a purpose the text never mentions (stopping foreign rulers from buying tapestries made elsewhere). B repeats a true detail about how long production took, but that detail only explains why owners guarded their secrets; it isn't the main point. C matches the older view the text pushes back on, and it also gets the facts wrong: the foreign workshops didn't invent their own methods, because migrant weavers brought the expertise with them.

quality.seed: economics and business — Flemish tapestry workshops and apprenticeship guilds protecting luxury textile production secrets competition

hardJudge.note: 정답 D 검증: 지문 구조(기존 견해 → Vermeulen의 반론 → 이주 직공이 기술 확산)와 정확히 일치. A는 지문에 없는 목적 서술, B는 배경 세부사항, C는 기존 견해이자 "독자적 방법 개발"이라는 사실 왜곡으로 배제됨. B·C가 부분적으로 지문 근거를 가져 비교가 필요하고, A도 그럴듯하여 medium에 적합. 한·영 해설 결론·글자 참조 일치, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음. Vermeulen은 가상 인물로 보이나 역사적 배경(브뤼셀·아라스 태피스트리, 길드 규제, 종교 박해로 인한 직공 이주)은 사실과 부합. 저작권 의심 없음.

advisory.note: 기존 견해와 반론으로 짜인 표준 구조다. C는 기존 견해를 담은 함정, B는 세부 사실을 담은 함정으로 작동한다. A는 다소 약하지만 말은 된다. 중간 난이도에 맞다.

problem.passage:
In the early sixteenth century, the Portuguese crown sought to profit from the pepper trade by controlling the sea route around Africa and channeling all imports through the Casa da Índia, a royal trading house in Lisbon that set wholesale prices for European buyers. Historians have long assumed that this arrangement gave the crown strong pricing power. Yet records show that whenever Lisbon raised its prices sharply, Venetian merchants increased their purchases of pepper that had traveled overland through the Red Sea and Levantine ports, a route the Portuguese never managed to close. European buyers, in other words, could turn to a second supply whenever Lisbon's pepper became too expensive. These records therefore suggest that ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
problem.stimulus: In the early sixteenth century, the Portuguese crown sought to profit from the pepper trade by controlling the sea route around Africa and channeling all imports through the Casa da Índia, a royal trading house in Lisbon that set wholesale prices for European buyers. Historians have long assumed that this arrangement gave the crown strong pricing power. Yet records show that whenever Lisbon raised its prices sharply, Venetian merchants increased their purchases of pepper that had traveled overland through the Red Sea and Levantine ports, a route the Portuguese never managed to close. European buyers, in other words, could turn to a second supply whenever Lisbon's pepper became too expensive. These records therefore suggest that ______
problem.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: the Casa da Índia's ability to raise pepper prices was limited by competition from a trade route outside Portuguese control.
the Casa da Índia's control of the route around Africa allowed it to set pepper prices largely as it wished.
the Casa da Índia's pricing decisions mattered less to Venetian merchants than the cost of shipping through Levantine ports.
the Casa da Índia's high prices eventually forced the Portuguese crown to close the overland route through the Red Sea.
problem.explanation: 지문은 리스본이 가격을 올리면 유럽 구매자가 포르투갈이 막지 못한 홍해·레반트 육로 공급으로 옮겨 갔다고 하므로, 왕실의 가격 결정력은 대체 경로의 경쟁으로 제한되었다는 A가 정답이다. B는 역사가들의 기존 가정을 되풀이할 뿐이며, 'Yet'으로 시작하는 기록은 바로 그 가정을 반박한다. C는 레반트 항구를 언급하지만, 지문에 따르면 베네치아 상인들은 리스본 가격에 맞춰 구매량을 바꿨으므로 리스본 가격이 그들에게 중요했다. D는 포르투갈이 그 경로를 끝내 막지 못했다는 지문 내용과 정면으로 어긋난다.
problem.explanationEn: The text says that when Lisbon raised its prices, buyers switched to pepper shipped over a route Portugal never closed. That means competition limited the crown's pricing power, so A is correct. B just repeats the historians' old assumption, and the records introduced with "Yet" contradict that assumption. C mentions the Levantine ports, but Venetian merchants changed their purchases in response to Lisbon's prices, so those prices clearly mattered to them. D directly contradicts the text, which says the Portuguese never managed to close the overland route.

quality.seed: economics and business — Portuguese spice monopoly Casa da India and pricing power in Asian trade route control

hardJudge.note: 정답 A 검산 일치: 리스본이 가격을 올리면 구매자가 포르투갈이 폐쇄하지 못한 홍해·레반트 경로로 이동했다는 기록은 왕실의 가격 결정력이 외부 경로 경쟁으로 제한되었음을 시사. B는 'Yet' 이전의 기존 가정(반박 대상), C는 베네치아 상인이 리스본 가격에 반응했다는 내용과 충돌, D는 '끝내 막지 못했다'와 정면 모순. 해설(한/영) 결론·글자 참조 일치, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 역사적 사실(Casa da Índia, 베네치아-레반트 후추 경쟁)에 오류 없음. 난이도: 'Yet' 전환 구조 파악 + 'in other words' 문장과 연결하는 두 단계 판단 필요, B·C가 부분적 근거를 가진 오답으로 기능하여 medium에 부합. 다만 'in other words' 문장이 정답을 거의 직접 서술하여 easy 쪽으로 다소 기울어 있음.

advisory.note: 지문의 "European buyers, in other words, could turn to a second supply..." 문장이 결론을 거의 그대로 알려 줘서 추론 단계가 사실상 하나뿐이다. B는 Yet 이후의 반박 대상이라 쉽게 지워지고, D는 "never managed to close"와 정면으로 충돌해 바로 배제된다. 그럴듯한 오답은 C 하나뿐이라, 오답 2개 이상이 부분 근거를 가져야 한다는 medium 기준에 미치지 못한다.

problem.passage:
In the 1870s and 1880s, cheap wheat from the American Midwest, carried by railroads and steamships, began flooding European markets. Large grain estates in eastern Prussia, owned by the landed nobility known as Junkers, relied on armies of seasonal laborers working the fields by hand. Some economic historians argue that the Junkers' political push for high tariffs on imported grain stemmed less from general hostility to trade than from a specific weakness: their labor-intensive methods left them unable to match the falling production costs of mechanized American farms, so that without protection their estates would have operated at a loss.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support the historians' argument?
problem.stimulus: In the 1870s and 1880s, cheap wheat from the American Midwest, carried by railroads and steamships, began flooding European markets. Large grain estates in eastern Prussia, owned by the landed nobility known as Junkers, relied on armies of seasonal laborers working the fields by hand. Some economic historians argue that the Junkers' political push for high tariffs on imported grain stemmed less from general hostility to trade than from a specific weakness: their labor-intensive methods left them unable to match the falling production costs of mechanized American farms, so that without protection their estates would have operated at a loss.
problem.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the historians' argument?
options: Junker estates that switched from grain to sugar beets in the 1880s hired even more seasonal laborers than before, though their landowners kept lobbying for grain tariffs.
Junker landowners publicly opposed tariffs on imported manufactured goods during the same decades in which they pushed for tariffs on imported grain.
American wheat shipped to German ports in the 1880s sold for roughly the same price as wheat grown on small family farms in western Germany.
Estate account books show that per-bushel costs on Junker estates in the 1880s exceeded the price at which American wheat was then selling in Berlin.
problem.explanation: 이 주장의 핵심은 융커 영지의 생산비가 미국 밀 가격을 따라가지 못해 보호 없이는 손실을 봤다는 것이다. D는 융커 영지의 부셸당 비용이 베를린에서 팔리던 미국 밀 가격보다 높았음을 보여 주므로 이를 직접 뒷받침한다. B는 무역 전반에 대한 적대감이 아니라는 점과는 맞지만, 비용 열세를 보여 주지는 않는다. C는 융커 영지가 아니라 서부 독일 소농과 비교한 것이므로 융커의 비용을 알 수 없다. A는 노동 집약성은 언급하지만 곡물 생산비 문제와 연결되지 않고, 곡물을 재배하지 않는데도 관세를 원했다면 오히려 주장을 약화시킬 수 있다.
problem.explanationEn: The core of the argument is that Junker estates couldn't match American production costs, so without tariffs they would have lost money. D shows that the Junker estates' per-bushel costs were higher than the price of American wheat in Berlin, which supports that point directly. B fits the idea that the Junkers weren't hostile to trade in general, but it says nothing about their costs being too high. C compares American wheat with small farms in western Germany, not with Junker estates, so it tells you nothing about Junker costs. A brings up heavy use of labor, but not grain costs. And if estates that no longer grew grain still lobbied for grain tariffs, that could actually weaken the argument.

quality.seed: economics and business — Prussian junker estates and labor-intensive grain production competing against American wheat exports nineteenth century

hardJudge.note: D는 "보호 없이는 손실" 구절을 비용 vs. 미국 밀 가격 비교로 직접 입증하므로 정답 타당. B는 주장의 전반부(무역 일반에 대한 적대감 아님)를 부분 지지하고, C는 가격 비교라는 표면적 유사성, A는 노동 집약성 언급으로 각각 그럴듯한 오답 구성. 한국어·영어 해설 결론과 선택지 참조가 일치하고 영어는 자연스러우며 한글 혼입 없음. 1879년 독일 곡물관세와 융커 배경은 역사적으로 타당한 범위.

advisory.note: D는 비용이 가격을 넘어 보호 없이는 손실이라는 점을 직접 보여 준다. B는 '무역 전반에 대한 적대감이 아니다'라는 부분만 뒷받침하는 그럴듯한 오답이고, C는 비교 대상을 바꿔 놓은 함정, A는 오히려 주장을 약화시키는 선택지다. 오답 간 비교가 필요하므로 medium 난이도에 맞다.

problem.passage:
In the late nineteenth century, Chile's government drew a large share of its revenue from export taxes on nitrate mined in the Atacama Desert, much as Peru had earlier relied on guano exports. Some economic historians argue that this dependence made Chile unusually vulnerable: because the tax was levied on the volume of nitrate shipped, the historians claim, state revenue rose and fell mainly with how much nitrate foreign buyers bought, not with the price nitrate fetched. On this view, the collapse in Chilean public finances after synthetic nitrogen production spread in the 1920s happened chiefly because export volumes dropped, not because prices fell.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support the historians' claim?
problem.stimulus: In the late nineteenth century, Chile's government drew a large share of its revenue from export taxes on nitrate mined in the Atacama Desert, much as Peru had earlier relied on guano exports. Some economic historians argue that this dependence made Chile unusually vulnerable: because the tax was levied on the volume of nitrate shipped, the historians claim, state revenue rose and fell mainly with how much nitrate foreign buyers bought, not with the price nitrate fetched. On this view, the collapse in Chilean public finances after synthetic nitrogen production spread in the 1920s happened chiefly because export volumes dropped, not because prices fell.
problem.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the historians' claim?
options: In years when world nitrate prices fell sharply but tonnage shipped from Chile held steady, Chilean export-tax receipts changed very little.
In years when world nitrate prices fell sharply, foreign-owned mining firms in the Atacama reported much lower profits even though tonnage shipped held steady.
In years when world nitrate prices rose sharply, Chilean export-tax receipts climbed by a similar proportion even though tonnage shipped held steady.
In years when Peruvian guano exports fell sharply, Peru's government revenue declined by a larger proportion than Chile's later did.
problem.explanation: 역사가들의 주장은 칠레 세수가 가격이 아니라 수출 물량에 따라 움직였다는 것이다. A는 가격이 급락해도 물량이 일정하면 세수가 거의 변하지 않았다고 하므로, 세수가 가격과 무관하고 물량에 좌우됨을 직접 보여 준다. B는 가격 하락이 기업 이윤에 영향을 준 사실일 뿐 국가 세수에 관한 것이 아니어서 주장과 연결되지 않는다. C는 물량이 일정한데 가격 상승에 따라 세수가 늘었다는 것으로, 오히려 세수가 가격에 좌우됨을 보여 주므로 주장을 약화한다. D는 페루와 칠레의 세수 감소 폭을 비교할 뿐, 칠레 세수가 물량과 가격 중 무엇에 따라 움직였는지는 다루지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The historians claim that Chile's revenue tracked the volume of nitrate shipped, not its price. A directly supports this: when prices fell but tonnage held steady, tax receipts barely changed, so revenue followed volume rather than price. B is about private firms' profits, not state revenue, so it doesn't speak to how the tax worked. C actually weakens the claim, because it shows receipts rising with price while volume stayed the same. D compares how much revenue Peru and Chile each lost, but it doesn't tell you whether Chile's revenue depended on volume or on price.

quality.seed: economics and business — Chilean nitrate monopoly and guano trade wealth extraction before synthetic fertilizer market disruption

hardJudge.note: 주장은 "세수가 가격이 아닌 물량에 좌우됨"이며, A는 가격 변동·물량 고정 조건에서 세수가 불변임을 보여 변수를 분리해 직접 지지한다. C는 동일 구조(물량 고정)이지만 세수가 가격을 따라가므로 주장을 약화하는 반대 사례, B는 국가 세수가 아닌 민간 이윤, D는 페루 비교로 무관. 한·영 해설 모두 정답과 선택지 참조가 일치하고 영어 해설에 한글 없음. 칠레 질산염 수출세·페루 구아노·1920년대 합성 질소 확산 등 배경 사실도 문제없음. 주장 파악 후 변수 분리 구조를 비교해야 하므로 medium에 적합하며, C가 훑어 읽으면 혼동되는 강한 오답, B도 가격 영향이라는 부분 근거를 가짐.

advisory.note: A는 물량을 고정한 채 가격이 변하는 상황을 보여 주어 세수가 가격과 무관하다는 주장을 직접 뒷받침한다. B(이윤 vs 세수)와 C(방향 반대)는 정독해야 배제되는 그럴듯한 오답이고, D는 비교를 다루는 무관한 오답이다. 중간 난이도에 적합하다.

problem.passage:
In the 1830s, the silk weavers of Lyon, known as canuts, worked mostly in small household workshops, where a master weaver owned a few looms and hired journeymen. After the canuts staged major uprisings in 1831 and 1834 over the low piece rates paid by silk merchants, the industry gradually shifted toward rural factories filled with mechanized looms. Some economic historians argue that the strikes themselves drove this shift: by this account, merchants who had experienced repeated work stoppages in the city deliberately moved production to places where they could control a workforce more directly, even though mechanized looms in that era were not clearly cheaper to run than urban hand weaving.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support the economic historians' argument?
problem.stimulus: In the 1830s, the silk weavers of Lyon, known as canuts, worked mostly in small household workshops, where a master weaver owned a few looms and hired journeymen. After the canuts staged major uprisings in 1831 and 1834 over the low piece rates paid by silk merchants, the industry gradually shifted toward rural factories filled with mechanized looms. Some economic historians argue that the strikes themselves drove this shift: by this account, merchants who had experienced repeated work stoppages in the city deliberately moved production to places where they could control a workforce more directly, even though mechanized looms in that era were not clearly cheaper to run than urban hand weaving.
problem.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the economic historians' argument?
options: Mechanized looms installed in rural factories during the 1840s produced plain silk cloth at a substantially lower cost per meter than hand looms operated in Lyon's household workshops.
Merchants' letters from the 1840s show that firms whose Lyon workshops had halted during the 1831 and 1834 uprisings opened rural factories at higher rates than firms that had faced no stoppages.
Records show that the number of household workshops in Lyon fell steadily throughout the 1850s and 1860s, while the number of rural silk factories in the surrounding region rose.
Several canuts who took part in the 1834 uprising later took jobs in rural silk factories, where they reported earning piece rates similar to those they had received in Lyon.
problem.explanation: 이 주장의 핵심은 merchants가 파업을 겪었기 때문에 직접 통제하려고 일부러 농촌 공장으로 생산을 옮겼다는 인과관계이다. B는 봉기 때 작업 중단을 겪은 회사가 그렇지 않은 회사보다 농촌 공장을 더 많이 열었다는 내용이므로 파업 경험과 이전을 직접 연결해 주장을 뒷받침한다. A는 기계화가 더 싸서 이전했다는 대안 설명을 제시하므로 오히려 주장을 약화시킨다. C는 이 전환이 일어났다는 사실만 보여 줄 뿐, 원인이 파업이었다는 것은 보여 주지 못한다. D는 노동자들의 이후 행적과 임금에 관한 내용이라 merchants의 동기와는 관련이 없다.
problem.explanationEn: The argument is a cause-and-effect claim: merchants moved production to rural factories because they had lived through strikes and wanted more direct control. B links the two directly, since firms whose workshops were shut down during the uprisings opened rural factories more often than firms with no stoppages, so B supports the argument. A gives another explanation, lower costs, which cuts against the claim that cost wasn't what drove the shift. C only shows that the shift happened. It doesn't show that strikes caused it. D is about what workers did and earned later, so it tells you nothing about why the merchants acted.

quality.seed: economics and business — French silk industry Lyonnais workshops and labor strikes catalyzing mechanization and factory system adoption

hardJudge.note: 정답 B 검산: 지문의 주장은 "파업 경험 → merchants의 의도적 농촌 이전"이라는 인과관계이며, B는 작업 중단을 겪은 회사가 그렇지 않은 회사보다 농촌 공장을 더 많이 열었다는 비교 자료로 이 인과관계를 직접 뒷받침함. A는 비용 우위라는 대안 설명으로 지문의 "not clearly cheaper" 전제와 충돌해 약화, C는 전환의 발생만 보여 주고 원인은 제시하지 못함(시기도 1850~60년대로 늦음), D는 노동자 측 정보로 merchants의 동기와 무관. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 동일 결론과 글자 참조를 가지며 모순 없음. 1831·1834 canuts 봉기 등 역사적 사실 적합. 오답 A·C가 부분적 타당성을 가져 비교가 필요하고 D도 말이 되므로 medium 난이도에 부합.

advisory.note: B는 파업 경험 여부에 따라 회사를 비교하는 증거여서 인과 주장을 직접 뒷받침한다. A는 비용이라는 대안 설명을 제시해 주장을 약화시키고, C는 전환이 일어났다는 사실만 확인하며, D는 노동자 측 이야기로 상인의 동기와 관계가 없다. 오답이 모두 그럴듯해 medium 난이도에 맞는다. 다만 B가 비교군을 포함한 증거라 정답이 다소 쉽게 드러날 수 있다.

problem.passage:
Text 1
Historians often credit the collapse of the British railway share mania of the mid-1840s with prompting new rules for protecting investors. But an account of why a regulation emerged is persuasive, I would argue, only if it can show that lawmakers' own records connect the rule to the crisis; a rule that merely follows a crash in time, without such documented links, may have been driven by older concerns that the crash simply made convenient to cite.

Text 2
In 1844 and 1845, speculators poured money into hundreds of proposed railway companies, many of which never laid a mile of track. When share prices fell sharply in 1847, thousands of small investors were ruined. Within a few years, Parliament had tightened requirements for company accounts and audits. The sequence makes clear that the mania's collapse was what produced Britain's early investor protection laws.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 1 most likely evaluate the conclusion presented in Text 2?
problem.stimulus:
Text 1
Historians often credit the collapse of the British railway share mania of the mid-1840s with prompting new rules for protecting investors. But an account of why a regulation emerged is persuasive, I would argue, only if it can show that lawmakers' own records connect the rule to the crisis; a rule that merely follows a crash in time, without such documented links, may have been driven by older concerns that the crash simply made convenient to cite.

Text 2
In 1844 and 1845, speculators poured money into hundreds of proposed railway companies, many of which never laid a mile of track. When share prices fell sharply in 1847, thousands of small investors were ruined. Within a few years, Parliament had tightened requirements for company accounts and audits. The sequence makes clear that the mania's collapse was what produced Britain's early investor protection laws.
problem.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 1 most likely evaluate the conclusion presented in Text 2?
options: As well supported, since Text 2 shows that the losses suffered by thousands of small investors were severe enough to demand a legislative remedy
As partly supported, since the short interval between the 1847 price collapse and the new accounting requirements counts as some evidence of a documented link
As insufficiently supported, since Text 2 relies on the order of events without citing any evidence of what motivated the lawmakers who passed the rules
As doubtful, since financial regulations are usually written long before a crisis occurs and are rarely changed quickly in response to one
problem.explanation:
Text 1의 저자는 규제가 생겨난 이유에 대한 설명이 설득력을 가지려면 입법자들의 기록이 규제를 위기와 연결해 보여야 한다는 기준을 제시한다. 시간상 뒤따랐다는 것만으로는 부족하다는 것이다. Text 2는 "The sequence makes clear"라고 하며 사건의 순서에만 기대어 결론을 내리므로, Text 1의 기준에서는 근거가 부족하다(C).
A: Text 2 자신의 기준(피해가 컸다는 점)으로 평가한 것이다. 피해 규모는 입법 동기를 기록으로 증명하지 못한다.
B: 두 저자의 기준을 섞은 것이다. 시간 간격이 짧다는 점을 기록상 연결의 일부로 쳐주지만, Text 1은 시간상 선후 관계를 기록 증거로 명시적으로 인정하지 않는다.
D: 지문과 관계없는 일반 통념이다. Text 1은 규제가 위기에 반응해 생길 수 있음을 부정하지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn:
Text 1's author sets a standard: an explanation of why a regulation emerged is persuasive only if the lawmakers' own records tie the rule to the crisis. A rule that simply comes after a crash doesn't meet that standard. Text 2 bases its conclusion on sequence alone ("The sequence makes clear"), so by Text 1's standard it is insufficiently supported. That makes C correct.
A judges the conclusion by Text 2's own reasoning, that the losses were severe. But severe losses don't show what actually motivated the lawmakers.
B mixes the two authors' standards. It counts the short time gap as partial evidence of a documented link, but Text 1 explicitly rejects timing as a substitute for records.
D relies on a general assumption that isn't in the texts. Text 1 never says regulations can't respond quickly to crises.

hardJudge.note: Text 1 기준(입법자 기록으로 규제-위기 연결 증명 필요)이 명시되어 있고, Text 2는 "The sequence makes clear"로 순서에만 의존하므로 C가 유일하게 Text 1 관점에서 도출된다. A는 Text 2 저자의 기준(피해 규모)으로 평가한 결과, B는 시간 간격을 '기록상 연결'로 쳐주는 혼합 관점(Text 1은 이를 명시적으로 배제), D는 지문 밖 일반화이며 Text 1의 입장을 과장한 것. 해설은 정답과 수치·논리적으로 일치하며 모순 없음. 1840년대 철도 마니아, 1847년 폭락, 이후 회계·감사 요건 강화는 역사적 사실과 부합. 형식·저작권 문제 없음. 난이도는 관점 유지와 선택지 강도 구별에서 오며 단순 복잡성이 아님.

advisory.note: Text 1의 기준(입법 기록상의 연결)이 명시되어 있고, Text 2는 순서에만 의존하므로 C가 맞음. B는 '부분 지지'라는 강도 함정으로 두 관점을 혼합함. 다만 기준이 Text 1에 거의 직접 진술되어 있어 hard 난도로는 경계선 수준.

problem.passage:
Text 1
Historians who defend the German cartels of the early twentieth century, such as the Rhenish-Westphalian Coal Syndicate, argue that these price-fixing agreements stabilized industries prone to ruinous swings. By setting common prices and production quotas, the defenders claim, coal and steel firms avoided destructive price wars during downturns and could therefore keep workers employed and plan long-term investments in new equipment.

Text 2
A newer line of research examines what cartel members actually did rather than what their agreements said. Records from the chemical and steel industries show that firms routinely exceeded their quotas and offered secret discounts whenever demand fell, precisely the moments when holding the line mattered most. Agreements were renegotiated or collapsed again and again, and prices in cartelized sectors fluctuated nearly as much as in sectors without cartels.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the defenders' claim described in Text 1?
problem.stimulus:
Text 1
Historians who defend the German cartels of the early twentieth century, such as the Rhenish-Westphalian Coal Syndicate, argue that these price-fixing agreements stabilized industries prone to ruinous swings. By setting common prices and production quotas, the defenders claim, coal and steel firms avoided destructive price wars during downturns and could therefore keep workers employed and plan long-term investments in new equipment.

Text 2
A newer line of research examines what cartel members actually did rather than what their agreements said. Records from the chemical and steel industries show that firms routinely exceeded their quotas and offered secret discounts whenever demand fell, precisely the moments when holding the line mattered most. Agreements were renegotiated or collapsed again and again, and prices in cartelized sectors fluctuated nearly as much as in sectors without cartels.
problem.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the defenders' claim described in Text 1?
options: By agreeing that common prices and production quotas let coal and steel firms avoid price wars and plan investments in new equipment
By pointing out that cartel agreements were renegotiated or collapsed many times over the period
By arguing that any stability the cartels produced came at the expense of consumers, who paid higher prices
By questioning whether the stability the defenders credit to cartels existed, since members abandoned the agreements in exactly the conditions where they were meant to work
problem.explanation:
정답 D: Text 2의 전제는 회원사들이 수요가 줄 때(협정이 가장 중요한 순간) 할당량을 넘기고 몰래 할인했으며 가격 변동도 비카르텔 부문과 비슷했다는 것이다. 여기서 Text 1의 핵심 주장, 즉 카르텔이 불황기에 안정을 가져왔다는 주장 자체가 사실인지 의문을 제기하는 반응이 도출된다.
A: Text 1의 내용을 그대로 반복할 뿐이다. Text 2의 증거와 정면으로 충돌한다.
B: Text 2에 나오는 사실을 되풀이할 뿐, 그 사실이 Text 1의 안정화 주장에 어떤 의미를 갖는지는 말하지 않는다. 부분적으로만 맞는 답이다.
C: 소비자 피해나 높은 가격은 Text 2가 전혀 다루지 않는 쟁점이다. 게다가 이 선택지는 안정이 실제로 있었다고 인정하는 셈인데, Text 2는 바로 그 점을 의심한다.
problem.explanationEn:
D is correct. Text 2 shows that cartel members exceeded their quotas and gave secret discounts whenever demand fell, which is exactly when the agreements were supposed to matter most. It also shows that prices in cartelized sectors swung almost as much as prices elsewhere. From these points, the author would doubt that the stability Text 1's defenders describe ever really happened.
A is wrong because it just repeats Text 1's claim, and Text 2's evidence contradicts that claim.
B is wrong because it only restates a detail from Text 2. It doesn't say how that detail answers the defenders' claim about stability.
C is wrong because consumer harm is never discussed in Text 2. This option also accepts that the cartels created stability, and that is the very point Text 2 calls into question.

hardJudge.note: D는 Text 2의 증거(수요 하락 시 할당량 초과·비밀 할인, 비카르텔 부문과 유사한 가격 변동)에서 Text 1의 '불황기 안정화' 주장 자체를 의심하는 반응으로 정확히 도출된다. A는 Text 1 반복, C는 소비자 가격이라는 외부 쟁점 도입, B는 Text 2의 사실을 되풀이하지만 Text 1 주장에 대한 함의를 담지 않아 D보다 약한 답. 단, B도 Text 2에서 사실로 뒷받침되는 '반응'으로 읽힐 여지가 있어 D와의 변별이 '가장 완전한 답' 수준에 의존한다는 점은 유의(허용 범위 내). Text 2는 Text 1을 직접 언급하지 않고, 정답 도출에 두 텍스트 종합이 필요하며, 선택지 강도 구분(B vs D)을 요구하므로 hard 적합.

advisory.note: 정답 D는 맞다. 다만 이 문항은 전형적인 medium 수준이다. Text 2는 '수요 감소 시 협정 이탈'과 '비카르텔 부문과 비슷한 가격 변동'을 명시해 안정화 주장에 사실상 직접 반박한다. 그래서 반응을 따로 추론할 여지가 적다. A(Text 1 반복)와 C(외부 쟁점·안정 전제)는 쉽게 걸러진다. B는 Text 2의 사실을 그대로 옮긴 것이다. 그 사실이 Text 1의 안정화 주장을 약화하는 근거로 읽힐 수 있어 반쯤 그럴듯한 응답이지만, D가 더 완전하므로 정답 다툼까지는 아니다. 강도를 미묘하게 따지거나 관점을 유지한 채 평가해야 하는 요소가 없어 hard 특성은 충족하지 못한다.

problem.passage:
After Rhodesia's 1965 unilateral declaration of independence, the United Nations imposed sanctions meant to cripple the colony's economy, and tobacco, its leading export, was a prime target. Some economists later argued that the sanctions failed broadly, since Rhodesia's overall output kept growing into the early 1970s as manufacturers replaced lost imports with local goods. Historian Mira Castellanos offers a narrower assessment. Examining marketing board records, she found that tobacco growers, unlike manufacturers, could not substitute domestic buyers for foreign ones: the crop had to be sold abroad, typically through intermediaries routing it via South Africa and Mozambique at steep discounts. __Castellanos documents that, during the sanctions period, the average price Rhodesian growers received per kilogram fell by nearly half, even in years when total economic output rose.__ She concludes that the sanctions did not cripple Rhodesia's economy as a whole but did severely damage sectors whose supply chains depended on foreign buyers.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
problem.stimulus: After Rhodesia's 1965 unilateral declaration of independence, the United Nations imposed sanctions meant to cripple the colony's economy, and tobacco, its leading export, was a prime target. Some economists later argued that the sanctions failed broadly, since Rhodesia's overall output kept growing into the early 1970s as manufacturers replaced lost imports with local goods. Historian Mira Castellanos offers a narrower assessment. Examining marketing board records, she found that tobacco growers, unlike manufacturers, could not substitute domestic buyers for foreign ones: the crop had to be sold abroad, typically through intermediaries routing it via South Africa and Mozambique at steep discounts. __Castellanos documents that, during the sanctions period, the average price Rhodesian growers received per kilogram fell by nearly half, even in years when total economic output rose.__ She concludes that the sanctions did not cripple Rhodesia's economy as a whole but did severely damage sectors whose supply chains depended on foreign buyers.
problem.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It provides evidence that sanctions severely weakened the Rhodesian economy as a whole, contradicting the economists who claimed the sanctions failed.
It provides evidence that sanctions inflicted serious harm on an export sector reliant on foreign buyers even while the broader economy expanded.
It provides evidence that tobacco growers suffered price losses, without bearing on how other sectors or the overall economy fared under sanctions.
It provides evidence that the rise in Rhodesia's total output caused the decline in the prices tobacco growers received for their crop.
problem.explanation: 정답 B: 밑줄 문장은 담배 가격이 거의 절반으로 떨어졌다는 사실과, 그 시기에도 전체 생산은 증가했다는 사실을 함께 제시한다. 이는 '경제 전체는 무너지지 않았지만 해외 구매자에 의존하는 부문은 큰 타격을 입었다'는 Castellanos의 결론과 범위가 정확히 일치한다. A: 근거가 경제 전체의 약화까지 입증한다고 과장했다. 밑줄 문장은 오히려 전체 생산이 증가했다고 밝힌다. C: 가격 하락 부분만 반영하고 '전체 생산이 증가한 해에도'라는 비교 정보를 빠뜨려 너무 좁게 해석했다. 이 비교가 바로 부문별 피해와 경제 전체의 성과를 구분하는 근거다. D: 인과 관계를 잘못 설정했다. 지문에서 가격 하락의 원인은 제재와 할인된 우회 판매이며, 생산 증가는 원인이 아니라 대조되는 배경일 뿐이다.
problem.explanationEn: B is correct. The underlined sentence pairs two facts: growers' prices fell by nearly half, and this happened even while total output rose. Together, these facts support exactly what Castellanos concludes: sanctions didn't cripple the whole economy, but they badly hurt sectors that depended on foreign buyers. A goes too far. The sentence actually says overall output rose, so it can't show that the whole economy was weakened. C reads the sentence too narrowly. It ignores the comparison with rising total output, and that comparison is what separates the damage to one sector from how the economy performed overall. D gets the cause wrong. The text blames the price drop on sanctions and discounted resale through intermediaries. Rising output is presented as a contrast, not as the cause.

hardJudge.note: 밑줄 문장은 '가격 절반 하락'과 '전체 생산 증가'를 동시에 제시해 Castellanos의 부문별·제한적 결론을 정확히 뒷받침하며, B가 그 범위와 일치한다. A는 경제 전체 약화로 과장, C는 비교 정보를 제거한 좁은 해석, D는 생산 증가→가격 하락이라는 잘못된 인과를 설정한 오답으로 체크리스트 전 항목 충족. 경제학자들의 '광범위한 실패' 주장과 역사학자의 '좁은 평가'를 대비해 근거의 논리적 역할을 식별해야 하므로 medium을 넘는 사고를 요구한다. 역사적 배경(1965 UDI, UN 제재, 담배 주요 수출, 수입대체 성장, 남아공·모잠비크 우회 판매)도 사실과 부합한다. Castellanos는 가상 인물로 보이며 문제 없음.

advisory.note: B만 근거(가격 반토막과 총생산 증가의 대비)와 '부문별 피해, 경제 전체는 아님'이라는 결론의 범위가 맞는다. A는 과장, C는 범위를 좁힌 해석, D는 인과를 뒤집은 선택지다. 경제학자의 주장, 반론, 근거, 결론을 연결해야 풀 수 있다. 실제 역사적 사실과 어긋날 수 있지만 '역사가'의 기록으로 제시되어 문제없다.

problem.passage:
Historians often trace the Dutch Republic's seventeenth-century commercial dominance to its spice voyages, but economic historian Jan de Vries points to a humbler source: herring. Dutch fleets cured their catch with salt at sea, so the fish stayed edible for months and could be sold across Europe. The steady profits from this trade did not merely supplement merchants' incomes; they ______ the later ventures, supplying the capital that paid for ships, warehouses, and the long-distance expeditions often credited with creating the Golden Age.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.stimulus: Historians often trace the Dutch Republic's seventeenth-century commercial dominance to its spice voyages, but economic historian Jan de Vries points to a humbler source: herring. Dutch fleets cured their catch with salt at sea, so the fish stayed edible for months and could be sold across Europe. The steady profits from this trade did not merely supplement merchants' incomes; they ______ the later ventures, supplying the capital that paid for ships, warehouses, and the long-distance expeditions often credited with creating the Golden Age.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: overshadowed
resembled
underwrote
postponed
problem.explanation: 지문은 청어 무역의 이윤이 단순한 부수입이 아니라 선박과 창고, 원거리 원정에 쓸 자본을 '공급했다'고 말하므로, 재정적으로 뒷받침했다는 뜻의 C(underwrote)가 정답이다. A(overshadowed)는 청어가 향신료 무역보다 과소평가되었다는 지문의 대비 구도와 얼핏 맞아 보이지만, 무엇이 무엇을 가렸는지가 아니라 자금 공급 관계를 설명하는 문맥과 맞지 않는다. B(resembled)는 두 사업이 모두 무역이라는 점에서 그럴듯하지만, 'supplying the capital'이 나타내는 인과·자금 관계를 담지 못한다. D(postponed)는 '나중의(later)' 사업이라는 시간 표현에 끌린 오답으로, 이윤이 사업을 가능하게 했다는 내용과 정반대다.
problem.explanationEn: The text says the herring profits were more than extra income: they supplied the capital for ships, warehouses, and expeditions. That means they financially backed the later ventures, so C (underwrote) is correct. A (overshadowed) might seem to fit because the passage contrasts herring with the spice voyages, but the blank describes a funding relationship, not one trade outshining the other. B (resembled) sounds reasonable since both were commercial activities, but it leaves out the cause-and-effect link that "supplying the capital" sets up. D (postponed) is tempting because of the word "later," but it says the opposite of what the text means, since the profits made those ventures possible.

quality.seed: economics and business — Dutch herring fisheries and herrings salt trade profitability funding Golden Age merchant expansion capital

hardJudge.note: "did not merely supplement...; they ___ the later ventures, supplying the capital" 구조에서 underwrote가 유일하게 자금 제공 관계를 담음. A는 지문의 대비 구도(향신료 vs 청어)에, D는 'later'에 끌리는 부분적 근거가 있고 B도 말이 됨. 세미콜론 대비 + 분사구 확인의 두 단계 판단 필요하여 medium 적합. Jan de Vries의 네덜란드 경제사 연구 및 청어 무역의 역할은 역사학적으로 통용되는 내용. 해설 한/영 일치, 글자 참조 정확.

advisory.note: 'supplying the capital'이 정답 단서로 명확하다. underwrote는 어휘 수준이 있고 overshadowed는 대비 구도 때문에 그럴듯한 함정이라 medium에 적합하다. 다만 B와 D는 비교적 쉽게 배제된다. de Vries의 청어 논지는 대체로 사실에 부합한다.

problem.passage:
For centuries, Antwerp's diamond cutters passed their techniques from master to apprentice within tightly organized guilds, and much of that knowledge was never written down. Economic historians argue that this tacit expertise helped the city ______ its lead in gemstone processing: even when rival centers gained access to the same rough stones and similar tools, they struggled to match the precision of Antwerp's polished diamonds, because the skills themselves could not easily be copied or exported.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.stimulus: For centuries, Antwerp's diamond cutters passed their techniques from master to apprentice within tightly organized guilds, and much of that knowledge was never written down. Economic historians argue that this tacit expertise helped the city ______ its lead in gemstone processing: even when rival centers gained access to the same rough stones and similar tools, they struggled to match the precision of Antwerp's polished diamonds, because the skills themselves could not easily be copied or exported.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: establish
advertise
surrender
sustain
problem.explanation: 지문은 경쟁 도시들이 같은 원석과 도구를 얻은 '뒤에도' 안트베르펜의 정밀함을 따라잡지 못했다고 하므로, 이미 가진 우위를 계속 '유지하다'는 뜻의 D(sustain)가 정답이다. A(establish)는 우위와 관련은 있지만 처음 '확립'하는 것을 뜻하고, 지문은 경쟁이 생긴 뒤의 지속을 강조한다. B(advertise)는 명성과 관련된 듯 보이지만 지문은 홍보가 아니라 모방하기 어려운 기술 이야기다. C(surrender)는 우위를 '포기하다'라는 뜻이라 지문 논리와 정반대다.
problem.explanationEn: The text says rival centers still couldn't match Antwerp's precision even after they got the same stones and tools, so the tacit skills helped the city keep a lead it already had. That makes D ("sustain") the answer. A ("establish") is about advantage too, but it means creating the lead in the first place, while the text is about the lead lasting once competition showed up. B ("advertise") might seem to fit because of reputation, but the passage is about skills that are hard to copy, not about promotion. C ("surrender") means giving up the lead, which is the opposite of what the passage describes.

quality.seed: economics and business — Antwerp diamond cutting cluster and guild apprenticeship preserving gemstone processing techniques competitive advantage

hardJudge.note: 검산: "its lead"(이미 보유한 우위) + "even when rival centers gained access... they struggled to match"(경쟁 발생 후에도 우위 지속) → '유지하다' sustain(D)이 유일하게 정확. A(establish)는 우위 관련이라 부분적으로 그럴듯하지만 '처음 확립'은 지문 흐름(경쟁 이후의 지속)과 맞지 않음; B(advertise)는 명성 맥락으로 유혹적이나 지문은 홍보가 아닌 복제 불가능한 기술을 다룸; C(surrender)는 정반대. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 D 결론과 선택지 글자 참조 일치, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 안트베르펜 다이아몬드 길드 역사 서술에 사실 오류 없음. 두 단계 판단(어휘 의미 + 'even when' 맥락 확인) 필요, 오답 2개가 부분적 근거를 가져 medium 적합.

advisory.note: 'its lead'와 'even when rivals gained access'를 함께 읽으면 이미 가진 우위의 지속을 말한다는 것이 분명하다. 그래서 establish가 그럴듯한 오답이 된다. advertise는 약한 오답이고 surrender는 반대말이다. 오답 중 강하게 경쟁하는 것은 하나뿐이지만 medium 범위 안이다.

problem.passage:
In rural Finland, many small landowners pool their forests through cooperatives that jointly own pulp mills. Instead of sending timber profits to distant investors, the network of cooperatives ______ earnings back to member families, helping to support schools and shops in remote villages.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: In rural Finland, many small landowners pool their forests through cooperatives that jointly own pulp mills. Instead of sending timber profits to distant investors, the network of cooperatives ______ earnings back to member families, helping to support schools and shops in remote villages.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: returns
return
are returning
have returned
problem.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 "network"이고, "of cooperatives"는 주어를 꾸미는 수식어일 뿐이다. 따라서 동사도 단수형이어야 하므로 A "returns"가 정답이다. B "return", C "are returning", D "have returned"는 모두 복수 동사형이어서, 바로 앞의 복수 명사 "cooperatives"에 동사를 잘못 맞춘 것이다.
problem.explanationEn: The subject of this sentence is the singular noun "network." The phrase "of cooperatives" only describes it. A singular subject needs a singular verb, so choice A, "returns," is correct. Choices B ("return"), C ("are returning"), and D ("have returned") are all plural verb forms. They wrongly agree with the nearby plural noun "cooperatives" instead of the real subject.

quality.seed: economics and business — Finnish forestry cooperatives and pulp mill collective ownership distributing timber industry profits to rural communities

hardJudge.note: 주어 "network"(단수) + 수식어 "of cooperatives" 구조의 전형적 주어-동사 수 일치 문항. 정답 A "returns" 검산 완료. 오답 3개 모두 인접 복수 명사 "cooperatives"에 끌린 복수형으로 그럴듯한 오개념 선택지임. 한·영 해설 결론·글자 참조 일치, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 핀란드 산림 협동조합 서술은 일반적 사실과 모순 없음. 단일 규칙·한 단계 추론으로 easy에 적합.

advisory.note: 주어 "network"와 동사의 수 일치를 묻는 단일 규칙 문항이며, 수식어 "of cooperatives"가 끼어 있어 헷갈리게 만든다. 오답 3개는 모두 복수형이라 규칙을 알면 바로 배제되므로 easy 난이도에 맞다. "have returned"도 복수형이라 단수 주어와 맞지 않아 오답임이 분명하다.

problem.passage:
In eighteenth-century Ulster, much Irish linen was made under the putting-out system. Merchant middlemen delivered flax yarn to rural households and later returned to collect the finished cloth. The weavers in each cottage ______ paid by the piece, usually at rates the merchants alone decided, which left many families deeply dependent on these intermediaries.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: In eighteenth-century Ulster, much Irish linen was made under the putting-out system. Merchant middlemen delivered flax yarn to rural households and later returned to collect the finished cloth. The weavers in each cottage ______ paid by the piece, usually at rates the merchants alone decided, which left many families deeply dependent on these intermediaries.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: was
were
is
has been
problem.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 복수 명사 "weavers"이며, "in each cottage"는 주어를 꾸미는 전치사구일 뿐이다. 따라서 복수 동사가 필요하고, 과거 일을 서술하는 글이므로 B "were"가 정답이다. A, C, D는 모두 단수 동사여서 바로 앞의 단수 명사 "cottage"에 잘못 맞춘 것이다. 게다가 C와 D는 과거 사건을 서술하는 지문의 시제와도 맞지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The subject of this sentence is the plural noun "weavers." The phrase "in each cottage" is just a prepositional phrase describing that subject. That means the verb has to be plural, and since the passage describes the past, choice B, "were," is correct. Choices A, C, and D are all singular verbs, so each one wrongly agrees with the nearby singular noun "cottage." C and D also break the past-tense pattern of the passage.

quality.seed: economics and business — Irish linen manufacturing and putting-out system exploitation of rural domestic weavers through merchant middlemen

hardJudge.note: 주어 "weavers"(복수) + 과거 시제 문맥 → "were"가 유일한 정답. 오답 셋은 모두 단수형으로, 인접 명사 "cottage"에 끌리는 전형적 오개념을 반영하며, C·D는 시제 불일치까지 겹침. 한·영 해설 결론·글자 참조 일치, 영어 해설 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 18세기 얼스터 리넨 putting-out 시스템 서술은 사실에 부합. 단일 규칙(개입 전치사구가 있는 주어-동사 일치)으로 풀리는 easy 적합 문항.

advisory.note: 주어-동사 수 일치 하나만 알면 풀리는 문항이다. 바로 앞의 단수 명사 cottage가 그럴듯한 함정 역할을 하고, 오답 셋 모두 단수형이라 규칙을 알면 바로 배제된다. 엄밀히 따지면 이 빈칸은 시제가 아니라 수 일치만 묻는다. 하지만 B 하나만 복수형이라 답이 유일하게 정해지므로 문제없다.

problem.passage:
When the impeller of a hydraulic pump spins fast enough, local pressure in the surrounding water can drop below the liquid's vapor pressure, and tiny vapor bubbles form. The violent collapse of these bubbles against nearby metal surfaces, repeated millions of times as the fluid circulates through valves and pipes, ______ microjets and pressure waves strong enough to pit even hardened steel over time.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: When the impeller of a hydraulic pump spins fast enough, local pressure in the surrounding water can drop below the liquid's vapor pressure, and tiny vapor bubbles form. The violent collapse of these bubbles against nearby metal surfaces, repeated millions of times as the fluid circulates through valves and pipes, ______ microjets and pressure waves strong enough to pit even hardened steel over time.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: generate
generates
generating
having generated
problem.explanation: 두 번째 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 "The violent collapse"이고, "of these bubbles ... pipes"는 주어와 동사 사이에 끼어든 수식어구이다. 이 문장에는 다른 정동사가 없으므로 빈칸에는 단수 주어와 일치하는 정동사가 와야 하며, 따라서 B "generates"가 정답이다. A는 정동사이긴 하지만 바로 앞의 복수 명사 bubbles, surfaces, times에 맞춘 복수형이어서 단수 주어와 일치하지 않는다. C와 D는 분사 형태라 정동사 역할을 하지 못하므로 문장에 본동사가 없는 불완전한 문장이 된다.
problem.explanationEn: The subject of the second sentence is the singular noun "The violent collapse," and the phrase "of these bubbles ... pipes" is a modifier that sits between the subject and its verb. The sentence has no other main verb, so the blank needs a finite verb that agrees with a singular subject. That makes B, "generates," the correct answer. A is a finite verb, but it is plural, matching the nearby plural nouns bubbles, surfaces, and times instead of the actual subject. C and D are participle forms that can't act as a main verb, so either one would leave the sentence without a main verb and make it incomplete.

quality.seed: physical science — Cavitation erosion damage in hydraulic systems and bubble collapse pressure wave mechanisms analysis

hardJudge.note: 주어 "The violent collapse"(단수)와 동사 사이에 전치사구와 분사구("repeated ... pipes")가 길게 끼어 있어 근접 복수 명사(bubbles, surfaces, times, pipes)에 이끌릴 수 있는 설계. 문장에 다른 정동사가 없으므로 단수 정동사 "generates"(B)가 유일하게 옳다. A는 근접 명사 유인 오답, C는 앞선 "repeated" 분사 패턴과 맞물려 그럴듯하며, D도 분사형으로 말이 된다. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 정답과 글자 참조가 일치하고 문법적 설명이 정확함. 캐비테이션 관련 과학 서술도 사실에 부합. 형식 문제 없음.

advisory.note: 단수 주어와 동사 사이에 긴 수식어구와 복수 명사(bubbles, surfaces, valves, pipes)가 끼어 있어 A를 고르게 만드는 함정이 있다. C와 D는 비정동사이다. 표준적인 medium 수준이다. 해설에서 꼽은 복수 명사 목록에 빈칸 바로 앞의 pipes가 빠졌지만 사소한 점이다.

problem.passage:
Superabsorbent polymers, the cross-linked polyacrylate networks found in diapers and agricultural soil additives, can absorb hundreds of times their own mass in pure water. The density of cross-links strongly governs this capacity. A lightly cross-linked hydrogel, whose chains can stretch far apart as water rushes ______ swells to a larger final volume but reaches equilibrium more slowly than a densely cross-linked one.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: Superabsorbent polymers, the cross-linked polyacrylate networks found in diapers and agricultural soil additives, can absorb hundreds of times their own mass in pure water. The density of cross-links strongly governs this capacity. A lightly cross-linked hydrogel, whose chains can stretch far apart as water rushes ______ swells to a larger final volume but reaches equilibrium more slowly than a densely cross-linked one.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: in,
in;
in
in, and
problem.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 "A lightly cross-linked hydrogel"이고 동사는 "swells"이다. 그 사이에 "whose"로 시작하는 비제한 관계절이 들어가 있으며, 앞쪽에 쉼표가 있으므로 뒤쪽에도 쉼표가 있어야 관계절이 닫힌다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 세미콜론을 쓰는데, 세미콜론 앞부분이 독립절이 아니고 뒷부분에도 주어가 없으므로 틀렸다. C는 닫는 쉼표가 없어 삽입구가 끝나지 않으며, "rushes in swells"가 하나로 이어진 것처럼 읽힌다. D는 "and"를 붙여 "swells"를 관계절 안의 두 번째 동사로 만들기 때문에 주어 "hydrogel"에 맞는 본동사가 없어진다.
problem.explanationEn: The subject of this sentence is "A lightly cross-linked hydrogel," and its verb is "swells." Between them sits a nonrestrictive clause that begins with "whose." That clause opens with a comma, so it also needs a comma to close it, which makes A correct. B uses a semicolon, but the words before it aren't an independent clause, and the words after it have no subject. C leaves out the closing comma, so the inserted clause never ends and "rushes in swells" runs together. D adds "and," which turns "swells" into a second verb inside the relative clause, so the subject "hydrogel" is left with no main verb.

quality.seed: physical science — Superabsorbent polymer water absorption capacity and cross-linked polyacrylate hydrogel swelling kinetics

hardJudge.note: 주어 "hydrogel"과 동사 "swells" 사이의 비제한 관계절("whose ... rushes in")을 쉼표 쌍으로 닫아야 하므로 A가 유일한 정답. B는 세미콜론 앞이 비독립절, C는 닫는 쉼표 누락, D는 "and"로 본동사를 관계절 안으로 끌어들여 주절 동사 상실. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 동일한 결론과 선택지 참조를 가지며 오류 없음. 과학적 배경(고흡수성 고분자, 가교 밀도와 팽윤 용량·속도 관계)도 타당. 긴 삽입절 뒤 쉼표 판단 + 동사 구조 확인이라는 두 단계 판단이 필요하고 C·D가 그럴듯한 오답이므로 medium 적합.

advisory.note: 비제한 관계절을 닫는 쉼표를 묻는 표준 문항이다. 문장 안에 'rushes in'과 'stretch far apart' 같은 방해 요소가 있어 중간 난이도에 맞다. D의 'and'는 관계절 안의 등위 구조로 읽혀 그럴듯한 오답이 된다.

problem.passage:
Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) are porous crystals built from metal ions linked by organic molecules, and their internal channels can be tuned to favor one gas over another. In a framework known as Mg-MOF-74, the magnesium sites that line each hexagonal ______ these open metal sites bind carbon dioxide far more strongly than they bind nitrogen, allowing the material to pull CO₂ selectively from a simulated flue gas stream.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) are porous crystals built from metal ions linked by organic molecules, and their internal channels can be tuned to favor one gas over another. In a framework known as Mg-MOF-74, the magnesium sites that line each hexagonal ______ these open metal sites bind carbon dioxide far more strongly than they bind nitrogen, allowing the material to pull CO₂ selectively from a simulated flue gas stream.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: channel are left partially uncovered,
channel are left partially uncovered;
channel, are left partially uncovered;
channel are left partially uncovered, and,
problem.explanation: 빈칸 앞의 'the magnesium sites that line each hexagonal channel are left partially uncovered'는 완전한 독립절이고, 뒤의 'these open metal sites bind...'도 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이므로 두 절은 세미콜론으로 연결해야 한다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A는 두 독립절을 쉼표만으로 이어 쉼표 오류(comma splice)가 된다. C는 세미콜론은 맞지만 필수 관계절 'that line each hexagonal channel'과 동사 'are' 사이에 불필요한 쉼표를 넣어 주어와 동사를 갈라놓는다. D는 'and' 뒤에 쉼표를 넣어 등위접속사와 다음 절 사이를 부적절하게 끊는다.
problem.explanationEn: The words before the blank, "the magnesium sites that line each hexagonal channel are left partially uncovered," form a complete independent clause. The words after it, "these open metal sites bind...," form another complete independent clause, so a semicolon is the right way to join them. That makes B correct. A joins two independent clauses with only a comma, which is a comma splice. C uses the correct semicolon, but it adds an extra comma between the essential relative clause "that line each hexagonal channel" and the verb "are," which splits the subject from its verb. D puts a comma right after "and," which wrongly separates the conjunction from the clause it introduces.

quality.seed: physical science — Metal-organic framework gas separation selectivity and porous crystal structure for carbon dioxide capture

hardJudge.note: 빈칸 앞 'the magnesium sites that line each hexagonal channel are left partially uncovered'와 뒤 'these open metal sites bind...' 모두 독립절이므로 세미콜론(B)이 유일하게 옳음. A는 comma splice, C는 주어-동사 사이 불필요 쉼표, D는 'and' 뒤 부적절 쉼표로 각각 배제됨. Mg-MOF-74의 육각 채널·개방 금속 자리·CO₂/N₂ 선택성 서술은 사실과 부합. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 정답 및 선택지 참조가 일치하고 영어 해설에 한글 없음. 긴 관계절 'that line each hexagonal channel'로 주어-동사 경계를 가려 두 단계 판단(절 경계 식별 + 구두점 규칙)이 필요하며, C(세미콜론은 맞음)·D(접속사 사용)는 부분적 근거를 가져 medium에 적합.

problem.explanationEn: The part before the blank, "Spark plasma sintering ... concentrates heat at the contact points between grains," is one independent clause, even though a long appositive sits inside it. The part after the blank, "the material can reach...," is also an independent clause. You need a semicolon to join two independent clauses, and the conjunctive adverb "as a result" takes a comma after it, so C is correct. A and B join the two clauses with only a comma, which makes a comma splice. B puts commas on both sides of "as a result" so it looks like an aside, but a conjunctive adverb can't join two clauses with just a comma. D has no punctuation between the clauses, so it creates a run-on sentence.

problem.passage:
When a glow-in-the-dark material absorbs light, some of its excited electrons end up in what physicists call a triplet state. Returning from this state to the ground state by emitting light is "spin-forbidden," meaning the transition can happen only rarely, so the stored energy leaks out slowly as a faint glow that can last for seconds or even hours. For decades, chemists assumed that making this glow last longer simply required finding molecules whose triplet states were even more strongly forbidden from emitting. In practice, however, the longest-lasting commercial phosphors, such as strontium aluminate doped with europium and dysprosium, owe little to that strategy. In these materials, the dysprosium ions create defects that trap excited electrons before they reach any emitting state at all. Heat at room temperature then releases the trapped electrons a few at a time, and only after release do they reach the europium ions and give off light. The afterglow's duration is therefore set mainly by how deep the traps are, not by how slowly any single emitting state decays.

problem.passage:
Engineers once assumed that carbon-fiber laminates fail mainly when the fibers themselves snap under tension. Because the fibers are far stronger than the epoxy matrix that binds them, designers concentrated on fiber strength and orientation. Yet materials scientist Hana Okafor and her colleagues found that, in laminates containing a drilled bolt hole, failure often began elsewhere. Using acoustic sensors and X-ray imaging during tensile tests, the team observed that stress concentrated at the edges of the hole and caused thin cracks to open along the boundary where fibers meet the matrix. These cracks spread between layers, separating them, well before any significant number of fibers broke. Once the layers had separated, the fibers no longer shared the load evenly, and the laminate failed at a stress about 30 percent below what fiber strength alone predicted. Okafor's group therefore argues that improving the bond at the fiber-matrix interface may do more to strengthen such parts than using stronger fibers would.

problem.passage:
When a strip of a viscoelastic polymer such as polyisobutylene is stretched to a fixed length and held there, the force needed to keep it stretched does not stay constant. Instead, the internal stress falls steadily over time, a phenomenon known as stress relaxation. Engineers once treated this decline as a minor nuisance to be corrected for in measurements, but materials scientist Hana Okafor argues that it is better understood as a direct record of molecular motion. In her view, the long, tangled chains that make up the polymer gradually slide past one another and untangle while the strip is held, so the stress that the chains initially bore is released bit by bit.

To test this idea, Okafor's team performed relaxation tests on the same polymer at several temperatures. If chain rearrangement drives the decline, warmer samples, whose chains move more freely, should relax faster, and the curves from different temperatures should match once time is rescaled accordingly. The results fit both predictions: stress at 60°C dropped to half its starting value in roughly a tenth of the time required at 25°C, and the rescaled curves overlapped almost perfectly.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

problem.explanationEn: C is correct because the text presents Okafor's claim that stress relaxation records polymer chains gradually sliding and untangling, and then shows that the temperature tests matched her predictions. A borrows the older engineers' view of relaxation as a nuisance to correct, which the text sets up only to reject, and the warmer tests were never meant to remove an error. B correctly notes that chains move more freely when warm, but that is just a supporting detail, and the text never says warm polymers are unsuitable. D says the chains break, but the text describes them sliding past one another and untangling, not breaking.

problem.passage:
A quartz crystal microbalance (QCM) measures mass by tracking the resonant frequency of a thin quartz disk that vibrates when voltage is applied. When molecules adsorb onto the disk's surface, the added mass lowers the frequency in proportion to that mass, a relationship that lets researchers detect changes smaller than a single layer of atoms. This proportional rule, however, assumes that the adsorbed film is rigid and moves in lockstep with the vibrating crystal. Chemist Lena Hartwig used a QCM to monitor two coatings: a thin metal film and a hydrated polymer gel that holds water and deforms softly as the crystal oscillates. Both coatings produced similar frequency drops, but the gel also caused a sharp rise in energy dissipation, meaning the vibrations died out much faster. Hartwig therefore concluded that ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?

When molecules adsorb onto the disk's surface, the added mass lowers the frequency in proportion to that mass, a relationship that lets researchers detect changes smaller than a single layer of atoms. This proportional rule, however, assumes that the adsorbed film is rigid and moves in lockstep with the vibrating crystal. Chemist Lena Hartwig used a QCM to monitor two coatings: a thin metal film and a hydrated polymer gel that holds water and deforms softly as the crystal oscillates. Both coatings produced similar frequency drops, but the gel also caused a sharp rise in energy dissipation, meaning the vibrations died out much faster. Hartwig therefore concluded that ______
problem.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: the gel and the metal film must have added nearly identical masses to the crystal, since their frequency drops were similar.
the gel's frequency drop must reflect less mass than the metal film's, since soft coatings always lower frequency more than rigid ones do.
the metal film's frequency drop cannot be used to estimate its mass, since the film increased energy dissipation as much as the gel did.
the gel's frequency drop cannot be converted to mass with the standard proportional rule, since the gel does not move rigidly with the crystal.
problem.explanation: 지문은 진동수 감소와 질량이 비례한다는 규칙이 막이 단단해 결정과 함께 움직일 때만 성립한다고 말하고, 젤은 부드럽게 변형되며 에너지 소산이 컸다고 한다. 이 두 정보를 연결하면 젤의 진동수 감소에는 표준 규칙을 적용할 수 없으므로 D가 정답이다. A는 비례 규칙을 그대로 적용했는데, 젤에는 그 규칙의 전제가 깨졌다는 점을 놓친 것이다. B는 젤의 질량이 더 적다고 단정하고 '항상'이라는 근거 없는 일반화를 쓴다. C는 소산이 크게 증가한 것은 젤뿐이었다는 지문 내용과 맞지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The text says the proportional frequency-to-mass rule works only when the film is rigid and moves along with the crystal, and it describes the gel as soft and deforming, with a sharp rise in dissipation. Put those two facts together and you can see the standard rule doesn't apply to the gel's frequency drop, so D is correct. A applies the proportional rule anyway, missing that the gel breaks the rule's basic assumption. B claims the gel added less mass and relies on an "always" generalization the text never supports. C contradicts the text, since only the gel caused the sharp rise in dissipation.

In most such crystals, warming causes the helix to wind more tightly. Materials scientist Lena Okafor tested a new formulation and found that, as she warmed a sample from 28°C to 34°C, its reflected color shifted steadily from blue toward red. Because the reflected color depends on pitch alone, Okafor concluded that in her formulation, ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
problem.stimulus: Thermochromic liquid crystals change color because their rod-shaped molecules stack in a twisted, helical arrangement. The distance over which the helix completes one full turn, called the pitch, determines which wavelength of light the crystal reflects most strongly: a longer pitch reflects longer (redder) wavelengths, and a shorter pitch reflects shorter (bluer) wavelengths. In most such crystals, warming causes the helix to wind more tightly. Materials scientist Lena Okafor tested a new formulation and found that, as she warmed a sample from 28°C to 34°C, its reflected color shifted steadily from blue toward red. Because the reflected color depends on pitch alone, Okafor concluded that in her formulation, ______
problem.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: rising temperature lengthens the helical pitch, unlike in most such crystals.
rising temperature shortens the helical pitch, just as it does in most such crystals.
rising temperature leaves the helical pitch unchanged while altering how the molecules absorb light.
rising temperature lengthens the helical pitch, just as it does in most such crystals.
problem.explanation: 지문에 따르면 피치가 길수록 더 붉은 빛을 반사하고, 색은 피치에만 의존한다. 오카포의 시료는 가열할 때 파랑에서 빨강으로 변했으므로 피치가 길어졌고, 이는 대부분의 결정이 가열 시 나선이 더 촘촘해지는(피치가 짧아지는) 것과 반대이므로 A가 정답이다. B는 일반적인 결정의 경향만 맞을 뿐 관찰된 붉은 쪽 이동과 모순된다. C는 색이 피치에만 의존한다는 전제와 어긋난다. D는 피치가 길어진다는 점은 맞지만 그것이 대부분의 결정과 같다고 잘못 말한다.
problem.explanationEn: The passage tells you that a longer pitch reflects redder light and that color depends on pitch alone. Since Okafor's sample shifted from blue to red as it warmed, its pitch must have grown longer, which is the opposite of most crystals, whose helix tightens (shortens) when warmed, so A is correct. B gets the typical behavior right but contradicts the observed shift toward red. C contradicts the premise that color depends only on pitch. D correctly says the pitch lengthens but wrongly claims this matches most such crystals.

problem.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: the modified liquid would tolerate higher voltages than the unmodified liquid, since the bulky side group shields the ions from breaking down.
the modified liquid should conduct current more effectively than the unmodified liquid without giving up the voltage stability that makes ionic liquids useful.
the modified liquid would conduct current less effectively than the unmodified liquid, since bulky cations are likely to move more slowly through the electrolyte.
the modified liquid should replace conventional solvents in all batteries, since ion pairing was the only obstacle to using ionic liquids as electrolytes.
problem.explanation: 지문은 결합된 이온쌍은 중성이라 전하를 운반하지 못한다고 설명하므로, 자유 이온 비율이 높아지면 전도성이 향상될 것으로 추론된다. 또 고전압 분해 저항은 변하지 않았다고 했으므로 B가 두 정보를 모두 연결한다. A는 전압 안정성이 '변하지 않았다'는 진술과 모순된다. C는 큰 양이온이 느리게 움직일 수 있다는 그럴듯한 추론이지만 지문은 이동 속도에 대해 아무 정보도 주지 않으며, 자유 이온 증가라는 핵심 근거를 무시한다. D는 이온쌍 형성이 유일한 장애라거나 모든 배터리에 적용된다는, 지문이 뒷받침하지 않는 과도한 일반화이다.
problem.explanationEn: The passage says bound ion pairs are neutral and carry no charge, so a higher fraction of free ions should mean better conduction. It also says high-voltage stability was unchanged, so B links both facts correctly. A contradicts the statement that decomposition resistance did not change. C sounds reasonable because bulky ions might move slowly, but the passage says nothing about ion speed, and C ignores the key evidence about free ions. D overgeneralizes: the passage never says ion pairing is the only obstacle or that the liquid suits all batteries.

problem.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: the aerogel with mostly micrometer-scale pores will insulate better, because its larger cells leave less solid graphene to carry heat.
the two aerogels will insulate about equally well, because heat moving through their solid walls should be limited to the same degree.
the aerogel with mostly sub-50-nanometer pores will insulate better, because the air inside it should carry noticeably less heat.
the aerogel with mostly sub-50-nanometer pores will insulate better, because its finer structure should make its graphene walls less dense.
problem.explanation: 두 에어로젤의 밀도가 같으므로 고체 벽을 통한 열전도는 같은 수준이고, 차이는 기체 전도에서만 생긴다. 50nm보다 작은 기공은 공기 분자의 평균 이동 거리(약 70nm)보다 좁아 기체 전도가 급격히 줄어든다. 따라서 C가 맞다. A는 밀도가 같다는 조건을 무시하고 고체량 차이를 가정한다. B는 고체 전도가 같다는 점은 맞지만 기공 크기에 따른 기체 전도 차이를 놓친다. D는 결론은 맞지만, 밀도가 같으니 벽이 덜 조밀해진다는 근거가 지문과 모순된다.
problem.explanationEn: Because the two aerogels have the same density, heat moving through their solid walls should be about the same, so any difference has to come from the gas inside. Pores smaller than 50 nanometers are narrower than air's roughly 70-nanometer mean free path, so gas conduction in that sample drops sharply. That makes C correct. A ignores that the densities are equal and assumes one sample has less solid graphene. B is right that solid conduction should match, but it misses how pore size changes gas conduction. D reaches the right conclusion for the wrong reason: since the densities are equal, the passage gives no support for the walls being less dense.

advisory.note: 밀도가 같으면 고체 전도가 같다는 점과, 50nm가 평균자유행로 70nm보다 작아 기체 전도가 준다는 점을 연결해야 하는 두 단계 추론이다. B와 D가 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가진 오답이라 medium에 적합하다. 0.16 mg/cm³급 에어로젤 밀도와 공기 평균자유행로 약 68-70nm는 사실과 맞다.

problem.passage:
In capillary electrophoresis, charged molecules are separated as an electric field pulls them through a narrow silica tube. The tube's inner wall carries negative charges that drag the surrounding fluid toward one end, a bulk movement called electroosmotic flow. Because this flow pushes fluid evenly across the whole width of the tube, bands of molecules stay sharp instead of spreading out, which is why the method can tell apart molecules whose speeds differ only slightly. But when chemist Lena Ortiz ran samples containing proteins that stick readily to silica, she found that the proteins coated parts of the wall and canceled its charge there, leaving uneven flow along the tube. Given this, Ortiz concluded that for samples with such proteins, the method's usual ability to distinguish closely related molecules ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
problem.stimulus: In capillary electrophoresis, charged molecules are separated as an electric field pulls them through a narrow silica tube. The tube's inner wall carries negative charges that drag the surrounding fluid toward one end, a bulk movement called electroosmotic flow. Because this flow pushes fluid evenly across the whole width of the tube, bands of molecules stay sharp instead of spreading out, which is why the method can tell apart molecules whose speeds differ only slightly. But when chemist Lena Ortiz ran samples containing proteins that stick readily to silica, she found that the proteins coated parts of the wall and canceled its charge there, leaving uneven flow along the tube. Given this, Ortiz concluded that for samples with such proteins, the method's usual ability to distinguish closely related molecules ______
problem.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: would get better, since proteins covering the wall would stop the molecules from losing speed through contact with the silica.
would stay the same, since the electric field pulling the charged molecules would still be at full strength along the whole tube.
would matter less, since proteins that stick to silica would all leave the tube at the same time no matter how fast they moved.
would probably be weakened, since the condition that keeps the molecule bands narrow would no longer be met.
problem.explanation: 지문에 따르면 분해능은 관 벽 전체에서 고른 전기삼투 흐름이 생겨 띠가 날카롭게 유지되는 데서 나온다. 단백질이 벽의 전하를 상쇄하면 흐름이 고르지 않게 되므로 이 조건이 깨지고, 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 벽 접촉이라는 그럴듯한 이유를 대지만, 지문은 흐름이 고르지 않게 된다고만 말한다. B는 전기장이 그대로라는 점은 맞을 수 있으나, 분해능을 좌우하는 것은 흐름의 균일성이다. C는 모든 단백질이 동시에 나온다는 근거가 지문에 없다.
problem.explanationEn: The passage says the method can resolve close molecules because electroosmotic flow is even across the tube, which keeps bands sharp. Ortiz found that sticky proteins canceled the wall's charge in some places and made the flow uneven, so that condition breaks down. That makes D the answer. A offers a plausible-sounding idea about wall contact, but the passage only says the coating makes flow uneven, not that it helps. B may be right that the field stays at full strength, but what drives resolution here is even flow. C claims the proteins all exit at the same time, and nothing in the passage supports that.

advisory.note: D는 '고른 흐름 → 날카로운 띠 → 분해능'과 '단백질 코팅 → 고르지 않은 흐름'이라는 두 정보를 이어야 고를 수 있어 medium 수준에 맞는다. 다만 경계선에 있다. C는 근거가 약해 쉽게 배제되고, D의 'probably'라는 단서도 정답을 드러낸다. 또 지문에서 고른 흐름은 '관의 폭 전체(across the whole width)'인데 단백질 문제는 흐름이 '관을 따라(along the tube)' 고르지 않다는 것이어서 표현이 약간 어긋난다. 그래도 추론 자체는 성립한다.

problem.passage:
In organic solar cells, absorbed light creates excitons—tightly bound pairs of electrons and holes—that must be split apart before any current can flow. Splitting happens at the interface between a donor material and an acceptor material, where the electron hops to the acceptor and briefly forms a "charge-transfer state" with the hole left behind. Materials chemist Lena Okafor and colleagues hypothesize that the main barrier to efficiency in many blends is not how many charge-transfer states form but whether those states break apart: when the energy offset between donor and acceptor is too small, they argue, charge-transfer states tend to recombine before the charges can separate.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support Okafor and colleagues' hypothesis?
problem.stimulus: In organic solar cells, absorbed light creates excitons—tightly bound pairs of electrons and holes—that must be split apart before any current can flow. Splitting happens at the interface between a donor material and an acceptor material, where the electron hops to the acceptor and briefly forms a "charge-transfer state" with the hole left behind. Materials chemist Lena Okafor and colleagues hypothesize that the main barrier to efficiency in many blends is not how many charge-transfer states form but whether those states break apart: when the energy offset between donor and acceptor is too small, they argue, charge-transfer states tend to recombine before the charges can separate.
problem.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Okafor and colleagues' hypothesis?
options: In blends with small donor-acceptor energy offsets, charge-transfer states appear about as often as in large-offset blends, but a much larger share of them recombine before yielding free charges.
In blends with small donor-acceptor energy offsets, charge-transfer states appear far less often than in large-offset blends, and the few that do appear rarely recombine before yielding free charges.
In blends with small donor-acceptor energy offsets, charge-transfer states appear about as often as in large-offset blends, and the devices absorb a wider range of wavelengths of light.
In blends with large donor-acceptor energy offsets, charge-transfer states appear about as often as in small-offset blends, but the devices lose more energy as heat during operation.
problem.explanation: 가설의 핵심은 두 가지다: 에너지 오프셋이 작아도 전하이동 상태의 생성 수는 문제가 아니며, 그 상태들이 분리되기 전에 재결합하는 것이 문제라는 것이다. A는 생성 빈도는 비슷하지만 재결합 비율이 크다는 두 조건을 모두 보여 주므로 직접 지지한다. B는 오히려 생성 수가 문제이고 재결합은 드물다고 하여 가설과 반대다. C는 생성 빈도 부분은 맞지만 광흡수 범위는 분리·재결합과 무관하다. D 역시 생성 빈도가 비슷하다는 점은 맞으나 열 손실은 가설이 다루는 재결합 메커니즘을 보여 주지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The hypothesis has two parts: the number of charge-transfer states that form isn't the main problem, and when the offset is small, those states recombine before the charges separate. A shows both parts: states form about equally often, but far more of them recombine in small-offset blends, so it directly supports the hypothesis. B points the other way, since it makes formation the problem and says recombination is rare. C gets the formation part right, but light absorption range has nothing to do with whether the states break apart or recombine. D also matches on formation, but heat loss in large-offset devices doesn't show the recombination mechanism the hypothesis describes.

advisory.note: 정답 A는 가설의 두 요소(생성 수는 비슷함, 작은 오프셋에서 재결합이 많음)를 모두 충족한다. B는 반대 방향이고, C와 D는 생성 요소만 맞을 뿐 재결합과 무관하다. 오답 중 두 개가 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 갖고 있어 medium 난이도에 맞는다. 다만 A만 'recombine'이라는 핵심어를 담고 있어 훑어 읽어도 맞힐 여지가 조금 있다.

problem.passage:
Below about 2.17 kelvin, liquid helium-4 enters a superfluid state in which part of the liquid appears to flow with no viscosity at all. Physicists describe this with a "two-fluid" model: the liquid behaves as if it were a mixture of a normal component, which has viscosity and carries heat, and a superfluid component, which has zero viscosity and carries no entropy. Physicist Lena Ortiz argues that the model explains a puzzling observation. When superfluid helium is forced through a capillary only a few micrometers wide, it flows almost as if the channel were not there. Ortiz's explanation is that only the superfluid component passes through such narrow channels, while the viscous normal component is effectively held back.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support Ortiz's explanation?
problem.stimulus: Below about 2.17 kelvin, liquid helium-4 enters a superfluid state in which part of the liquid appears to flow with no viscosity at all. Physicists describe this with a "two-fluid" model: the liquid behaves as if it were a mixture of a normal component, which has viscosity and carries heat, and a superfluid component, which has zero viscosity and carries no entropy. Physicist Lena Ortiz argues that the model explains a puzzling observation. When superfluid helium is forced through a capillary only a few micrometers wide, it flows almost as if the channel were not there. Ortiz's explanation is that only the superfluid component passes through such narrow channels, while the viscous normal component is effectively held back.
problem.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Ortiz's explanation?
options: Helium that has flowed through a narrow capillary moves faster at 1.5 kelvin than at 2.0 kelvin, a temperature at which the normal component makes up a larger share of the liquid.
Helium collected right after it flows through a narrow capillary is colder than the helium left behind, as would happen if the liquid that gets through carries no heat.
When superfluid helium is poured into a wide beaker, it measurably resists stirring, as would be expected if the normal component were present.
Above 2.17 kelvin, liquid helium passes through the same narrow capillaries only very slowly, as would be expected from an ordinary viscous fluid.
problem.explanation: Ortiz의 주장은 좁은 모세관을 통과하는 것이 오직 초유체 성분뿐이라는 것이다. 초유체 성분은 엔트로피(열)를 운반하지 않으므로, 통과한 헬륨이 더 차갑다는 B의 발견은 통과한 것이 초유체 성분만이라는 점을 직접 보여 준다. A는 초유체 비율과 흐름 속도의 관계를 보여 줄 뿐, 정상 성분이 막히는지는 직접 확인하지 못한다. C는 정상 성분이 존재한다는 것만 보여 주고, 모세관 안에서 무슨 일이 일어나는지는 다루지 않는다. D는 초유체 전이 전후의 차이만 보여 주므로, 성분이 걸러진다는 주장 자체는 검증하지 못한다.
problem.explanationEn: Ortiz claims that only the superfluid component gets through narrow capillaries. The superfluid component carries no entropy (no heat), so if the helium that comes out is colder, as B says, that directly shows that the liquid getting through is the superfluid component alone. A only links the superfluid fraction to flow speed. It doesn't confirm that the normal component is actually held back. C shows that the normal component exists, but it says nothing about what happens inside the capillary. D only compares helium above and below the transition, so it doesn't test the claim that the two components are separated.

'엔트로피 없음→차가움' 연결과 A와의 비교가 필요하므로 medium에 적합.

advisory.note: B는 실제로 관측되는 기계열 효과(mechanocaloric effect)와 맞는다. 모세관을 빠져나온 액체는 차가워지고 남은 액체는 따뜻해지므로 물리적으로 정확하다. A는 부분적인 근거를 가진 강한 오답이지만 간접적인 증거에 그친다. C와 D도 그럴듯하지만 '걸러짐' 자체를 검증하지는 못한다. 따라서 medium 난이도에 적합하다.

problem.passage:
A single glass lens bends blue light more strongly than red light, so the colors in an image come to a focus at slightly different distances and objects appear edged with colored fringes. In the 1700s, opticians found that pairing a converging lens of crown glass with a weaker diverging lens of flint glass could largely cancel this effect. Optical engineer Mariela Ostrowski argues that the pairing works not because flint glass bends light more strongly overall, but because flint glass spreads colors apart (its dispersion) much more than crown glass does relative to how much it bends light. On this view, the weak flint lens can undo the crown lens's color spread while removing only part of its focusing power, so the pair still brings light to a focus.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support Ostrowski's argument?
problem.stimulus: A single glass lens bends blue light more strongly than red light, so the colors in an image come to a focus at slightly different distances and objects appear edged with colored fringes. In the 1700s, opticians found that pairing a converging lens of crown glass with a weaker diverging lens of flint glass could largely cancel this effect. Optical engineer Mariela Ostrowski argues that the pairing works not because flint glass bends light more strongly overall, but because flint glass spreads colors apart (its dispersion) much more than crown glass does relative to how much it bends light. On this view, the weak flint lens can undo the crown lens's color spread while removing only part of its focusing power, so the pair still brings light to a focus.
problem.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Ostrowski's argument?
options: Doublets made from a crown glass and a flint glass with much higher overall bending power produced less color fringing than single crown lenses did, regardless of the dispersion of the flint glass used.
Pairing a crown lens with a flint lens reduced color fringing in a doublet, but the doublet focused light less strongly than the crown lens used alone.

Pairing a crown lens with a flint lens that bent light as strongly as the crown but spread colors only slightly more failed to correct fringing, whereas a flint whose bending power was similar but whose dispersion was far greater corrected it.
Pairing a crown lens with a second crown lens of the same glass reduced color fringing only when the second lens was shaped to cancel nearly all of the first lens's focusing power.
problem.explanation: 오스트로프스키의 주장은 교정의 핵심이 전체 굴절력이 아니라 굴절력 대비 분산 비율이라는 것이다. C는 굴절력을 비슷하게 맞춘 채 분산만 바꿨을 때 분산이 큰 플린트만 교정에 성공했음을 보여 주므로 이 주장을 직접 지지한다. A는 분산과 관계없이 굴절력이 높은 플린트만으로 효과가 났다는 결과라서 오히려 주장을 약화시킨다. B는 이중렌즈의 초점력이 줄어든다는 사실만 보여 줄 뿐, 그 원인이 분산인지 굴절력인지 가려 주지 못한다. D는 같은 유리로는 초점력을 거의 다 없애야만 교정된다는 결과로 주장과 어울리긴 하지만, 플린트 유리의 분산이 원인이라는 점을 직접 검증하지는 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: Ostrowski's claim is that what makes the correction work is flint glass's dispersion relative to its bending power, not its overall bending power. C keeps bending power about the same and changes only dispersion, and only the high-dispersion flint corrects the fringing, so it isolates exactly the factor she names. A says higher bending power reduced fringing no matter what the dispersion was, which actually points against her view. B only shows that the doublet focuses light less strongly, and it doesn't tell you whether dispersion or bending power is responsible. D fits her reasoning in a general way, but it involves only crown glass, so it never tests whether flint's dispersion is the cause.
