problem.passage:
Ceramic capacitors made from barium titanate store unusually large amounts of charge because the material's dielectric constant is very high. That constant is not fixed, though: near about 120°C, barium titanate's crystal structure shifts, and the dielectric constant rises sharply and then falls, so capacitance can drift a great deal as a circuit heats up. Materials engineer Lena Varga has proposed that adding small amounts of zirconium to barium titanate makes capacitance more stable mainly because the zirconium spreads that structural shift across a wide range of temperatures instead of letting it happen at one sharp point. On this view, zirconium doesn't make the material a better dielectric overall; it just turns one sharp peak into a broad, gentle plateau.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support Varga's hypothesis?
problem.stimulus: Ceramic capacitors made from barium titanate store unusually large amounts of charge because the material's dielectric constant is very high. That constant is not fixed, though: near about 120°C, barium titanate's crystal structure shifts, and the dielectric constant rises sharply and then falls, so capacitance can drift a great deal as a circuit heats up. Materials engineer Lena Varga has proposed that adding small amounts of zirconium to barium titanate makes capacitance more stable mainly because the zirconium spreads that structural shift across a wide range of temperatures instead of letting it happen at one sharp point. On this view, zirconium doesn't make the material a better dielectric overall; it just turns one sharp peak into a broad, gentle plateau.
problem.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Varga's hypothesis?
options: Zirconium-doped barium titanate capacitors had a higher average dielectric constant from 20°C to 150°C than undoped capacitors, and their structural shift still happened in a narrow band near 120°C.
Zirconium-doped barium titanate capacitors kept their capacitance more steady than undoped capacitors when the frequency of the applied signal went from 1 kHz to 1 MHz at a constant room temperature.
Undoped barium titanate capacitors lost much of their capacitance after repeated heating and cooling, while zirconium-doped capacitors lost very little capacitance after the same treatment.

Zirconium-doped barium titanate capacitors had a lower peak dielectric constant than undoped capacitors, and X-ray measurements showed their structural shift happening gradually from about 60°C to 130°C.
problem.explanation: Varga의 가설에는 두 부분이 있다. 지르코늄이 구조 변화를 넓은 온도 범위로 퍼뜨린다는 점, 그리고 유전체 성능 자체를 높이는 것은 아니라는 점(날카로운 피크가 완만한 평탄부로 바뀜)이다. D는 피크가 낮아졌고 구조 변화가 60~130°C에 걸쳐 서서히 일어났음을 보여 주므로 두 부분을 모두 직접 뒷받침한다. A는 평균 유전율이 높아졌고 변화가 여전히 좁은 구간에서 일어났다고 하므로 오히려 가설을 약화한다. B는 온도가 아닌 주파수에 대한 안정성이고, C는 반복 가열에 따른 노화를 다루므로 둘 다 안정성은 보여 주지만 가설이 말하는 메커니즘은 검증하지 못한다.
problem.explanationEn: Varga's hypothesis has two parts: zirconium spreads the structural shift across a wide temperature range, and it doesn't make the material a better dielectric overall, so a sharp peak becomes a broad plateau. Choice D supports both parts directly: the peak is lower, and X-rays show the shift happening gradually from about 60°C to 130°C. Choice A actually weakens the hypothesis, because it reports a higher overall dielectric constant and a shift that stays in a narrow band. Choice B is about stability as frequency changes, not temperature. Choice C is about aging after repeated heating. Both B and C show some kind of stability, but neither tests the mechanism Varga proposes.

advisory.note: D는 메커니즘(점진적 구조 변화)과 '더 나은 유전체가 아님'(피크 저하)을 모두 충족한다. B와 C는 안정성이라는 부분 근거만 가진 오답이고, A는 주의를 끄는 반대 방향 오답이라 medium 난이도에 맞다. BaTiO3의 퀴리점이 약 120°C이고 Zr 도핑이 상전이를 확산시킨다는 내용은 실제 사실과 맞다.

problem.passage:
Potassium-argon (K-Ar) dating estimates the age of a volcanic rock by measuring how much argon-40 has built up from the radioactive decay of potassium-40 since the rock crystallized. The method assumes that molten lava releases essentially all of its argon gas, so that the "clock" starts at zero when the rock solidifies. Geochemist Lena Okafor has proposed that this assumption fails for some lavas that cool quickly underwater: in her view, the high water pressure keeps preexisting argon from escaping, so these rocks begin with "excess" argon and yield K-Ar ages that are older than their true crystallization ages.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support Okafor's hypothesis?
problem.stimulus: Potassium-argon (K-Ar) dating estimates the age of a volcanic rock by measuring how much argon-40 has built up from the radioactive decay of potassium-40 since the rock crystallized. The method assumes that molten lava releases essentially all of its argon gas, so that the "clock" starts at zero when the rock solidifies. Geochemist Lena Okafor has proposed that this assumption fails for some lavas that cool quickly underwater: in her view, the high water pressure keeps preexisting argon from escaping, so these rocks begin with "excess" argon and yield K-Ar ages that are older than their true crystallization ages.
problem.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Okafor's hypothesis?
options: Basalt that erupted underwater at great depth in a historically recorded eruption a few decades ago gives K-Ar ages of several hundred thousand years, while basalt from the same eruption that flowed onto land gives ages near zero.

Basalt that erupted on land in a historically recorded eruption a few decades ago gives K-Ar ages of several hundred thousand years, while basalt from the same eruption that flowed underwater gives ages near zero.
Basalt that erupted underwater at great depth contains more potassium-40 than basalt that erupted on land, which causes argon-40 to build up faster in the underwater samples after they solidify.
Basalt that erupted underwater at great depth gives K-Ar ages that closely match the ages given by a separate dating method that does not depend on argon.
problem.explanation: Okafor의 가설은 깊은 수중에서 빨리 식은 용암이 기존 아르곤을 잡아 두어 실제보다 오래된 연대가 나온다는 것이다. A는 나이를 알고 있는 최근 분출에서 수중 시료만 지나치게 오래된 연대를 보이고 육상 시료는 정상적이라는 내용이므로, 수중 조건이 오류의 원인임을 직접 보여 준다. B는 같은 틀이지만 수중과 육상이 뒤바뀌어 있어 가설과 반대 방향이다. C는 오래된 연대의 원인을 칼륨 양이 많아 고화 후 아르곤이 더 빨리 쌓이는 것으로 설명하므로, 처음부터 있던 과잉 아르곤 메커니즘과 다르다. D는 수중 시료의 연대가 정확하다는 것을 보여 주므로 오히려 가설을 약화한다.
problem.explanationEn: Okafor claims that lava cooling quickly deep underwater traps preexisting argon, so its K-Ar ages come out too old. A fits this: in an eruption of known recent age, only the underwater samples give far-too-old ages, while the land samples are correct, which points to the underwater setting as the cause. B uses the same setup but flips land and underwater, so it points the opposite way. C explains older ages by extra potassium making argon build up faster after the rock solidifies, which is a different mechanism from argon trapped at the start. D shows the underwater ages are accurate, so it weakens the hypothesis instead of supporting it.

Bricks with a high alumina content are often preferred because they keep their shape and strength even above 1,500°C, while bricks with less alumina tend to soften and crack. For this reason, high-alumina refractory bricks are considered especially ______ for lining furnaces that run at extreme temperatures.

problem.explanation: 지문은 알루미나 함량이 높은 벽돌이 1,500°C 이상에서도 형태와 강도를 유지해서 선호된다고 말하므로, 빈칸에는 이 벽돌이 고온 노에 '적합하다'는 뜻의 단어가 들어가야 한다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A는 '깨지기 쉬운'이라는 뜻으로, 강도를 유지한다는 설명과 정반대다. C는 '장식적인'이라는 뜻인데, 지문은 외관이 아니라 내열 성능을 다룬다. D는 '일시적인'이라는 뜻으로, 오랜 기간 견딘다는 내용과 맞지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The text says high-alumina bricks are preferred because they keep their shape and strength above 1,500°C, so the blank needs a word meaning they are a good fit for very hot furnaces. That makes B the correct answer. A means "easily broken," which is the opposite of keeping strength. C means "ornamental," but the text is about how well the bricks handle heat, not how they look. D means "short-lived," which contradicts the idea that the bricks survive heat for long periods.

problem.passage:
Text 1
Perovskite solar cells built from mixed halide crystals let engineers tune the bandgap simply by swapping iodide for bromide. Because laboratory measurements show that a cell's bandgap shifts smoothly and predictably as the bromide fraction rises, and because that bandgap stays fixed once the film is made, researchers can choose a single mixed composition matched to the upper layer of a tandem cell. Such compositions, the author concludes, offer a straightforward route toward record photovoltaic efficiency.

Text 2
When materials scientist Lena Okafor shone continuous light on mixed iodide-bromide perovskite films, she found that within minutes the halide ions migrated and separated into iodide-rich and bromide-rich pockets. The iodide-rich regions, which have a narrower bandgap, trapped charge carriers, so the voltage the film produced fell well below what its initial measured bandgap predicted. The effect largely reversed when the films were kept in the dark.

Based on the texts, which part of Text 1's reasoning would the author of Text 2 most likely challenge?

C is something Text 2 actually accepts: it relies on the idea that the initially measured bandgap depends on composition.

hardJudge.note: Text 1은 "Because… and because… the author concludes" 구조로 결론과 두 근거를 명확히 구분한다. Text 2의 광유도 할라이드 분리(실제 Hoke 효과와 부합, 암소에서 가역적) 관찰은 '제작 후 밴드갭 고정' 가정(D)만을 직접 겨냥하며, 조성에 따른 초기 밴드갭 변화(C)는 Text 2가 전제로 삼으므로 동의 부분 오답으로 적절. A는 결론 자체라 간접적으로만 약화되어 매력적 오답으로 기능하며, 수험생이 '직접 공격 대상'과 '결과적으로 약화되는 결론'의 강도 차이를 가려야 한다. B는 Text 2가 다루지 않는 세부. 해설은 정답과 오답 모두를 모순 없이 뒷받침한다. 사실 오류·저작권 문제 없음.

advisory.note: Text 2의 할라이드 분리 관찰은 Text 1의 'bandgap stays fixed once the film is made'를 거의 그대로 반박하는 사례다. 그래서 정답 D가 표면적으로 바로 대응되고, 입장을 추론하는 데 깊은 사고가 필요하지 않다. 결론(A)과 가정(D)을 구분하는 것은 전형적인 medium 수준의 함정이다. 선택지 강도의 미묘한 차이나 양쪽 입장을 종합하는 과정도 실질적으로 요구되지 않는다. 따라서 hard 특성을 충족하지 못한다.

problem.passage:
Text 1
Researchers studying electrospinning, in which a high voltage draws a charged polymer solution into a thin jet that whips chaotically before depositing as nanofibers, often propose rules for controlling fiber diameter. In my view, such a rule earns trust only if it holds when the same voltage and viscosity settings are tried on different equipment and in different labs. A rule that works only on one apparatus describes that apparatus, not the process.

Text 2
Materials engineer Priya Okonjo tuned a single custom electrospinning rig over eighteen months, adjusting voltage and solution viscosity in hundreds of trials. On that rig, raising viscosity while keeping voltage moderate reliably damped the jet's whipping instability and produced fibers within a narrow diameter band. Okonjo concludes that this combination is the general key to diameter control in electrospinning, and she points to the large number and consistency of her trials as proof.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 1 most likely evaluate Okonjo's conclusion described in Text 2?
problem.stimulus:
Text 1
Researchers studying electrospinning, in which a high voltage draws a charged polymer solution into a thin jet that whips chaotically before depositing as nanofibers, often propose rules for controlling fiber diameter. In my view, such a rule earns trust only if it holds when the same voltage and viscosity settings are tried on different equipment and in different labs. A rule that works only on one apparatus describes that apparatus, not the process.

Text 2
Materials engineer Priya Okonjo tuned a single custom electrospinning rig over eighteen months, adjusting voltage and solution viscosity in hundreds of trials. On that rig, raising viscosity while keeping voltage moderate reliably damped the jet's whipping instability and produced fibers within a narrow diameter band. Okonjo concludes that this combination is the general key to diameter control in electrospinning, and she points to the large number and consistency of her trials as proof.
problem.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 1 most likely evaluate Okonjo's conclusion described in Text 2?
options: As premature, because results gathered on one rig, however numerous, do not show that the viscosity-voltage combination would work on other setups
As well supported, because hundreds of consistent trials over eighteen months make the viscosity-voltage combination dependable
As partly supported, because the consistency of the trials confirms the rule for most setups even though a few other labs might find exceptions
As questionable, because adjusting both voltage and viscosity together makes it impossible to tell which factor reduced the whipping instability
problem.explanation:
정답 A: Text 1 저자의 기준은 다른 장비·다른 실험실에서도 재현되는지이다. Okonjo의 결과는 아무리 많고 일관돼도 장비 하나에서 나온 것이라 그 기준을 충족하지 못한다. 그래서 '일반적인 열쇠'라는 결론은 성급하다.
B: Text 2 저자 자신의 기준(시행 횟수와 일관성)으로 평가한 것이다. Text 1 저자는 장비 하나에서만 반복한 것은 그 장비를 설명할 뿐이라고 본다.
C: 두 기준을 섞은 평가이다. 장비 하나에서의 일관성이 '대부분의 장비'에서도 통한다고 인정하는데, Text 1 저자는 그런 추론 자체를 받아들이지 않는다.
D: 변수 교란이라는 일반적인 실험 상식에 따른 비판이다. Text 1이 내세운 기준은 아니다. 게다가 Text 2는 두 변수를 함께 쓰는 조합을 결론으로 내세우므로, 어느 변수 하나 때문인지 가려낼 필요가 없다.
problem.explanationEn:
A is correct. The author of Text 1 trusts a diameter-control rule only if it holds across different equipment and labs. Okonjo's evidence comes from one rig, no matter how many trials she ran. So her claim that the combination is the "general key" is premature by that standard.
B judges the conclusion by Okonjo's own standard (many consistent trials). Text 1 says results from one apparatus describe only that apparatus.
C blends the two standards. It treats one rig's consistency as proof for "most setups," which is exactly the inference Text 1 rejects.
D uses a general rule about confounded variables that Text 1 never brings up. Also, Okonjo's conclusion is about the combination itself, so she doesn't need to separate the two factors.

hardJudge.note: Text 1 기준(다른 장비·다른 실험실 재현성)이 명시되어 있고, Text 2의 결론은 단일 리그 결과를 일반화한 것이므로 그 기준으로 '성급함' 판정이 가능. A는 Text 1 기준에서만 도출되며 "however numerous"로 Text 2의 근거를 직접 기각함. B는 Text 2 저자의 기준(횟수·일관성), C는 두 관점을 섞어 '대부분의 장비'로 부분 인정, D는 본문에 없는 교란변수 비판. 전기방사 관련 서술(고전압, 휘핑 불안정, 점도-직경 관계)은 사실과 부합. 오답 C의 강도 차이 구분이 요구되어 hard 적합.

advisory.note: Text 1의 기준은 여러 장비·여러 실험실에서 재현되는지이고, 그 기준에 따라 단일 장비 결론을 성급하다고 본 A가 정답이다. B는 Okonjo 자신의 기준이고 C는 두 관점을 섞은 강도 함정, D는 그럴듯하지만 기준 밖의 비판이다. 다만 Text 1이 기준을 거의 그대로 밝히고 있어 추론 부담은 중상 수준이다.

problem.passage:
Nitinol, an alloy of nickel and titanium, has an unusual ability often called "shape memory." At room temperature, the metal's atoms are arranged in a flexible structure known as martensite, so a nitinol wire can be bent into a new shape fairly easily. When the wire is heated, its atoms shift into a different, more rigid arrangement called austenite, and the wire returns to the shape it was originally set in. __For example, some heart stents are made of nitinol: doctors compress the tiny tube to slip it into a blood vessel, and the warmth of the body causes it to expand back to its original open form.__ Because of this property, engineers see nitinol as useful wherever a part must change shape on its own in response to heat.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
problem.stimulus: Nitinol, an alloy of nickel and titanium, has an unusual ability often called "shape memory." At room temperature, the metal's atoms are arranged in a flexible structure known as martensite, so a nitinol wire can be bent into a new shape fairly easily. When the wire is heated, its atoms shift into a different, more rigid arrangement called austenite, and the wire returns to the shape it was originally set in. __For example, some heart stents are made of nitinol: doctors compress the tiny tube to slip it into a blood vessel, and the warmth of the body causes it to expand back to its original open form.__ Because of this property, engineers see nitinol as useful wherever a part must change shape on its own in response to heat.
problem.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It explains why nitinol's atoms rearrange into martensite at room temperature.
It presents a practical case of the heat-triggered shape recovery described earlier.
It describes a drawback that limits the use of nitinol in medicine.
It introduces an alloy that behaves differently from nitinol when heated.
problem.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 "For example"로 시작하며, 앞에서 설명한 '가열하면 원래 모양으로 돌아가는' 성질을 심장 스텐트라는 실제 사례로 보여 준다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A는 마르텐사이트가 생기는 원인을 다루지만 밑줄 문장은 그 원인을 설명하지 않는다. C는 단점을 말하지만 스텐트 사례는 오히려 장점을 보여 준다. D는 다른 합금을 말하지만 스텐트도 니티놀로 만든 것이다.
problem.explanationEn: The underlined sentence begins with "For example" and uses heart stents to show, in a real setting, the property described just before it: nitinol returning to its original shape when heated. That makes B correct. A is wrong because the sentence never explains why martensite forms at room temperature. C is wrong because the stent example shows a benefit of nitinol, not a drawback. D is wrong because the stent is made of nitinol itself, not of a different alloy.

hardJudge.note: 밑줄 문장은 "For example"로 시작해 앞의 가열 시 형상 회복 성질을 심장 스텐트 사례로 구체화하므로 B가 유일하게 맞다. A(원인 설명), C(단점), D(다른 합금)는 지문 내용과 명백히 불일치하지만 '구조·기능' 문항의 전형적 오답 유형이라 그럴듯함. 니티놀 스텐트·마르텐사이트/오스테나이트 설명은 사실에 부합. 해설 한·영 일치, 영어 자연스러움, 한글 혼입 없음. 명시적 담화표지 하나로 풀리는 easy 난이도 적합.

advisory.note: "For example"라는 명시적 단서 하나로 풀리는 문항이라 easy 난이도에 맞다. 오답은 모두 지문 속 요소(마르텐사이트, 의료 용도, 가열)를 활용해 그럴듯하게 만들어졌다. 니티놀 스텐트가 체온에서 다시 펴진다는 설명은 초탄성/형상기억 스텐트에 대한 일반적 설명으로 볼 수 있어 허용 범위다.

problem.passage:
Liquid crystals are materials whose rod-shaped molecules can flow like a liquid but still line up in a shared direction, like a crystal. In a display pixel, a thin layer of these molecules sits between two filters that block light unless its vibration direction is turned. When no voltage is applied, the molecules are arranged in a gentle twist that turns the light so it can pass through the second filter. __When a small electric field is switched on, however, the molecules rotate to point along the field, and the light is no longer turned, so the pixel goes dark.__ By adjusting the voltage on millions of pixels, a screen can control exactly how much light each one lets through.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
problem.stimulus: Liquid crystals are materials whose rod-shaped molecules can flow like a liquid but still line up in a shared direction, like a crystal. In a display pixel, a thin layer of these molecules sits between two filters that block light unless its vibration direction is turned. When no voltage is applied, the molecules are arranged in a gentle twist that turns the light so it can pass through the second filter. __When a small electric field is switched on, however, the molecules rotate to point along the field, and the light is no longer turned, so the pixel goes dark.__ By adjusting the voltage on millions of pixels, a screen can control exactly how much light each one lets through.
problem.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It defines liquid crystals by comparing them with ordinary liquids and solid crystals.
It explains why the filters in a pixel block light that has not been turned.
It describes what changes in a pixel when voltage is applied, in contrast to the condition just described.
It argues that the twisted arrangement of molecules is a flaw in display design.
problem.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 'however'로 시작하여, 앞 문장의 '전압이 없을 때' 상태와 대비되는 '전기장을 켰을 때' 분자가 회전하고 픽셀이 어두워지는 변화를 서술하므로 C가 정답이다. A는 액정의 정의로, 첫 문장의 역할이다. B는 필터가 빛을 막는 원리를 설명한다고 하지만, 그것은 둘째 문장에서 이미 제시되었고 밑줄 문장은 필터의 작동 원리를 설명하지 않는다. D는 꼬인 배열이 결함이라는 주장인데, 지문은 그러한 평가를 전혀 하지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The underlined sentence begins with "however" and shows what happens when an electric field is switched on: the molecules rotate and the pixel goes dark. This contrasts with the no-voltage state described in the sentence just before it, so C is correct. A describes the job of the first sentence, which defines liquid crystals. B is wrong because the filters' role is stated in the second sentence, and the underlined sentence doesn't explain how they work. D is wrong because the text never criticizes the twisted arrangement as a flaw.

hardJudge.note: 밑줄 문장은 'however'로 앞 문장(전압 없음→빛 통과)과 대비하여 전기장 적용 시 변화(분자 회전→픽셀 어두워짐)를 서술하므로 C가 정답. A는 1문장, B는 2문장의 기능이며 D는 지문에 없는 평가. 한·영 해설 결론 및 글자 참조 일치, 영어 자연스러움. TN-LCD 작동 원리 설명도 과학적으로 정확. 명시적 대비 신호어 하나로 풀리는 1단계 추론이라 easy에 적합.

advisory.note: 'however'라는 명시적 단서 하나로 풀 수 있다. 오답 A와 B는 지문의 다른 문장이 하는 역할을 그대로 가져온 전형적인 함정이고, D는 지문에 없는 평가를 덧붙인 선택지다. 액정 디스플레이(TN 방식, 전압을 걸면 어두워지는 normally white 구조)에 대한 서술도 사실과 맞다.

problem.passage:
When two metals such as copper and zinc are pressed together and heated, atoms from each side migrate across the boundary. In a classic 1947 experiment, Ernest Kirkendall showed that this exchange is not even: zinc atoms diffuse into copper faster than copper atoms move the other way. Because more atoms leave the zinc-rich side than arrive to replace them, vacant lattice sites pile up there and eventually merge into tiny pores. Engineers who join dissimilar metals therefore regard the mismatch in migration rates not as a curiosity but as a ______ weakness, since the resulting voids can make a joint brittle long before any visible crack appears.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.stimulus: When two metals such as copper and zinc are pressed together and heated, atoms from each side migrate across the boundary. In a classic 1947 experiment, Ernest Kirkendall showed that this exchange is not even: zinc atoms diffuse into copper faster than copper atoms move the other way. Because more atoms leave the zinc-rich side than arrive to replace them, vacant lattice sites pile up there and eventually merge into tiny pores. Engineers who join dissimilar metals therefore regard the mismatch in migration rates not as a curiosity but as a ______ weakness, since the resulting voids can make a joint brittle long before any visible crack appears.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: temporary
superficial
deliberate
latent
problem.explanation: 지문은 원자 이동 속도 차이로 생긴 공극이 눈에 보이는 균열이 나타나기 훨씬 전부터 접합부를 취약하게 만든다고 설명하므로, 빈칸에는 '겉으로 드러나지 않고 잠재해 있는'이라는 뜻의 D(latent)가 들어가야 한다. A(temporary)는 공극이 점점 쌓여 합쳐진다는 진행 과정과 맞지 않는데, 이 결함은 사라지지 않고 오히려 커진다. B(superficial)는 '보이지 않는'이라는 단서를 '사소한'으로 잘못 읽은 오답으로, 접합부를 부서지기 쉽게 만드는 결함은 사소하지 않으며 공극은 표면이 아니라 내부에 생긴다. C(deliberate)는 공학자가 결함을 다룬다는 맥락에서 그럴듯해 보이지만, 공극은 의도해서 만든 것이 아니라 자연스럽게 생기는 결과이다.
problem.explanationEn: The text says the voids from unequal migration rates can weaken a joint "long before any visible crack appears," so the blank needs a word meaning present but hidden. That makes D (latent) the answer. A (temporary) doesn't fit, because the vacancies keep piling up and merging into pores, so the weakness grows over time rather than going away. B (superficial) might tempt you if you read "not visible" as "minor," but a flaw that makes a joint brittle isn't minor, and the voids form inside the metal, not on its surface. C (deliberate) can sound reasonable since engineers are mentioned, but nobody creates the voids on purpose; they come from the diffusion process itself.

hardJudge.note: 정답 D(latent) 검증: "not as a curiosity but as a ___ weakness" + "long before any visible crack appears"라는 두 단서를 연결해야 하며, 숨어 있다가 나중에 드러나는 결함이라는 의미로 latent가 유일하게 적합. A(temporary)는 공극이 누적·합쳐진다는 서술과 모순, B(superficial)는 '보이지 않음'을 '표면적/사소함'으로 오독할 때 유인되는 오답, C(deliberate)는 공학자 언급에서 오는 표면적 그럴듯함. 사실관계(Kirkendall 1947, 아연이 구리보다 빠르게 확산, 공극 형성)도 정확. 한·영 해설 모두 선택지 글자 참조 일치, 영어 해설 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 두 단서 결합이 필요하고 B·C가 부분적 근거를 가지므로 medium 적합.

advisory.note: 커켄달 효과 설명은 사실에 부합한다(1947년, Zn이 Cu보다 빠르게 확산, 공공 응집으로 기공 형성). 정답의 핵심 단서는 'long before any visible crack appears'이다. 오답 중 B와 A는 부분적으로 그럴듯해 비교가 필요하다. C는 다소 쉽게 배제되지만 중간 난이도 범위 안이다.

problem.passage:
When a hot ceramic plate is plunged into cold water, its surface cools and contracts faster than its interior. This uneven shrinking creates tension at the surface, and the cracks that form during such thermal shock ______ often traced by engineers to tiny flaws already present in the material.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: When a hot ceramic plate is plunged into cold water, its surface cools and contracts faster than its interior. This uneven shrinking creates tension at the surface, and the cracks that form during such thermal shock ______ often traced by engineers to tiny flaws already present in the material.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: is
are
was
has been
problem.explanation: 빈칸의 주어는 복수 명사 "the cracks"이며, "that form during such thermal shock"는 주어를 꾸미는 수식어일 뿐이다. 따라서 복수 동사가 필요하고, 지문의 현재 시제와도 맞는 B "are"가 정답이다. A "is"와 D "has been"은 단수 동사라서 복수 주어 "cracks"와 수가 일치하지 않는다. C "was"도 단수 동사이며, 지문의 현재 시제(cools, creates)와도 맞지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The subject of the blank is the plural noun "the cracks." The phrase "that form during such thermal shock" only describes the cracks. So you need a plural verb that also matches the passage's present tense, and B ("are") does both. A ("is") and D ("has been") are singular verbs, so they don't agree with the plural subject "cracks." C ("was") is also singular, and it breaks the present tense used throughout the passage (cools, creates).

problem.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "these bonds resist being pulled apart extremely well"과 빈칸 뒤 "engineers add the tubes..."는 각각 독립절이다. D는 마침표로 두 절을 나누고 "As a result,"로 다음 문장을 시작하므로 올바르다. problem.explanationEn: Look at both sides of the blank: "these bonds resist being pulled apart extremely well" and "engineers add the tubes..." are both independent clauses. D is correct because it ends the first sentence with a period and starts a new one with "As a result," so the clauses are properly separated. A joins two independent clauses with only a comma, which is a comma splice. B puts the clauses together with no punctuation at all, which makes a run-on sentence. C adds an unnecessary comma after "and," and since the sentence already has a clause joined by "and," the structure becomes awkward.

depended

C ("were depending") is a finite verb, but it's plural. It wrongly agrees with nearby plural nouns like "generations" or "limits" instead of the real subject, "survival."
